works.title: Impacts of Biological Filtration on Disinfection Byproduct Control during Drinking Water Purification: A Critical Review
works.abstract: Abstract Biofiltration, particularly biological activated carbon and sand filtration, is widely implemented as a low-chemical, energy-efficient barrier to attenuate disinfection byproduct (DBP) precursors. However, biofilters are living, time-evolving ecosystems that can transition from a net “sink” to a net “source” of reactive precursors. This review synthesized evidence that biofiltration exhibits selective removal: hydrophobic and high-molecular-weight C-DBP precursors are preferentially removed, whereas hydrophilic N-DBP (e.g., HANs, NDMA) precursors readily break through and may be newly produced. The authors clarified the mechanistic basis of precursor generation, highlighting (i) biofilm turnover that releases intracellular organic matter enriched in amines and nucleic acids, (ii) continuous production and sloughing of soluble microbial products and extracellular polymeric substances that elevate protein-like DON, and (iii) media aging and stratification that diminish removal efficacy. Regression analysis estimated sink–source transition for N-DBP precursor removal at approximately log10(bed volumes) = 5.38 (∼240,000 bed volumes), a practical reference in drinking water treatment plants. Furthermore, the authors identified critical operational tipping points, including oxidant pre-exposure, temperature fluctuations, and nutrient stoichiometry, that can trigger this functional inversion. Finally, a risk-oriented framework is proposed, advocating for precursor-specific monitoring (e.g., fluorescence signatures) and intelligent process control to stabilize biofilter performance against emerging genotoxic risks.

works.title: A Scenario-Based Probabilistic First-Tier Screening of Potential Chemical Risk to European Groundwater Ecosystems
works.abstract: Abstract Groundwater supplies much of the freshwater used by humans while supporting highly specialized biological communities characterized by high endemism and limited taxonomic, functional, and phylogenetic redundancy. Yet European Union groundwater legislation remains resource-oriented and addresses the ecological consequences of chemical contamination only indirectly. We conducted a continent-wide, first-tier screening of potential chemical risk to European groundwater ecosystems. Harmonized European surface water and groundwater monitoring data were combined with geostatistical interpolation and transport modeling to estimate contaminant concentrations at the groundwater table, while uncertainty in hydrogeological conditions, chemical fate, and preferential transport was propagated through Monte Carlo simulations. We compared a Surface Water Baseline scenario, based on model-derived groundwater concentrations and existing freshwater regulatory thresholds, with a Groundwater-Informed Conservative scenario integrating measured groundwater concentrations, groundwater-fauna toxicity data, and precautionary adjustments where groundwater-specific evidence was unavailable. Potential risk was summarized as the average frequency of exceedance (AFE) across contaminants and uncertainty realizations; its maps indicate the frequency and spatial distribution of threshold exceedances, not their magnitude or the severity of ecological damage. Mean AFE was low under the baseline scenario but increased 5-fold under the conservative scenario, revealing areas in the medium-to-very-high screening classes in the Pyrenean–Catalan sector, Sierra Nevada, and the eastern Balkan–Carpathian region. The framework provides a replicable basis for prioritizing monitoring, ecotoxicological testing, and management.

works.title: Turning Abandoned Mines into Carbon Sinks: Laboratory Demonstration of CO2 Hydrate Sequestration in Cold-Region Goafs under Permafrost Conditions
works.abstract: Abstract Carbon capture, utilization, and storage (CCUS) is a key technology for carbon neutrality, but conventional CO2 geological sequestration suffers from high injection pressure, limited stability, and restricted storage space. Hydrate-based CO2 sequestration offers high capacity, low cost, and intrinsic safety. This study proposes a novel in situ CO2 hydrate formation and sequestration method in coal mine goafs containing permafrost layers in cold regions. The natural low-temperature permafrost environment provides favorable conditions for hydrate formation, while goafs offer large storage space. To avoid hydrate plugging and improve engineering feasibility, a liquid-first CO2 constant-pressure supply and predissolution mode was adopted. We simulated goaf conditions at depths of 110–130 m and ∼1 MPa. Experiments tested three injection temperatures (293.15, 298.15, and 303.15 K) and five goaf temperatures (269.15–277.15 K) using tetrahydrofuran and tryptophan as promoters. Results proved efficient sequestration at a low pressure of 1 MPa. Under optimal conditions (injection temperature of 298.15 K, goaf temperature of 271.15 K), capacity reached 60.9 mmol of CO2/mol of water (mmol/mol) with an efficiency of 135.36 (kg·m–3)/MPa. The 26.7 h stability experiments under depressurization showed 4.21–16.09 mmol/mol dissociated initially, but 66.38%–90.77% CO2 remained sequestered. Further, one-month tests under the pressure-release condition revealed hydrate dissociation almost stopped after day 1, yielding a 65.32% permanent sequestration ratio. Crucially, under the pressure-maintained condition, the system continued to form CO2 hydrates over the 30-day period, resulting in an additional 31.04% CO2 storage. These results validate the feasibility and long-term stability of this novel approach.

works.title: Spectroscopic Insights into Ion Pairing in Sulfate Electrolytes: Implications for Sorption in Aqueous Systems
works.abstract: Abstract Ion pairing, including contact, solvent-shared, and solvent-separated ion pairs (CIPs, SIPs, and SSIPs, respectively), affects aqueous reaction chemistry, sorption, and precipitation processes. Accurate characterization of ion pairing in aqueous sulfate electrolytes is essential for understanding their thermodynamics and hydration structure, yet comprehensive quantification across aqueous and mixed-solvent systems remains limited. We combine Raman spectroscopy with dielectric spectroscopy, using waveguide-based setups (WR-62 and WR-28, applied for the first time) and a broadband probe station (10 MHz–50 GHz), to characterize ion pairing and solvent–solute interactions in monovalent cation sulfate salts in water and water/methanol solutions. Dielectric spectroscopy resolved SSIP and SIP fractions, with SSIPs dominating Li2SO4 and Na2SO4. Raman spectroscopy quantified CIPs (K2SO4 > Na2SO4 ≈ Li2SO4), consistent with cation hydration and polarizability. Methanol increased SIP and CIP concentrations. Ion association stability constants and mean activity coefficients were calculated with Archer’s form of the Pitzer model, incorporating short-range binary and ternary ion–ion interactions. This approach predicts mean activity coefficients at elevated ionic strengths without double-counting ion-pairing contributions, enabling determination of stability constants and aqueous speciation. Resolving ion-pair speciation is important for accurate thermodynamic models of sulfate-bearing waters relevant to membrane separations and resource recovery.

works.title: Nanoconfinement Controls Hydrogen Transport in Shales
works.abstract: Abstract Underground hydrogen storage (UHS) in sedimentary formations requires understanding how hydrogen migrates, persists, and is released under nanoscale confinement in fine-grained rocks that may act as reservoirs or caprocks. Here, we combine in situ small-angle neutron scattering (SANS) with molecular dynamics simulations to examine how wetting state controls hydrogen reversibility and postcycling pore occupancy in shale nanopores. SANS-derived pore-size distributions reveal a clear hierarchy: dry shale exhibits near-complete reversibility, decane-saturated shale shows partial recovery, and water-saturated shale displays minimal recovery, with persistent postcycling occupancy concentrated in pores <2 nm. Molecular simulations support a mechanistic interpretation in which this hierarchy arises from coupled nanoscale effects, including cavity-formation penalties, confinement-induced stress anisotropy, and fluid-specific interfacial free-energy barriers at mineral and organic surfaces. Water-saturated nanopores are associated with strong thermodynamic and mechanical constraints consistent with reduced hydrogen reversibility, whereas these constraints are substantially weaker in dry pores and intermediate in decane-filled pores. Together, the experimental and molecular simulation results provide a framework linking nanoscale fluid–rock interactions to hydrogen hysteresis and retention, with implications for subsurface hydrogen recoverability and containment in underground storage systems.

works.title: Long-Term PM2.5 Exposure Promoted Vascular Calcification through XBP1s-Associated Osteogenic Switching and Inflammatory Crosstalk
works.abstract: Abstract Fine particulate matter (PM2.5) is a major environmental risk factor for cardiovascular disease, yet the mechanisms underlying long-term exposure-induced vascular calcification remain incompletely understood. Whether PM2.5 directly participates in mineral nucleation remains unclear. We found that PM2.5 accelerated the transformation of amorphous calcium phosphate (ACP) into crystalline hydroxyapatite (HAP) and may act as a heterogeneous nucleation interface under simulated physiological conditions. Mice were exposed to environmentally relevant PM2.5 concentrations (5 or 35 μg/m3) for 180 days using a whole-body inhalation system. Long-term PM2.5 exposure increased arterial stiffness and promoted vascular remodeling and calcification. Mechanistically, PM2.5 increased XBP1s expression in mouse aortic smooth muscle cells (MOVAS), promoting proliferative and osteogenic phenotypic switching. Genetic deletion of Xbp1 markedly attenuated PM2.5-induced MOVAS proliferation, migration, osteogenic transformation, and mineralization. In addition, PM2.5-stimulated MOVAS acquired a pro-inflammatory secretory phenotype that promoted macrophage recruitment and M1 polarization, whereas Xbp1 deficiency attenuated these effects. We also established a human iPSC-derived blood vessel organoid (BVO)-macrophage coculture system and found that macrophages substantially amplified PM2.5-induced osteogenic remodeling and calcification. Collectively, these findings revealed the involvement of both physicochemical mineralization and XBP1-associated osteogenic and inflammatory responses in PM2.5-induced vascular calcification, providing new insights into the mechanisms underlying PM2.5-associated vascular injury.

works.title: Aldehyde-philic Portal Engineering of γ-Cyclodextrin MOF for Synergistic Capture of Toluene and Formaldehyde in Humid Atmospheric Environments
works.abstract: Abstract Efficient removal of multicomponent volatile organic compounds (VOCs) from real environments remains challenging, particularly under humidity. This study introduces an “aldehyde-philic portal modification” strategy that precisely anchors dopamine (DA) at γ-cyclodextrin-based metal–organic framework (γ-CD-MOF) outer rim via H-bonding to construct oligomeric polydopamine (o-PDA) structures. This pore design partitions the cyclodextrin cavity into an aldehyde-philic outer rim and arene-philic interior for efficient synergistic capture of formaldehyde and toluene in humidity. Exposed pyrrolic N sites on o-PDA enable γ-CD-MOF@PDA2 to preferentially bind CH2O, which then act as new sites to enhance subsequent C7H8 capture via CH−π interactions while hindering H2O binding to peripheral hydroxyls and preventing large-sized water clusters from blocking cavity openings. Furthermore, the hydrophobic inner cavity exhibits strong π–π conjugation with C7H8, facilitating its diffusion and establishing an “outer capture–inner fixation” pathway, significantly enhancing toluene capacity. At ∼40% relative humidity, the toluene working capacity of γ-CD-MOF@PDA2 in the multicomponent system increased by 106% over the single-component system, while the formaldehyde capacity remained unchanged. Consequently, the total working capacity of toluene and formaldehyde reached twice the sum of their single-component adsorption capacities, demonstrating marked synergistic coadsorption. This work provides a feasible approach for controlling multicomponent VOCs in complex humid atmospheric environments.

works.title: Strategies for Eliminating Heavy Air Pollution in the Beijing–Tianjin–Hebei Region: Insights from Joint Practices during the 2022 Olympic and Paralympic Winter Games
works.abstract: Abstract The 2022 Olympic Winter Games (OWG) and Paralympic Winter Games (PWG) marked the first time the Beijing–Tianjin–Hebei (BTH) region implemented joint air pollution prevention and control measures for a winter mega-event. Notably, while Beijing maintained clean air (daily PM2.5 concentration ≤ 75 μg/m3, according to the Ambient Air Quality Standards in effect at the time) during the OWG, a heavy-pollution episode occurred during the PWG, with the 24-h average PM2.5 concentration peaking at 155 μg/m3. Combining field observations, dynamic emission characterization, and The Comprehensive Air quality Model with extensions (CAMx) simulations, we conducted a closed-loop study to investigate the underlying causes of this episode. Results show that while the industrial sector effectively regulated emissions, the mobile-source activity levels recovered rapidly after the Chinese New Year, outweighing the control measures implemented for mobile sources. This recovery increased total NOx emissions by 13% in the BTH region, driving nitrate-dominated PM2.5 pollution. During the study period, the PM2.5 nitrate concentration (normalized by the carbon monoxide concentration) was found to increase by 3 × 10–4 and 1 × 10–5 for each one-ton increase in NOx emissions in Beijing and the BTH region, respectively. To eliminate heavy PM2.5 pollution under the meteorological conditions observed during the PWG, NOx emissions would need to be further reduced by ≥1% in Beijing and ≥7% in the BTH region. This work underscores the urgent need to mitigate emissions from diesel trucks and nonroad machinery, especially under extremely adverse meteorological conditions in the BTH region.

works.title: TP-Agent: An Auditable LLM Agent for Predicting Pollutant Transformation Products in Oxidative Water Treatment
works.abstract: Abstract Predicting the transformation products (TPs) of organic micropollutants is important for characterizing their chemical fate during oxidative water treatment and prioritizing candidate structures for high-resolution mass spectrometry (HRMS) analysis. Limited labeled data and diverse reaction pathways make this task challenging. TP-Agent combines a large language model (LLM), training-only analog retrieval, and executable atom/bond edits to rank TP candidates with inspectable structural records. On 231 standardized-parent-disjoint reactions, TP-Agent achieved 78.8% strict Top-5 accuracy, compared with 65.8% for the bare LLM, 76.2% for standalone retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), and 56.3 ± 1.5% for TP-Transformer across three training seeds. Parent-clustered bootstrap analysis supported the gain over the bare LLM; the 2.6-percentage-point difference from RAG was not statistically significant. Retrieval supplied most of the accuracy gain, while graph execution added candidate-linked structural records. Among 1095 candidates, 92.7% had exact edit-replay or deterministic-projection records, measuring structural linkage rather than mechanistic validity. Where available, candidate-linked LLM rationales provide chemical hypotheses for inspection. Estimated parallel latency and API-equivalent cost were 3.5 and 7.4 times those of RAG, respectively. TP-Agent thus combines TP candidate ranking with traceable structural operations and inspectable chemical hypotheses for HRMS follow-up.

works.title: Global Analysis and Prediction of Bicarbonate in Groundwater under Climate Change
works.abstract: Abstract Bicarbonate (HCO3–) is a major contributor to the alkalinity of groundwater, and low concentrations can reduce buffering capacity and increase the potential susceptibility of water to corrosion-related quality deterioration, particularly in untreated groundwater systems with corrosion-prone infrastructure. Here, we use machine learning and a comprehensive data set of 28,902 groundwater samples from 80 countries to produce a global probability map of HCO3– concentrations below 80 mg/L and estimate the population residing within the Low-Alkalinity Corrosion Risk Potential Zone (LACRPZ). From 2000 to 2020, LACRPZ was mainly concentrated in Southeast Asia and South America, with approximately 704 million people residing within these zones, particularly in Oceania (52.92%) and South America (35.09%). Although the area of LACRPZ is projected to decline under future climate change, the resident population in LACRPZ is expected to increase. This study reveals the evolution of global groundwater bicarbonate concentrations and resident population, underscoring the importance of integrating bicarbonate into water safety management strategies.

works.title: Evaluating Pollution Prevention Effectiveness for Toxic Substances in Canada Using Advanced Difference-in-Differences Methods
works.abstract: Abstract This study evaluates the effectiveness of pollution prevention (P2) activities using facility-level data from Canada’s National Pollutant Release Inventory (NPRI) over 1993–2024. Leveraging recent advances in causal inference methodology that account for staggered treatment adoption and heterogeneous treatment effects, this Difference-in-Differences (DiD) analysis moves beyond conventional DiD to identify substantial heterogeneity in P2 impacts across time, sectors, regions, P2 activities, and substances. Key findings indicate analysis of staggered adoption matters, with cohort-specific release reductions ranging widely, and larger effects among earlier adoption cohorts (2001–2003 ∼0-76 vs 2021 ∼3%). P2 adoption is associated with an average 19% reduction in pollutant releases. In contrast, P2 activities are associated with a near-zero and statistically insignificant increase in waste. P2 is more effective for releases to water, and within specific sectors such as Mining and Quarrying and Conventional Oil and Gas extraction. Stronger effects are observed for activities related to Inventory Management/Purchasing, and in Ontario, Alberta, and Quebec, and for VOCs. Despite study limitations, the results suggest that P2 delivers net environmental benefits overall and highlight the importance of modern causal inference methods for evaluating P2 policies in settings with staggered treatment adoption, such as the NPRI.

works.title: Maternal 6PPD-Quinone Exposure is Associated with Infant Neurodevelopmental Delay: Epidemiological Evidence and Mechanistic Insights from a Birth Cohort Study
works.abstract: Abstract Tire-derived p-phenylenediamines (PPDs) and their quinone derivatives (PPD-Qs) have emerged as potential neurotoxicants, yet the associations of prenatal exposure with offspring neurodevelopment remain underexplored. Therefore, we conducted a nested case-control study within a prospective birth cohort (n = 1,317) and measured ten urinary PPDs/PPD-Qs at 6–16 weeks of gestation. In the primary adjusted model, higher urinary concentrations of 6PPD-quinone (6PPD-Q) and N,N′-di(o-tolyl)-p-phenylenediamine (DTPD) were associated with higher odds of neurodevelopmental delay. Quantile g-computation further indicated that a simultaneous one-quartile increase in all components of the PPDs/PPD-Qs mixture was associated with higher odds of neurodevelopmental delay (odds ratio = 1.33, 95% confidence interval: 1.03–1.72). Random forest analysis identified 6PPD-Q as having the highest variable importance among the measured PPDs/PPD-Qs. Network toxicology analysis implicated dopaminergic, serotonergic, and glutamatergic neurotransmission pathways as potentially relevant to 6PPD-Q-associated neurodevelopmental toxicity. In bEnd.3 mouse brain microvascular endothelial cells, 6PPD-Q exposure induced transcriptomic alterations involving xenobiotic metabolism, inflammatory signaling, and neurotransmission-related pathways. These changes were accompanied by decreased mRNA expression of the blood–brain barrier tight junction–related genes ZO-1 and occludin. Collectively, these epidemiological associations and complementary mechanistic findings support the biological plausibility of 6PPD-Q-associated developmental neurotoxicity and warrant further investigation and independent replication.

works.title: Quantitative Fish Biomonitoring by an Enhanced eDNA Metabarcoding Approach
works.abstract: Abstract Environmental DNA (eDNA)-based technologies have been increasingly employed in biodiversity surveys and ecological status assessments. However, most eDNA metabarcoding studies rely on relative read abundance, which limits their utility for quantitative environmental management and decision-making. To address this, we developed a quantitative calibration method incorporating dual internal standards: one added prior to DNA extraction and a three-concentration gradient added prior to PCR amplification, enabling independent correction of efficiencies for both steps. Results showed that within the tested aquatic matrices, DNA extraction efficiency had a greater impact on species quantification than PCR amplification efficiency. The dual internal standard calibration outperformed the single internal standard approach in both controlled laboratory experiments and field aquaculture ponds. The spiking of dual internal standards demonstrated excellent calibration across a wide range (2.4–54.1%), indicating that the method is broadly applicable and expandable without altering species detection. Field biomonitoring in the Yangtze River revealed that calibrated eDNA monitoring enhanced the spatial distribution patterns of an endangered species (Leiocassis longirostris) and a migratory species (Coilia nasus). Overall, calibrating DNA extraction and PCR amplification efficiency significantly improves the technical precision of eDNA quantification. While it strongly correlates with biomass under controlled conditions, in field applications, this dual calibration provides a robust analytical baseline that, when combined with ecological models, will be valuable for biodiversity conservation and ecological assessment. Pilot optimization of internal standard spiking volume is recommended for field surveys to balance sequencing cost and quantitative performance.

works.title: Unignorable Role of Iron Redox and Microbial Adaptation in Mediating Arsenic-Induced Suppression of Carbon Emissions in Paddy Soils
works.abstract: Abstract Arsenic (As) contamination disturbs organic carbon (OC) cycling in paddy soils, potentially influenced by microbial adaptive evolution and redox-active iron (Fe). Here, the association of As with C emissions (CH4 and CO2), microbes, and Fe dynamics in flooded paddy soils was investigated via microcosm experiments across two As levels (20 and 200 mg kg–1). Results showed that As contamination markedly inhibited CH4 (>90%) and CO2 (>38%) emissions, accompanied by inhibited ferric reduction, decreased OC bioavailability, and shifted microbial communities toward As-tolerant and oligotrophic strategies. Correlation analysis and validation experiments demonstrated that Fe reduction covaried negatively with available As but positively with C bioavailability indicators (p < 0.001). The suppressed C emissions under low-dose As were closely linked to perturbed Fe redox cycling, while high-dose As appeared to amplify this inhibition through additional microbial toxicity and community restructuring. Exogenous zerovalent iron increased CH4 emissions by 0.92–19.54-fold through coupled changes in As immobilization, redox conditions, C bioavailability, and abundance of Fe-reducing bacteria and methanogens. This work indicated that Fe redox and microbial adaptation are important contributors to As-mediated suppression of C emissions, providing evidence for the As–Fe–C nexus and offering insights for balancing As remediation with C emission mitigation.

works.title: Gradient-Charge Oxygen Vacancy Pairs Enable Synergistic Activation of O2 and H2O for Low-Temperature CH3CN Emission Control
works.abstract: Abstract Acetonitrile (CH3CN) emitted from industrial production severely threatens atmospheric quality due to its persistence and high toxicity. While selective catalytic oxidation (SCO) represents the most promising technology for CH3CN elimination, the inherent competition between O2-activated oxidation and H2O-activated hydrolysis pathways has long prevented the simultaneous achievement of excellent low-temperature activity and high N2 selectivity. Herein, we report a Cu-modified TiO2 catalyst and propose a Cu-induced gradient-charge oxygen vacancy pair structure (Ti–OVR–Cu–OVP–Ti) as the most plausible active site configuration that enables activation of O2 and H2O via electron filling of their antibonding orbitals to promote the reaction during CH3CN oxidation. The electron-rich OVR site can adsorb both O2 and H2O, donating electrons to populate the π* antibonding orbital of O2 and the σ* antibonding orbital of H2O. Meanwhile, the electron-poor OVP site adsorbs O2 or H2O and serves as a reservoir to sustain a continuous supply of active species. The optimized catalyst induced by Ti–OVR–Cu–OVP–Ti structure achieves complete CH3CN conversion at 220 °C with 96% N2 selectivity. This work highlights the critical role of electron configuration in tailoring oxygen vacancy functions, providing a general strategy for developing advanced environmental catalysts for practical CH3CN emission control.

works.title: Near-Real-Time Mapping of Seamless All-Hour Aerosol Optical Depth in China
works.abstract: Abstract Aerosol optical depth (AOD) is central to assessing aerosol climate forcing and air quality, yet persistent cloud cover and the absence of nighttime satellite retrievals preclude seamless, all-hour monitoring. Here, we develop an automated machine-learning framework that fuses a newly available gridded visibility data set with forecast AOD and spatiotemporal covariates to reconstruct AOD over China at an hourly 5 km resolution in near-real-time. Trained on geostationary satellite observations, the model achieves robust performance (Pearson correlation coefficient R = 0.95 in cross-validation) and outperforms reanalysis and forecast products while filling cloud- and darkness-induced gaps. Independent validation against MODIS and ground-based nighttime Aerosol Robotic Network (AERONET) measurements yields consistent accuracy (MODIS R = 0.61 and AERONET R = 0.76), confirming physical generalizability. The resulting seamless record exposes a pronounced diurnal cycle with a midday minimum and an early morning maximum, and documents a consistent year-on-year decline from 2020 to 2022 that aligns with China’s clean-air actions and COVID-19 lockdowns. During a record-breaking dust storm, the framework tracks aerosol dynamics during cloud-obscured and nocturnal phases, capturing an uninterrupted process-level account of the event. By delivering the day–night aerosol continuum at high resolution and low latency, this work bridges a critical observational gap in air-quality response, data assimilation, and diurnal aerosol-climate research.

works.title: Community science uncovers environmental azole resistance in Aspergillus fumigatus across Norway, including a novel tandem repeat variant (TR 62 )
works.abstract: ABSTRACT Azole-resistant Aspergillus fumigatus (AR Af ) is an emerging global health concern, mainly driven by environmental selection caused by azole fungicide use. Despite reports of environmental resistance across Europe, data from northern regions remain scarce. Here, we conducted the first nationwide investigation of environmental AR Af in Norway using a community science-based air sampling approach. Volunteers across the country collected airborne fungal spores using passive sticky-seal traps during three sampling periods between 2022 and 2023. In total, 2,332 air samples from 398 locations were analyzed, yielding 1,583 A. fumigatus isolates. Azole resistance screening identified 15 resistant isolates (0.95%) from 14 locations across four out of five Norwegian regions. Minimum inhibitory concentrations (MICs) confirmed resistance to medical azoles and elevated MICs toward azole fungicides. Whole-genome sequencing revealed known environmentally associated resistance mechanisms, including TR 34 /L98H ( n = 11) and TR 46 /Y121F/T289A ( n = 2), as well as a TR 46 /Y121F/T289A/S363P/I364V/G448S variant ( n = 1). In addition, a previously undescribed promoter tandem repeat variant (TR 62 ) was identified in one isolate that exhibited multi-azole resistance. Population genomic analyses indicated that resistant isolates were genetically diverse and not restricted to a single clonal lineage, suggesting both local expansion and recombination within a structured population. Although the observed resistance frequency was low, the presence of globally disseminated resistance mechanisms in airborne spores across Norway demonstrates that environmental azole resistance is established in the region. This study provides baseline data on the frequency and distribution of environmental AR Af in Norway and contributes to international efforts to strengthen monitoring of antifungal resistance. IMPORTANCE Azole-resistant Aspergillus fumigatus (ARAf) is an emerging public health concern, yet data from northern Europe remain limited. This study provides the first nationwide investigation of the frequency, distribution, and genetic diversity of environmental ARAf in Norway. By combining community-based environmental sampling with whole-genome sequencing, we demonstrate that resistance-associated genotypes of international concern are established in the Norwegian environment and occur across multiple regions. These findings provide important baseline data for future surveillance and contribute to global efforts to monitor and understand the emergence and spread of antifungal resistance.

works.title: Spatiotemporal recurrence and dissemination of Salmonella subpopulations in surface waters of central Chile
works.abstract: ABSTRACT Agricultural waters have been identified as one of the primary sources of Salmonella contamination, which has resulted in numerous outbreaks associated with the consumption of contaminated produce. Consequently, an improved understanding of Salmonella contamination of agricultural waters could facilitate the development of control strategies to prevent food contamination. The objective of this study was to examine the diversity and spatiotemporal recurrence of Salmonella isolates in surface water related to agricultural activities. Water samples ( n = 2,690) were collected between 2019 and 2024 in central Chile using modified Moore swabs, and whole-genome sequencing was carried out for 1 to 10 Salmonella isolates per sample. Non-clonal genomes from each sample ( n = 1,034) were analyzed, showing that the most frequently identified serovars were Infantis (14.6%), Typhimurium (10.8%), Newport (8.5%), and Enteritidis (5.8%). The highest antimicrobial resistance burden was shown by Salmonella Infantis, which carried up to 11 antimicrobial resistance genes simultaneously. Importantly, phylogenomic analyses revealed a highly clonal population structure among the most prevalent serovars and identified recurrent subpopulations that were repeatedly detected across multiple watersheds and consecutive years, including lineages associated with human infections. These findings provide genomic evidence that agricultural surface waters may serve as reservoirs and dissemination routes for recurrent Salmonella subpopulations in central Chile, including multidrug-resistant strains. Our work underscores the critical importance of continuous environmental surveillance and the integration of environmental and clinical genomic surveillance data to improve our understanding of the Salmonella ecology and inform evidence-based mitigation strategies aiming to protect public health. IMPORTANCE Salmonella enterica is a leading cause of foodborne illness worldwide, and contaminated irrigation water is an important pathway by which this pathogen can reach fresh produce. By analyzing more than 1,000 Salmonella genomes collected from agricultural waters in central Chile over 5 years, we found that specific bacterial lineages persisted across multiple watersheds and years, including multidrug-resistant strains linked to human infections. These findings indicate that agricultural surface waters in Chile can serve as reservoirs and dissemination routes for recurrent Salmonella subpopulations. Our study highlights the value of continuous environmental surveillance and the need to integrate data from environmental and human sources to identify potential contamination sources and reduce the risk of foodborne disease.

Tire-Derived Organic Pollutants across Urban Land Uses: Associations with Traffic Exposure
works.abstract: Abstract Tire-derived organic pollutants (TDOPs), particularly N-(1,3-dimethylbutyl)-N′-phenyl-p-phenylenediamine (6PPD) and its transformation product 6PPD-quinone (6PPD-Q), are increasingly recognized as emerging urban contaminants. However, their distribution and potential drivers in urban soils beyond the immediate roadside environment remain poorly characterized. In this study, 19 TDOPs were quantified in 28 urban soil samples representing four land-use types in Metro Detroit, Michigan, United States. TDOPs were widely detected in all soil samples, and 16 compounds exhibited detection frequencies ≥75%. Very low 6PPD/6PPD-Q ratios and the relative enrichment of N,N′-diphenyl-p-phenylenediamine (DPPD) over 6PPD suggest substantial environmental transformation of 6PPD. No statistically significant differences in the concentrations of TDOPs among land-use types or associations with measured soil properties were detected. In contrast, 6PPD exhibited a strong positive association with traffic-derived exposure metrics. The maximum Spearman rank correlation coefficient was observed for the commercial traffic exposure metric at a distance-decay parameter of 800 m (ρ = 0.76), and the association remained significant after optimization-adjusted permutation testing (pperm = 0.00030) and false discovery rate correction (q = 0.0048). This study demonstrates the widespread occurrence of TDOPs in urban soils beyond the immediate roadside environment and identifies modeled traffic exposure as an important correlate of soil 6PPD concentrations.

Electron Transfer Pathways Stretching from the Extracellular to Intracellular Membrane in Biohybrids Enable Enhanced CO2 Upcycling to Malate
works.abstract: Abstract Microbial electrosynthesis (MES) empowers one-step conversion of CO2 to long-chain chemicals under mild conditions, enabling sustainable biomanufacturing and achievement of a circular carbon economy. Although the construction of biohybrids has been explored to enhance the inherently low efficiency of MES, whether the binding modes between nanomaterials and microorganisms dictating CO2 conversion efficiency remain elusive. To address this query, we constructed biohybrids with three distinct integration modes (namely, internalization, outer membrane-contact, and transenvelope) between nanomaterials and Shewanella, enabling to proceed CO2-to-malate conversion. Upon MES-driven CO2-to-malate conversion, the transenvelope biohybrid constituted by polydopamine and Shewanella achieved a marked gram-scale malate titer of 19.14 mmol/L, as a result of the distinctive transenvelope capacity of polydopamine stretching from the extracellular to the intracellular membrane. This transenvelope capacity imparts extended electron transfer pathways spanning from the cytoplasmic membrane to the extracellular space, significantly reducing interfacial barriers at the electrode-microorganism interface and greatly promoting NADH and ATP synthesis for malate synthesis, which can enhance NADH synthesis. This work proposes the construction of a transenvelope biohybrid to optimize microbial metabolism, offering an alternative for the efficient valorization of CO2 to carbon-negative long-chain chemicals.

works.title: Organoid-Based Strategy for Exploration of Cancer-Related Early Signatures of Low-Dose Methylmercury Exposure
works.abstract: Abstract Methylmercury (MeHg) compounds are classified as Group 2B agents, possibly carcinogenic to humans by the International Agency for Research on Cancer (IARC), and as Group C possible human carcinogens by the U.S. Environmental Protection Agency (U.S. EPA), but the carcinogenic implications of environmentally relevant low-dose exposure remain unclear. Here, we established a population-informed organoid-based strategy to explore the potential of low-dose MeHg exposure leading to cancer incidence. A National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (NHANES)-based analysis revealed nonlinear associations of blood MeHg with overall cancer history with increased predicted cancer probability around 5.39 μg/L for MeHg. Liver organoid experiments showed that low-dose MeHg did not cause overt short-term cytotoxicity but induced DNA damage and stress-response signatures after prolonged exposure. Transcriptomic analysis further linked low-dose MeHg exposure to cancer-related stress pathways, including reactive oxygen species (ROS) associated chemical carcinogenesis, p53 signaling, DNA repair, mitochondrial stress, and cell-cycle regulation. These results indicate that low-dose MeHg exposure could trigger early biological responses related to cancer-associated processes before apparent cytotoxicity occurs. This study supports organoid models as a human-relevant strategy for linking population exposure signals with tissue-level toxicological evidence in MeHg research and provides a potentially adaptable framework for evaluating subtle health effects of low-dose environmental pollutants.

works.title: Biomass Hydrothermal Reduction Enables Direct Copper Recovery from Wastewater
works.abstract: Abstract Recovering copper (Cu) from strongly acidic copper wastewater (SACW) is essential for resource sustainability and environmental preservation, but conventional technologies bear high economic costs and generate secondary pollution. Here, we demonstrate a biomass waste-mediated hydrothermal reduction process that simultaneously removes and recovers Cu as metallic Cu from SACW. The process operates under mild conditions (180 °C, 7 h) and achieves over 99% removal of Cu(II) across a wide concentration range, directly reducing Cu(II) to metallic Cu(0) without incorporation into hydrochar. Notably, the liquid products from biomass hydrothermal treatment, particularly 2-furoic acid, served as electron donors for Cu(II) reduction, with its C2/C3 atoms potentially providing electron transfer channels that drive the stepwise reduction of Cu(II) to Cu(0). In a 5 L pilot test with two types of industrial wastewater, the technology achieved >99% Cu(II) removal (residual <0.5 mg/L) and recovered metallic Cu with a purity of 99.9% after simple calcination. Life-cycle assessment and technoeconomic analysis highlight superior economic and environmental benefits when treating high-concentration copper-containing wastewater, establishing a sustainable, generalized hydrothermal reduction platform for efficient Cu recovery from industrial wastewaters. This work establishes a chemistry-driven paradigm for sustainable wastewater treatment, enabling efficient circular recovery of high-value resources from acidic metal-containing wastewaters.

works.title: Zeolite-Regulated Electron-Rich Cu–O–Ce Sites for Efficient Denitrification against Alkali/Heavy Metal Poisoning
works.abstract: Abstract Enhancing the wide-temperature-window deNOx activity of catalysts under alkali/heavy metal poisoning conditions remains a pivotal challenge in the field of environmental catalysis. To tackle this issue, we designed a novel CuCeOx/ZSM-5 catalyst using an acid-rich zeolite-modulated electron-enriched metal site strategy. This strategy enables the contact between strong acid sites and Cu–O–Ce active sites, simultaneously regulating the efficient NH3–SCR temperature window and enhancing K/Pb poisoning resistance. Compared to CuCeOx, the engineered acid-rich interface significantly facilitates electron transfer from ZSM-5 to CuCeOx, generating electron-rich Cu–O–Ce active sites. These sites not only serve as adjacent adsorption and activation centers for reactants but also inhibit NH3 oxidation, and CuCeOx/ZSM-5 catalyst achieves >90% deNOx efficiency over a wide temperature range of 180–410 °C (T90 = 180–410 °C). K deactivates the catalyst mainly by reducing surface acidity and promoting the accumulation of less-reactive nitrate species, while Pb primarily suppresses Ce4+ → Ce3+ reduction via inducing Cu2+ → Cu+ conversion and occupying CeO2 oxygen vacancies. Notably, the poisoned CuCeOx/ZSM-5 catalyst still retains satisfactory deNOx performance, with the T90 = 230–380 °C. This work not only provides novel mechanistic insights into the deactivation pathways of NH3–SCR catalysts by alkali and heavy metal ions but also offers a viable strategy for the rational design of high-performance, poisoning-tolerant NH3–SCR catalysts tailored for complex flue gas environments.

works.title: Missed Opportunities Forgo One-Third of Mass Timber’s Carbon Storage Potential
works.abstract: Abstract Building materials are increasingly positioned as a scalable option for carbon dioxide removal (CDR). Carbon-storing engineered wood products, such as structural mass timber, will be instrumental for CDR. However, system-level perspectives can overlook operational choices that forfeit storage potential. Using stage-resolved life-cycle inventories, scenario-aware uncertainty analysis, and dynamic carbon accounting, we trace carbon flows across mass timber supply chains in the United States, from harvest slash and mill residue to wood products through end-of-life. Across modeled deployment scenarios, we show that management decisions, not technical limits, cut 1.4–2.6 gigatons (Gt) of CO2e storage by 2120, corresponding to roughly one-third of mass timber’s storage potential. Globally, storage losses from these choices could reach 3.8–12 Gt CO2e. We outline a storage-first pathway including slash pyrolysis, diversion of mill residue from bioenergy to wood panel markets, and reuse or pyrolysis at end-of-life. Together, these strategies redirect carbon into value-added, long-lived pools rather than short-lived fates, showing that release timing and supply chain routing choices can matter more than production decarbonization in shaping warming outcomes under mass timber deployment. If implemented, these choices recover forgone storage and aid in developing the built environment as a durable carbon reservoir.

works.title: Emerging Hexafluoropropylene Oxide Trimer Acid Potently Targets Farnesoid X Receptor and Triggers Hepatic Cholestasis
works.abstract: Abstract Per- and polyfluoroalkyl substance (PFAS) hepatotoxicity is a critical global health threat, and disrupted bile acid metabolism is considered a key driver of PFAS-triggered liver injury, yet the underlying mechanisms remain unclear. Herein, we explored the hepatotoxic mechanisms of emerging hexafluoropropylene oxide trimer acid (HFPO-TA) and dimer acid (HFPO–DA) via farnesoid X receptor (FXR), assessed their health risks, and further compared their effects against perfluorooctanoic acid (PFOA). In rat, HFPO-TA exerted more potent hepatotoxicity than PFOA and HFPO–DA, triggering typical cholestasis through impaired biliary excretion and altered bile acid pool. Mechanistically, all three PFASs promoted the intracellular bile acid accumulation by inhibiting FXR transcriptional activity, with potent HFPO-TA > PFOA > HFPO–DA. Accordingly, HFPO-TA, HFPO–DA, and PFOA can directly bind to FXR though entering the ligand-binding domain via hydrogen bonding and hydrophobic interactions to stabilize an antagonizing conformation. Notably, HFPO-TA bound FXR with 3.25-fold higher affinity than endogenous chenodeoxycholic acid and 50-fold higher affinity than PFOA, accompanied by elevated receptor-bound concentrations (RBCs). RBC-based risk assessment revealed moderate risk in 28.3% of HFPO-TA-exposed residents. Overall, HFPO-TA directly binds to FXR to induce hepatic cholestasis; such FXR-mediated cholestasis poses notable health risks and warrants broad vigilance toward PFAS liver hazards.

works.title: Redox-Active Electrodes Enable Selective Ammonium Recovery and Reuse for Rare Earth Mining
works.abstract: Abstract Rare earth element (REE) extraction from ion-adsorption deposits relies on ammonium (NH4+) assisted in situ leaching, yet the spent leachant is typically discarded as wastewater rather than recovered for reuse. Here, we report a redox-active electrosorption platform that selectively recovers NH4+ from REE tailings wastewater and enables its direct reuse in the leaching process, establishing a circular approach to nitrogen management. This platform employs nickel-substituted copper hexacyanoferrate as redox hosts for reversible ammonium storage. Nickel incorporation modifies the redox and ion-transport properties of CuHCF while improving framework stability. The resulting Cu0.8Ni0.2HCF redox-active electrode exhibits a high capacity of 82.6 mAh g–1, superior cycling durability (>90% retention after 30 h), and remarkable ammonium selectivity over Na+ (9.2), Ca2+ (19.3), Mg2+ (25.5), La3+ (38.5), and Y3+ (42.2). Multiscale characterizations and calculations support favorable NH4+ host–guest interactions and ion transport within the framework. The recovered ammonium is directly reused for ion-adsorption-type rare earth leaching with extraction performance comparable to fresh leachants. Life-cycle assessment and techno-economic analyses demonstrate reduced environmental footprint and favorable economic feasibility. This study established a redox-active electrosorption platform that shifts nitrogen management from a linear “treatment-discharge” model toward a circular “recovery-reuse” pathway.

works.title: Engineering High-Entropy Interfaces in a Single-Metal Cu System to Drive Concerted Nonradical Catalysis and Pollutant Sequestration
works.abstract: Abstract Nonradical direct electron transfer (DET) can make advanced oxidation less vulnerable to radical scavenging in complex waters, but requires catalysts with efficient charge transport, stability, and practical synthesis. High-entropy materials provide diverse local environments, yet their multimetal compositions and prolonged heat treatment limit implementation. We combined chemically induced self-internal heating (SIH) with chloride-induced interfacial reconstruction to prepare a single-metal Cu system with high-density grain boundaries (SM-HDGB). SIH formed a Cu-carbon precursor in 3.5 s through an internal pulse above 1200 °C. HCl treatment generated intergrown Cu, Cu2O, CuCl, and Cu2Cl(OH)3 domains spaced 2–10 nm apart, creating phase, oxidation-state, and coordination diversity described as empirical interfacial chemical-state entropy. SM-HDGB completely removed tetracycline within 10 min and increased the apparent rate constant 9.88-fold over the precursor, with little response to 10 mM coexisting anions. Electron paramagnetic resonance, scavenging, filtration, electrochemical, and in situ spectroscopic evidence supported predominantly surface-confined, catalyst-mediated DET. In packed-bed operation, SM-HDGB maintained more than 80% COD removal across four regeneration cycles (approximately 130 h), retained pollutant-derived organic products, and produced near-neutral effluent compatible with Chlorella growth. Laboratory-scale screening estimated at least 96.3% lower synthesis energy demand than conventional routes. Chemical-state-diverse single-metal interfaces can therefore couple rapid peroxydisulfate activation with stable continuous-flow treatment.

works.title: Organophosphate Flame Retardants Induce Neurodegenerative Pathologies by Paralyzing HSP90AB1 Chaperone Function: A Multi-Scale Computational and Biophysical Study
works.abstract: Abstract This study integrated computational toxicology with biophysical and cellular validation to investigate the neurotoxic potential of 10 flame-retardant-related compounds. ADMETlab 3.0 predicted blood-brain barrier probabilities of 0.989 for bis(1,3-dichloro-2-propyl) phosphate and 0.444 for diphenyl phosphate (DPHP), interpreted as screening predictions. Network topology analysis identified HSP90AB1 as a shared candidate hub target linking organophosphate flame retardants to Alzheimer’s and Parkinson’s diseases. Molecular dynamics simulations indicated a stable HSP90AB1 backbone in the DPHP complex (root-mean-square deviation ∼0.18 nm). Surface plasmon resonance measured an equilibrium dissociation constant of 1.49 μM. DPHP induced dose-dependent cytotoxicity in neuronal cells; the half-maximal inhibitory concentration was not determined within the tested range. HSP90AB1 overexpression mitigated DPHP-induced reactive oxygen species production and transcriptional upregulation of pro-apoptotic and pro-inflammatory genes. Single-cell virtual knockout identified candidate regulatory processes; Parkinson’s disease-related enrichment remained exploratory after multiple-testing correction. Together, the computational, biophysical, and cellular findings support HSP90AB1 as a candidate target of environmental neurotoxicity and motivate further investigation of DPHP.

works.title: Partition-Buffered Leaching of 6PPD-Quinone from Tire Wear Particles
works.abstract: Abstract 6PPD-quinone (6PPDQ; N-(1,3-dimethylbutyl)-N′-phenyl-p-phenylenediamine-quinone) forms on tire-derived solid surfaces, including those of intact tires and environmentally dispersed tire wear particles (TWPs), yet its leaching kinetics remain insufficiently characterized for confident use in watershed and coastal fate-and-transport models. Here, we conducted time-resolved saturated column leaching experiments to quantify 6PPDQ leaching from lab-generated TWPs and to derive a physically based parametrization. Across hour-to-month observation windows, TWPs exhibited sustained, nearly linear 6PPDQ release (α ≈ 1) and weak particle-size scaling of the characteristic time scale, inconsistent with whole-particle Fickian diffusion. We tested a mechanistic hypothesis that strong TWP-water partitioning buffers aqueous concentrations and limits 6PPDQ mass export. Using a well-mixed column reactor (WMCR) representation, we estimated the TWP-water partition coefficient Ksw for the columns. The regression yielded log10 Ksw = 4.37 ± 0.22. Building on this mechanistic interpretation, we derived a Newtonian first-order leaching term suitable for hydrologic and coastal modeling. A two-compartment formulation further indicated that the TWP concentration, cTWP, strongly controls the apparent fraction of 6PPDQ released to the dissolved phase. These findings may help explain variability across prior leaching studies while bridging inconsistencies between experimental and field measurements.

works.title: Solar-Driven Cu(II)–Cu(III) Redox Cycle on Decahedral BiVO4 for Scalable Water Purification
works.abstract: Abstract Conventional Fenton-like reactions rely on external oxidants to generate reactive oxygen species (ROS, e.g., high-valent metal-oxo species (HVMS)), a practice that is inherently unsustainable for water purification. Here, we propose a solar-driven Cu(II)–Cu(III) redox cycle that differs from the traditional view that HVMS generation originates from peroxide-mediated pathways. By tuning the anisotropic built-in field of decahedral BiVO4, photogenerated holes accumulate selectively on its {110} family, enabling hole-driven hydrated Cu(II) oxidation instead of water. This facilitates an oxygen atom transfer (OAT) from adjacent Bi–OH sites to the H-bonded Cu(II) center, stabilizing the Cu(III)-oxo center by forming the Bi–O–Cu(III)–O structure (Cu(III)). Meanwhile, electron-driven dissolved oxygen reduction maintains charge balance. The photosynthetic Cu(III) mediates antibiotic degradation with a rate constant of 0.174 min–1, representing a ∼16-fold enhancement in the degradation rate constant compared to traditional photocatalysis. Crucially, the solar BiVO4 sheet/Cu(II) system sustains consistent up to ∼85% moxifloxacin degradation efficiency in each cycle over 35 days. No total Cu was detected in the effluent of cycling experiments after pH adjustment (∼7.5). These findings provide a new solution to the long-standing challenge of achieving peroxide-free HVMS synthesis and scalable water purification.

works.title: Multitechnique Characterization of Dissolved Organic Matter from Naturally Acidic and Circumneutral Waters Reveals Molecular Controls on Organic Nitrogen Speciation
works.abstract: Abstract The molecular characteristics of dissolved organic matter (DOM) vary across seasons, catchments, and land uses, highlighting the need for generalized structure–function relationships that can predict intrinsic DOM bioavailability. This study characterized DOM from naturally acidic (pH 4.3–5.7) and circumneutral (pH 6.8–8.3) freshwaters over two seasons: winter-spring (WS) and summer-autumn (SA) using multiple characterization techniques (optical, fluorescence, targeted LC-MS/MS, 13C NMR, and FTIR). DOM from acidic environments was higher in aromaticity, more humic-like, with a higher C:N ratio but with a greater percentage of nitrogen in the form of amino acids (i.e., DCAA-N%). Seasonality was only observed for neutral samples, with differences between WS and SA dominated by a decrease in nominal molecular weight (MWn) in SA, likely driven by photochemical disaggregation. FTIR analysis indicates that neutral DOM has a higher amide group abundance than acidic DOM despite the lower DCAA-N%, suggesting the dominance of nonproteinaceous amide-N. Very strong dependencies were observed for dissolved organic nitrogen (DON) speciation against aromaticity (SUVA254) and an FTIR-derived ratio of deprotonated carboxylic:aromatic groups, describing the relative hydrophilicity–hydrophobicity of the DOM environment. These parameters largely explain the DCAA distribution and may provide a more generalized way of characterizing DOM that could be applied across different aquatic ecosystems.

works.title: Contrasting Dynamics of Particle-Bound Organophosphate Esters Reveal Distinct High-Altitude Contaminant Transport Processes over the Tibetan Plateau
works.abstract: Abstract Particle-bound semivolatile organic compounds (SVOCs) reaching high-mountain regions are commonly interpreted in terms of temperature-driven gas-particle partitioning and precipitation scavenging. To investigate these competing dynamics, we report year-round, synchronous measurements of particle-bound organophosphate esters (OPEs) in PM2.5 at two contrasting Tibetan Plateau sites: a southern Himalayan receptor (QOMS) and an inland background site (NAMORS). ΣOPEs averaged 111 ± 125 pg m–3 at QOMS and 20 ± 17 pg m–3 at NAMORS, exhibiting a counterintuitive warm-season maximum. This warm-season peak coincided with a 72–91% decline in hygroscopic secondary inorganic aerosols, indicating that trans-Himalayan transport sustains substantial particle-bound OPE inputs during the monsoon despite intense wet deposition. Furthermore, chlorinated congeners with stronger particle association (TCPP, TDCPP) dominated at both sites (TCEP/TCPP = 0.09–0.46). This contrasts with the highly volatile TCEP-dominated profiles reported for Arctic aerosols. Such a difference is consistent with an orographic modulation favoring particulate-phase retention during the shorter trans-Himalayan ascent. However, the lack of simultaneous gas-phase data and potential differences in regional emission histories must also be acknowledged. Back-trajectory clustering and principal component analysis both point to South Asian source regions as the principal control at QOMS. Consequently, correlations of OPEs with temperature and precipitation are better read as proxies for monsoon transport intensity than as evidence of local thermodynamic partitioning. Continued transboundary input suggests that particle-bound OPEs may contribute to deposition and subsequent accumulation in the alpine cryosphere, highlighting the urgent need to incorporate transboundary transport pathways into regional contaminant assessments.

works.title: Toward Dynamic Biointerface Toxicology of Micro- and Nanoplastics Using Organoids and Organ-on-a-Chip Models
works.abstract: Abstract Micro- and nanoplastic (MNP) toxicity depends on the exposure conditions under which particles encounter biological tissues, yet nominal material descriptors alone do not resolve these conditions. Environmental transformation, biomolecular adsorption, aggregation, and chemical release can alter particle delivery and biological interactions. This Review evaluates these processes alongside evidence from organoids and organ-on-a-chip models, distinguishing direct MNP findings from analogue studies and demonstrations of platform capability. We propose exposure identity as an analytical framework connecting particle history and state with tissue encounter and subsequent processing over time. The synthesis examines what available studies establish about tissue access, barrier responses, distal relay, and susceptibility, and where interpretation remains constrained by exposure characterization or unresolved mechanisms. Human-derived models provide opportunities to investigate tissue-specific responses, but neither biological complexity nor perfusion establishes environmental representativeness or predictive validity. We identify measurement and control requirements for separating particle transfer from chemical release and tissue-derived signaling, interpreting absent effects, and evaluating heterogeneous exposures. Priorities include traceable delivered-dose measurements, synchronized exposure and response sampling, targeted mechanistic tests, and independent validation for a defined use. The proposed framework organizes evidence and testable relationships while retaining uncertainty about generalization to human exposure and health outcomes.

works.title: Investigating the Relationships between the Structure and Cytotoxicity of Ionic Liquids in the Context of Cell Lines Being Affected
works.abstract: Abstract Current quantitative structure–activity relationship (QSAR) models of ionic liquid (IL) cytotoxicity are generally developed for specific biological systems and cannot be assumed to transfer across cell types. Here, we evaluated 81 ILs spanning eight cationic head groups and 13 anions in HEK293T, CaCo-2, and DF-1 cell lines. The alkyl side chain length was the dominant structural determinant within homologous series, whereas cation, anion, and functionalization effects were most evident among ILs with shorter alkyl side chains. Mechanistic assays with 1-alkyl-3-methylimidazolium chlorides revealed distinct 24-h cellular response profiles in HEK293T and DF-1 cells, including different patterns of membrane permeabilization, apoptosis, and mitochondrial membrane potential changes. Descriptor-cytotoxicity correlations were strong within homologous imidazolium series but were less transferable across other structural comparisons. These results show that structure-based models can be informative within a defined chemical and cellular domain, but the cell type and cytotoxic response must be considered when extrapolating the IL cytotoxicity and assessing the safety of ILs proposed as greener process media.

works.title: Non-Targeted Characterization and Hazard-Based Prioritization of Disinfection Byproducts and Co-Contaminants in U.S. Drinking Water Distribution Systems
works.abstract: Abstract Higher-carbon (>C2) disinfection byproducts (DBPs) remain poorly characterized in drinking water distribution systems (DWDSs) despite evidence that they may contribute substantially to drinking water toxicity. Here, we applied liquid chromatography–high-resolution mass spectrometry and non-targeted analysis to characterize >C2 DBPs and co-contaminants across 12 U.S. DWDSs spanning a range of pre-oxidation and disinfection strategies. For each DWDS, we analyzed finished drinking water and distribution system samples collected at locations representing short, medium, and long distances from the treatment plant. We identified multiple classes of >C2 DBPs, including non-halogenated and halogenated hydroxybenzoic acids, halohydroxybenzaldehydes, halonitrophenols, (halo)phenylacetamides, (halo)fumaric acids, and several emerging nitrogenous DBPs. In addition, we also detected various co-contaminants such as pesticides, pharmaceuticals, and industrial chemicals. DBPs and co-contaminants exhibited system-specific occurrence and spatial patterns, and non-halogenated hydroxybenzoic acids emerged as an overlooked and widespread class of DBPs. To support prioritization efforts, hazard data from EPA’s Hazard Comparison Module was used to develop and implement hazard-weighted prioritization metrics. This approach identified (halo)hydroxybenzoic acids, halonitrophenols, DEET, triazine herbicides, and 2-hydroxyquinoline as high-priority contaminants, indicating that both emerging DBPs and co-contaminants may contribute to mixture-level hazards in distributed drinking water. Overall, this work expands the known >C2 DBP landscape and provides a framework for prioritizing drinking water contaminants detected by non-targeted analysis.

works.title: Integrated physiological and multiomic analyses reveal the multilayered aluminum tolerance mechanisms of acidophilic alga Coccomyxa sp. A2
works.abstract: ABSTRACT Acid mine drainage (AMD) is a pervasive global environmental challenge, and algal-based bioremediation represents one of the most robust strategies for its treatment. However, the mechanisms by which algae survive in metal-rich AMD remain largely unclear. Here, we integrated physiological, transcriptomic, and proteomic analyses to explore the tolerance mechanisms of the acidophilic alga Coccomyxa sp. A2 to aluminum (Al), a metal prevalent in AMD. The results demonstrated that A2 exhibited substantially higher Al tolerance than the model alga Chlamydomonas reinhardtii under their respective optimal pH conditions. Upon Al exposure, A2 significantly increased the extracellular levels of three strong organic acids (oxalic, citric, and tartaric acids), thereby facilitating chelation of free Al 3+ present in the acidic environment. In the near-neutral cytosol, A2 accumulated a broader array of organic acids at higher concentrations to sequester Al despite severe extracellular H + stress. To restrict Al influx, A2 enhanced the synthesis of cellulose, hemicellulose, and proteins across the distinct layers of its cell wall, increasing cell wall dry weight by 66%. This remodeling was probably supported by starch degradation, enhanced gluconeogenesis, and Calvin cycle activation, which together supplied sufficient monosaccharide precursors for polysaccharide synthesis. Concurrently, the upregulation of glycosyltransferases facilitated rapid polysaccharide chain elongation. To scavenge ROS, the alga likely initiated a temporally coordinated, biphasic antioxidant response, in which non-enzymatic ascorbic acid pools compensated for lagging superoxide dismutase activity during the early acute phase of stress. Calcium, abscisic acid, and jasmonic acid coordinated these defense mechanisms, with calcium serving as the primary signaling hub. IMPORTANCE The conventional treatment method for acid mine drainage (AMD) involves neutralization with lime, which is costly and generates large amounts of sludge that is difficult to manage. The application of sulfate-reducing bacteria (SRB) presents a promising alternative by eliminating secondary pollution and enabling metal sulfide recovery. However, a key challenge of this approach is ensuring an affordable and sustainable organic carbon source for SRB since AMD is oligotrophic. A potential solution is the in-situ cultivation of acidophilic algae. Given the high metal concentrations in AMD, investigating the metal tolerance mechanisms of acidophilic algae is vital for producing sufficient biomass to support SRB. Meanwhile, about 40% of the world’s arable soils are acidic, and these soils typically contain high concentrations of aluminum (Al), which is a major factor limiting crop production. Therefore, research on the exceptional Al tolerance mechanisms of acidophilic algae can provide insights into improving crop metal resistance through genetic engineering techniques.

works.title: Temperature defines metabolic states that lead to seasonal adaptation of the soil nitrite oxidizer Nitrobacter vulgaris strain CN101
works.abstract: ABSTRACT Nitrite-oxidizing bacteria (NOB) play a central role in nitrification, yet their temperature-dependent ecophysiology remains poorly understood, particularly in terrestrial environments. In this study, the physiological and transcriptomic responses of Nitrobacter vulgaris strain CN101, isolated from forest soil in Japan, were investigated across different culture temperatures. Temperature-dependent kinetics revealed two distinct activation energies below and above 20°C, suggesting a shift in metabolic state. At lower temperatures, nitrite oxidation rates declined, and transcriptomic analysis showed reduced expression of genes involved in electron transport and protein synthesis, whereas genes related to carbon and nitrogen assimilation remained relatively unchanged. Electron microscopy revealed smaller cell size and simplified membrane structures under low-temperature conditions. Together, these findings indicate that metabolic activity is maintained while biomass production is constrained below 20°C. At higher temperatures, efficient electron transport, increased translational capacity, and enlarged cell morphology were restored, consistent with a growth-promoting state. These coordinated metabolic and structural changes suggest that strain CN101 adopts a temperature-dependent strategy that balances survival and proliferation in seasonally fluctuating forest soils. By integrating physiological, ultrastructural, and transcriptomic analyses, this study provides a concrete example of how temperature influences the ecophysiological adaptation of terrestrial NOB. IMPORTANCE Nitrification is a key microbial process in the global nitrogen cycle, yet how nitrifying microorganisms remain active under fluctuating environmental conditions remains poorly understood. In temperate soils, seasonal temperature variation strongly influences nitrification, but the physiological responses of nitrite-oxidizing bacteria (NOB) remain largely unexplored. In this study, we show that the soil nitrite oxidizer Nitrobacter vulgaris strain CN101 exhibits temperature-dependent physiological states, shifting from a metabolically active but growth-limited state at low temperatures to a state of active growth at higher temperatures. These findings demonstrate how temperature restructures NOB metabolism and physiology. This study provides a representative example of the seasonal ecophysiology of soil nitrifiers and highlights temperature-driven physiological restructuring as a key mechanism shaping nitrification dynamics in terrestrial ecosystems.

works.title: Cost-effective climate change mitigation through land sector contributions
works.abstract: Abstract Climate change mitigation from Agriculture, Forestry and Other Land Use (AFOLU) comes with severe sustainability risks and faces major implementation challenges. Yet, the consequences of missing out on AFOLU mitigation potential for the transition of the energy sector and the achievability of climate objectives are not well understood. Here, using the Integrated Assessment Modeling framework REMIND–MAgPIE, we derive future mitigation pathways under different AFOLU policy portfolios. We show that, without AFOLU contributions to mitigation, limiting warming to 1.5 °C is out of reach within the twenty-first century and for keeping peak warming below 1.7 °C consumption loss relative to a current-policy baseline increases from 1.3% to 3.5%. A portfolio of options alleviates the burden of energy sector decarbonization and substantially reduces energy price markups, but puts the AFOLU sector under stress. We show that prudent policy measures, such as limiting total bioenergy use to 100 EJ yr −1 and restricting CH 4 and N 2 O pricing to US$75 per tonne of CO 2 equivalent, can largely attenuate this pressure by reducing the need for yield increases and diminishing food price markups without severely compromising the achievability of climate targets. Our findings highlight both the need for effective climate action in the AFOLU sector and the importance of balanced and judicious sectorally aligned policies.

Biodegradation mechanisms of PBDE − 209: enzymatic, microbial, and omics-driven insights
works.abstract: Decabromodiphenyl ether (PBDE - 209) is the most extensively produced and environmentally persistent congener among polybrominated diphenyl ethers (PBDEs) and remains widely detected in soils, sediments, sludge, dust, and biota despite global regulatory restrictions. Its extreme bromination, strong hydrophobicity, and resistance to physicochemical degradation limit natural attenuation and complicate remediation efforts. Although biological processes are increasingly recognized as key drivers of BDE - 209 transformation, current knowledge remains fragmented across microbial, enzymatic, and molecular scales, hindering predictive understanding and effective remediation strategies. Unlike previous PBDE reviews that examine microbial taxa or degradation reactions in isolation, this review provides a systems-level synthesis that integrates microbial ecology, enzyme catalysis, metabolic bottlenecks, and multi-omics evidence to explain why PBDE - 209 biodegradation frequently remains incomplete in both natural and engineered systems. Reductive debromination, oxidative transformation, and stepwise formation of lower-brominated intermediates are critically examined alongside with their environmental relevance and toxicity implications. Recent advances in metagenomic, transcriptomics, proteomics, and metabolomics are integrated to identify key functional genes, active enzymes, metabolic constraints, and cooperative microbial interactions governing degradation efficiency. The review further evaluates emerging biotechnological strategies, such as bioaugmentation, biostimulation, engineered microbial systems, immobilized enzymes, synthetic consortia, rhizoremediation, and advanced bioreactor configurations, with emphasis on overcoming bioavailability limitations and minimizing accumulation of toxic intermediate. By consolidating mechanistic insights across biological scales, this review establishes a comprehensive systems-level framework to advance predictive understanding and guide the development of effective, field-applicable remediation strategies for BDE - 209 contaminated environment.

works.title: Extracellular Polymeric Substances Govern Horizontal Gene Transfer of Antibiotic Resistance Genes: Mechanisms, Pathway Specificity, and Research Gaps
works.abstract: Abstract The dissemination of antibiotic resistance genes (ARGs) in environmental systems is recognized as being shaped by local matrix conditions, yet the pathway-specific role of extracellular polymeric substances (EPS), the dominant matrix of biofilms, sludge flocs, and granules, remains poorly resolved. In this Review, we develop a mechanism- and pathway-resolved perspective for evaluating how EPS govern horizontal gene transfer (HGT) of ARGs. Current evidence indicates that conjugation is the most directly supported pathway, with EPS facilitating or restricting transfer through effects on donor–recipient contact, matrix organization, and transfer-related physiology. For transformation, EPS-associated extracellular ARGs constitute reservoirs, but EPS–DNA binding can both preserve genetic material and limit its immediate bioavailability. By contrast, EPS involvement in phage-mediated transduction and vesicle-mediated transfer remains mechanistically plausible but insufficiently validated. We identify five interconnected mechanisms: physical retention and spatial organization, DNA adsorption and bioavailability, regulation of intercellular contact, modulation of cell physiology and transfer competence, and community-scale mobilome coupling. By clarifying evidence boundaries across pathways, this Review moves EPS–HGT research from correlation-based interpretation toward mechanism-informed assessment of ARG mobility. We conclude by outlining research needs, including standardized EPS definition and extraction, component-resolved characterization, pathway-resolved causal assays, and validation in realistic environmental aggregates.

works.title: Chemically Stratified Urban Boundary Layer: Seasonally Reversing Vertical Changes in the Underlying Chemistry of Atmospheric Oxidation Capacity
works.abstract: Abstract The vertical structure of atmospheric oxidation capacity (AOC) and its underlying radical chemistry within the urban boundary layer remains poorly characterized, yet it governs secondary pollutant formation. Here, we combined tower-based vertical observations with process-resolved model simulations in Beijing across winter and summer. We find that AOC generally declined with height in both seasons, but radical concentrations exhibit opposite vertical gradients. Notably, enhanced biogenic volatile organic compounds (VOCs) emissions in summer suppress near-surface OH levels, creating a mid-altitude maximum. However, sharp vertical NO gradients drove an increase in ROx with height in winter. The underlying chemistry of vertical AOC variation shifts with the seasons. In winter, the photolysis of HONO dominates ROx production, and NOx-driven ROx loss prevails. In summer, the photolysis of oxygenated VOCs takes over, with radical self-reactions as the primary ROx sink. These findings demonstrate that surface observations alone may provide an incomplete representation of the whole boundary-layer chemistry.

works.title: Ionizing Radiation Sustains Fenton Oxidation through Radiolytic Fe Redox Cycling for Deep Mineralization of Refractory Pollutants
works.abstract: Abstract The limited regeneration of Fe(II) from Fe(III) constrains sustained oxidation and mineralization in conventional Fenton processes. Here, we investigate an ionizing radiation-assisted Fenton process (IRFP) in which radiolytic Fe redox cycling sustains Fe-mediated oxidation. Using sulfasalazine as a model pollutant, we demonstrate that radiolytically generated hydrated electrons support two coupled pathways: rapid H2O2 activation and the conversion of Fe(III) to Fe(II). The resulting Fe redox cycling dynamically replenishes the Fe(II) pool alongside radiolytic H2O2 activation, thereby sustaining oxidative transformation beyond the initial degradation stage. Compared with irradiation and conventional Fenton treatment, IRFP promoted deeper fragmentation of azo, sulfonamide, and aromatic structures, resulting in enhanced mineralization. Transformation-product analysis further showed that continued transformation in IRFP reduced the persistence of complex intermediates with elevated predicted toxicity. In real pharmaceutical and coking wastewaters, IRFP achieved effective treatment under near-neutral conditions with substantially lower H2O2 and Fe(II) requirements than Fenton treatment and lower absorbed doses than irradiation alone. Although its electricity demand remained higher than short-time Fenton treatment, the markedly lower dosage of chemicals reduced the potential iron sludge burden and resulted in lower estimated COD-normalized treatment costs under the investigated conditions. These findings establish radiolytic Fe redox cycling as a strategy for sustaining Fe-mediated oxidation and promoting deeper transformation and mineralization of refractory pollutants.
