Abnormal Event Monitoring of Drainage Pipelines Based on Distributed Optical Fiber Vibration Sensing
works.abstract: Abstract Urban drainage networks are critical infrastructure for modern cities, yet their complex and concealed nature makes real-time monitoring of abnormal events a persistent challenge. To address this, this work proposed a distributed optical fiber vibration sensing system based on phase-sensitive optical time-domain reflectometry (Φ-OTDR) for drainage pipeline monitoring. To accurately capture abnormal events from complex environmental noise, a two-tier intelligent processing architecture comprising localization and classification modules was developed. The localization module employed an enhanced You Only Look Once (YOLO) model integrating anchor-box optimization, a channel-attention module, and an additional small-target feature layer, achieving a mean average precision of 96.8% in laboratory tests. The classification module utilized a hybrid model combining convolutional neural network, bidirectional long short-term memory, and attention classifier, achieving an overall accuracy of 98.1% for five abnormal events. During two-week of continuous field monitoring, the system localized simulated events with errors below 2.60 m and distinguished internal leakage, knocking, and drilling from walking, running, and vehicle interference with precision and recall exceeding 99.6% for the tested classes. Notably, the system successfully detected and accurately localized an actual branch pipe leakage event, demonstrating its practical effectiveness under real-world operating conditions.

works.title: Microplastics Rapidly Sink and Beach in a Whole-Lake Experiment
works.abstract: Abstract Although advances in oceanographic and limnological modeling have increased our understanding of microplastic transport and persistence, we require more knowledge to effectively protect biodiversity. We initiated a whole-lake experiment (the pELAstic project) to measure the real-world fate and transport of microplastics. We added microplastics to a boreal lake, simulating stormwater input, at loading concentrations predicted to achieve environmentally relevant concentrations. Here, we introduce our experiment and describe the particle budget from the first microplastic addition. We observed rapid transport of microplastics to different ecosystem compartments. Transport patterns could not be fully explained by initial particle size and density, highlighting how natural processes modify plastic fate in real-world systems. Microplastic fragments rapidly redistributed─exiting the water column and settling on the bottom and shorelines. A particle budget across the water column, bottom sediments, and beaches accounted for 77% of the polyethylene, 48% polystyrene, and >100% polyethylene terephthalate. “Missing” plastic was likely in the nearshore littoral. Our observations suggest that if we prevent further inputs to aquatic ecosystems, microplastics will quickly disappear from the water column─washing up on shorelines and settling on the bottom. Thus, understanding rates of microplastic deposition and burial is critical to forecast the legacy of microplastic pollution.

works.title: Far-UVC Activation of Performic Acid Enables Concurrent Oxidative and Reductive Micropollutant Abatement
works.abstract: Abstract Conventional UV-driven advanced oxidation and reduction processes generally emphasize one redox regime and can be inhibited by wastewater constituents. Here, we characterize the photochemistry of performic acid (PFA) under 222 and 254 nm irradiation and evaluate the capacity of PFA solution, prepared from H2O2 and formic acid and thus containing residual H2O2 and formate, to generate concurrent oxidative and reductive pathways. Relative to 254 nm, 222 nm irradiation increased the fluence-normalized photodecay rate constants of neutral PFA (PFA0) and its conjugate base (PFA–) by 1.21- and 3.81-fold, respectively. The increase arose from 16.1- and 10.1-fold larger molar absorption coefficients at 222 nm, despite lower fitted innate quantum yields (0.367 and 0.804 molecule photon–1 at 222 nm versus 0.587 and 0.819 molecule photon–1 at 254 nm). The UV222/PFA solution system generated the reductant •CO2– together with oxidative HO• and oxygen-centered organic radicals. Pathway analysis attributed 34% of carbamazepine removal to •CO2– and 19% of naproxen removal to R-O• at 222 nm. Chloride and bromide enhanced fluence-normalized degradation through reactive-halogen chemistry; the largest increases were observed for carbamazepine (47.5-fold at 254 nm and 21.9-fold at 222 nm). In real municipal wastewater, UV222/PFA solution decreased total organic carbon by 33.5% within 60 min, compared with 21.6% under UV254/PFA solution, at an initial PFA concentration of 80 μM. These results suggest far-UVC activation of PFA solution as a dual-redox treatment platform, with the observed advantages maintained in the tested wastewater effluents.

works.title: Sulfur-Vacancy-Enabled Dual-Site MoS2 Enhances H* Utilization for Mo–H-Mediated Deep Dechlorination
works.abstract: Abstract Electrochemical dechlorination using molybdenum disulfide (MoS2) offers a cost-effective solution for treating chlorinated organic contaminants, yet its catalytic potential remains limited by the unclear roles of Mo and S sites in mediating hydrogen utilization and C–Cl bond cleavage. Herein, we engineer sulfur-vacancy-rich MoS2 (Sv-MoS2) electrodes to expose coordinatively unsaturated Mo sites and enable an efficient Mo–H*-mediated dechlorination pathway. Using florfenicol as a model chlorinated antibiotic, Sv-MoS2 achieved near-complete dechlorination with ∼15-fold faster kinetics than pristine MoS2, reaching a rate constant of 9.26 h–1 at low energy consumption (0.0083 kWh g–1). Mechanistic analyses combining CV, EPR, in situ Raman spectroscopy, kinetic isotope effects, and DFT calculations reveal a dual-site H* utilization mechanism: S sites primarily generate H*, while vacancy-exposed Mo sites stabilize Mo–H* species that selectively drive C–Cl bond cleavage. In contrast, pristine MoS2 follows a direct electron transfer-dominated pathway and shows limited deep dechlorination. The Mo–H*-mediated pathway on Sv-MoS2 substantially lowers the energy barriers for sequential C–Cl cleavage while promoting productive H* utilization over H2 formation. The Sv-MoS2 electrode further exhibits robust performance under variable pH, natural organic matter, coexisting anions, and repeated cycling. This work clarifies Mo/S site synergy in MoS2 electrocatalysts and establishes a dual-site design framework for efficient, selective, and sustainable electrochemical hydrodechlorination.

works.title: Technological Substitution in Pesticide Application Reduces Occupational Risk but Fails to Mitigate Dietary Residue Burden: Field Evidence from UAV versus Manual Spraying in Paddy Rice
works.abstract: Abstract UAV spraying has been widely promoted as superior to manual application in Asian rice production, yet its combined implications for food safety and occupational exposure have never been evaluated within a single integrated framework. Here, we report a full-season field trial comparing UAV and manual imidacloprid (IMI) application in paddy rice, simultaneously tracking grain residue dynamics and occupational exposure in 29 applicators through to harvest. Grain IMI concentrations at harvest were comparable between regimes (86−115 μg/kg) and exceeded the EU maximum residue limit (MRL, 10 μg/kg) in both groups. More critically, on an LC-HRMS-derived relative-concentration basis, parent IMI accounted for 30.4% of the detected IMI-related profile in grain, whereas transformation products collectively accounted for 69.6%. Among these, 6-hydroxynicotinic acid was the single highest-abundance compound, surpassing parent IMI itself, yet none of the detected transformation products are included in China’s residue definition for imidacloprid in plant-derived foods. Regarding occupational exposure, urinary IMI rose approximately 9-fold from pre-exposure baseline in UAV operators compared with 17-fold in manual applicators. Manual application also induced markedly greater lipid peroxidation stress, with median baseline-normalized MDA fold changes of approximately 3.8- and 2.6-fold in the manual and UAV groups, respectively (p = 0.001). These findings establish that application technology substitution effectively reduces occupational exposure risk but confers no advantage at the food safety end point. Current parent-compound-centered residue surveillance frameworks systematically underestimate the true IMI-related burden in harvested grain, and expansion of regulatory monitoring beyond the parent compound is warranted.

works.title: Emerging CRISPR Technologies for Environmental Protection: From Genetic Engineering and Biosensing to Environmental Deployment
works.abstract: Abstract Since its discovery, Clustered Regularly Interspaced Short Palindromic Repeats (CRISPR) has revolutionized biomedical science and engineering with its ability to recognize and edit gene sequences with high specificity and precision. Despite the growing interest in using these capabilities to address environmental and sustainability challenges, the broader potential of CRISPR in environmental systems remains unexplored relative to its biomedical applications. Here, we provide a critical perspective on the emerging use of CRISPR for pollution management, ecological conservation, and environmental monitoring. Rather than viewing CRISPR solely as a gene-editing or biosensing technology, we consider both capabilities together to examine how advances in CRISPR engineering can translate into practical environmental solutions. We highlight the fundamental principles behind CRISPR-based editing and sensing and evaluate the challenges that constrain their transition from proof-of-concept experiments to field deployment, including off-target effects, delivery methods, ecological risks, and low sensitivity. Addressing these hurdles requires a multifaceted approach that integrates emerging technologies such as reversible CRISPR technology, amplification and cascade reactions, and machine learning, with strict regulatory oversight and rigorous risk assessments. This perspective identifies critical strengths, weaknesses, and research priorities for advancing CRISPR from laboratory technology toward robust tools for environmental applications.

A conserved CusR-dependent regulatory pathway couples copper homeostasis with oxidative stress resistance in Klebsiella pneumoniae
works.abstract: ABSTRACT Host-derived copper toxicity is a central antimicrobial strategy that restricts bacterial survival during infection, yet how pathogens integrate copper detoxification with oxidative stress resistance remains incompletely understood. Here, we identify the response regulator CusR as a pivotal coordinator of copper homeostasis and oxidative stress defense in Klebsiella pneumoniae . Loss of cusR results in profound defects in copper tolerance, marked intracellular copper accumulation, and hypersensitivity to hydrogen peroxide, accompanied by elevated intracellular reactive oxygen species. Mechanistically, CusR directly activates the cusCFBA copper efflux operon through promoter binding, whereas regulation of the copA transporter occurs independently of CusR. Importantly, a conserved aspartate residue (D56) within CusR is essential for its activity; both plasmid-based and chromosomal substitution of this residue abolish copper efflux regulation, disrupt copper homeostasis, and exacerbate oxidative stress susceptibility. Comparative sequence analysis further demonstrates that this residue is highly conserved across diverse bacterial species, underscoring its evolutionary importance in copper-responsive signaling. Collectively, our findings reveal a conserved Asp-dependent CusR-CusCFBA regulatory axis that couples copper detoxification to oxidative stress resistance, enabling bacterial adaptation to host-imposed copper stress. IMPORTANCE Copper intoxication is an important host-mediated antimicrobial strategy that challenges bacterial pathogens during infection. Although copper resistance systems have been extensively studied, how bacteria coordinate copper detoxification with protection against oxidative stress remains poorly understood. In this study, we identify the response regulator CusR as a key factor linking copper homeostasis and oxidative stress resistance in Klebsiella pneumoniae . We demonstrate that CusR directly controls the cusCFBA copper efflux system through promoter binding and that a conserved aspartate residue is essential for this regulatory function. Loss of CusR disrupts copper balance, increases reactive oxygen species accumulation, and reduces bacterial resistance to oxidative stress. These findings reveal a conserved regulatory mechanism that integrates metal stress adaptation with oxidative stress defense, providing new insights into how bacterial pathogens survive under host-imposed environmental pressures.

works.title: Elevated ozone reshapes wheat root-associated microbiomes through coordinated plant responses and rhizosphere environmental filtering
works.abstract: ABSTRACT Elevated tropospheric ozone (O 3 ) threatens crop productivity, but how O 3 -induced changes in plant responses influence root-associated microbiomes remains unclear. We investigated the responses of microbial communities inhabiting the rhizosphere and root endosphere to elevated O 3 using four cultivars grown under ambient and 1.5-fold ambient O 3 in a field-based free-air O 3 -concentration enrichment (FACE) system. Plant traits, root-released organic carbon (ROC), rhizosphere properties, extracellular enzyme activities, and bacterial and fungal communities were jointly analyzed. Elevated O 3 reduced yield and root biomass, with cultivar-dependent changes in ROC. Elevated O 3 consistently increased rhizosphere pH and altered microbial resource allocation, increasing ecoenzymatic vector length by 4.1% and decreasing vector angle by 4.6%. Bacterial communities showed a stronger response than fungal taxonomic communities, particularly in the rhizosphere. However, variation partitioning indicated that soil properties, especially pH, rather than O 3 treatment alone, provided the strongest independent explanation for bacterial community variation. Fungal communities showed limited taxonomic turnover but exhibited shifts in predicted trophic guilds, including increased pathotroph- and saprotroph-associated groups and decreased symbiotroph-containing guilds under elevated O 3 . These results demonstrate that elevated O 3 reshapes the wheat root-associated microbiome through coordinated changes in plant performance, rhizosphere environmental filtering, and microbial functional strategies, highlighting the importance of plant-mediated processes in regulating belowground responses to atmospheric change. IMPORTANCE Elevated tropospheric O 3 is an increasing threat to crop production, but its effects on belowground microbial processes remain poorly understood. This study demonstrates that O 3 -induced root-associated microbiome changes are closely linked with altered plant carbon allocation and rhizosphere environmental conditions rather than O 3 exposure also. By integrating plant traits, soil properties, extracellular enzyme allocation, and microbial community analyses, we reveal a compartment-specific plant-soil-microbiome response to elevated O 3 . These findings improve our understanding of how atmospheric pollution may reshape crop-associated microbial functions and soil ecological processes under future climate change.

works.title: Hybrid genome assemblies of Bacteroidota isolates uncover mobile genetic elements, antimicrobial resistance genes, and novel antimicrobial peptides
works.abstract: ABSTRACT Members of the phylum Bacteroidota dominate the mammalian gut microbiota and represent promising candidates for next-generation probiotics. However, the resolution of complete Bacteroidota genomes is often hindered by extensive repetitive sequences and mobile genetic elements, a technical challenge further exacerbated by high intraspecies diversity and strain-level variants that drive assembly fragmentation and preclude the recovery of contiguous scaffolds. We recently isolated 18 strains that belonged to the Bacteroidales order of Bacteroidota from mouse ceca, human feces, and tortoise stool, which we now sequenced using both Illumina and Oxford Nanopore platforms. We developed a specialized assembly workflow to reconstruct high-resolution genomes and characterize their extrachromosomal landscapes. The hybrid pipeline yielded 2 fully closed, single-contig chromosomes, 10 almost closed genomes, and 6 draft assemblies. Genomic integrity was exceptionally high, with completeness scores ranging from 99.6% to 100% and contamination levels below 2%. A total of 12 circular plasmids were detected across 10 isolates; eight isolates harbored a single plasmid, while two isolates (241163E and 241171E) each carried two distinct circular plasmids. Seven of these plasmids were experimentally confirmed through isolation and sequencing, and five were classified as viral contigs. Functional annotation revealed a diverse repertoire of antimicrobial resistance genes and identified several predicted antimicrobial peptides in the assemblies through machine-learning analysis, of which two selected ones were experimentally verified. Overall, the resulting assemblies provide a reliable foundation for tracking mobile genetic elements, assessing resistance potential, and mining bioactive peptides in Bacteroidota species intended for therapeutic development. IMPORTANCE Bacteria in the phylum Bacteroidota are essential to mammalian gut health and are currently being developed as advanced probiotics. However, their complex DNA often prevents scientists from mapping their complete genetic blueprints, which can leave hidden traits like antibiotic resistance undetected. In this study, we combined two advanced DNA sequencing methods to create highly accurate and complete genetic maps for 18 Bacteroidota isolates from humans, mice, and tortoise. We successfully uncovered small, elusive DNA rings (potential plasmids) and confirmed their physical presence in the laboratory. Furthermore, we identified genes responsible for antibiotic resistance and used artificial intelligence to discover new antimicrobial peptides. This research provides a crucial foundation for the scientific community to accurately track mobile genes, rigorously evaluate the safety of potential gut therapeutics, and discover novel molecules for medical applications.

works.title: Widespread North American pollution and health impacts from early twentieth century copper production
Agricultural data source choice as a dominant control on nitrogen surplus uncertainty
works.abstract: Abstract Agricultural nitrogen (N) surplus (the residual of total N inputs after harvest removal, plant-tissue storage, runoff and atmospheric losses) is a leading cause of groundwater and other environmental contamination in intensive food-producing regions, yet N surplus estimates often depend on inconsistent fertilizer, harvest and manure datasets in an N balance. Using California’s Central Valley as a data-rich test case, we propagate expert, survey-based, regulatory and county-level datasets through a fixed crop-specific N surplus framework to generate 24 cases. Holding model structure and land use constant, we quantify the large divergence in estimated N surplus arising from data choice, especially for manure-treated field crops. The uncertainty about N surplus is consequential: it can reorder which crops, regions and pathways receive priority for groundwater protection. The resulting spread among N surplus outcomes is large enough to alter hotspot rankings, mitigation priorities and screening-level estimates of economic burden. Credible nitrogen assessment at farm to global scales therefore requires explicit propagation of agricultural data source uncertainty, which can materially affect resulting N surplus estimates. Absent specific local data, the uncertainty magnitudes reported here may guide N surplus uncertainty assessment in other regional, national and global analyses.

The limits of the water bankruptcy framing call for a water justice response
Projecting global deployment of interfacial solar evaporation
Co-hosting of Isotopic Water Species in Clathrate Hydrate Lattices: Implications for Isotopic Fractionation
works.abstract: Abstract Selective enrichment of deuterium oxide (D2O) from isotopic water mixtures remains challenging due to the nearly indistinguishable physicochemical properties of H2O and D2O. In this study, the feasibility of isotopic separation via hydrate crystallization was systematically evaluated using phase equilibrium measurements, in situ Raman spectroscopy, and high-pressure microdifferential scanning calorimetry. Phase equilibrium measurements of hydrates reformed from physically separated solid and liquid fractions of an equal-mass H2O/D2O mixture revealed no significant shift in phase boundaries relative to those of the initial mixture, indicating that the isotopic composition of the hydrate phase was governed primarily by the initial liquid composition rather than by the higher thermodynamic stability of D2O hydrates. Raman spectra exhibited merged vibrational features associated with HDO formation, without distinct spectral signatures corresponding to pure H2O- or D2O-based hydrates. In addition, calorimetric analysis revealed a single dissociation peak for the mixed systems, confirming the formation of a single hydrate phase rather than separate isotopic lattices. These findings demonstrate a fundamental limitation of thermodynamically driven hydrate crystallization for isotopic separation and highlight the necessity of developing alternative strategies, particularly those based on kinetic control, to suppress mixed lattice formation and enable effective isotopic fractionation.

Long-Term Exposure to PM2.5 Components and Respiratory Disease Mortality in South China: The Pearl River Cohort Study
works.abstract: Abstract Evidence on the effects of fine particulate matter (PM2.5) components on respiratory mortality remains limited, especially in large cohorts. Using data from 182,009 participants, we examined the single-component and joint associations of six major PM2.5 components (NH4+, NO3–, BC, OM, SO42–, and Cl–) with respiratory mortality. Marginal structural Cox models were used to estimate single-component effects, while quantile g-computation assessed mixture effects and component contributions. All six components were associated with increased respiratory mortality, with hazard ratios (HRs) ranging from 1.42 to 2.75. Each quartile increase in the mixture index was associated with a 29% higher hazard of respiratory disease mortality (HR = 1.29, 95%; CI = 1.23–1.34). NO3– contributed most strongly to the overall mixture association (weight = 0.48), followed by OM and Cl–. Older adults, nonsmokers, and nonexercisers showed greater susceptibility, with HRs ranging from 1.25 to 2.02. These findings highlight the importance of targeted air pollution control and protection of vulnerable populations.

works.title: Environmental Science & Technology Letters Presents the 2025 Excellence in Review Awards: Why?
Prenatal Per- and Polyfluoroalkyl Substances and Body Mass Index Trajectories in Childhood: Application of Multiphase Growth Mixture Models across the ECHO Cohort
works.abstract: Abstract We examined the associations of prenatal per- and polyfluoroalkyl substance (PFAS) exposures with body mass index (BMI) trajectories and growth parameters in the Environmental Influences on Child Health Outcomes Cohort. Maternal PFAS concentrations (perfluorohexanesulfonic acid [PFHxS], perfluorooctanesulfonic acid [PFOS], perfluorooctanoic acid [PFOA], perfluorononanoic acid [PFNA], perfluorodecanoic acid [PFDA], perfluoroundecanoic acid [PFUnDA], and N-methyl perfluorooctane sulfonamidoacetic acid [NMFOSAA]) were measured in serum or plasma during pregnancy. BMI trajectories and growth parameters were estimated using multiphase growth mixture modeling. Among 1,125 children ages 1–9.5 years, we identified a typical BMI trajectory (n = 998, 89%; reference group) and an atypical BMI trajectory characterized by early and rapid BMI increases (n = 127, 11%). Maternal PFOA (adjusted risk ratio [RR] = 1.22 per doubling; 95% CI = 1.05–1.41) and PFOS (adjusted RR = 1.14; 95% CI = 0.99–1.32) concentrations were associated with a higher risk of atypical trajectory membership. A doubling in maternal PFOA concentrations was associated with an earlier age at adiposity rebound by 19 (95% CI = 4–33) days. Other PFAS concentrations were not significantly associated with the atypical trajectory or adiposity rebound. In this pooled cohort study, higher prenatal exposure to certain PFAS was associated with a greater risk of an obesity-related growth trajectory and earlier adiposity rebound.

works.title: High-Throughput Fingerprinting of Polymer Biodegradation across Phylogenetically Diverse Microorganisms
works.abstract: Abstract With the growing accumulation of plastic waste, focus has been directed toward biodegradable polymers; however, understanding their performance across diverse microbial communities requires species-level degradation data, which throughput-limited studies of undefined or limited consortia have only partially provided, preventing the cross-species and cross-polymer comparisons driving mechanistic understanding. This work presents an integrative framework fingerprinting polymer biodegradation across phylogenetically diverse microorganisms. A modified high-throughput clear-zone assay was adapted to physiologically diverse species through minimal media formulations and used to characterize fragmentation across 19 microorganisms and 14 commercial polymers. Paucimonas lemoignei, Priestia megaterium, and Pseudomonas stutzeri showed expansive fragmentation capability. Poly(1,4-butylene adipate), degraded by 11 of 19 species, proved most universally degradable, while poly(butylene adipate-co-terephthalate), poly(ε-caprolactone), and poly(lactic acid) were degraded more selectively. Plate-based screening of protease, esterase, and urease activity supported the aliphatic-ester selectivity pattern. MicroResp quantification, addressing the often-conflated distinction between fragmentation and mineralization, confirmed mineralization in 63.3% (19 of 30) fragmentation-positive pairs. Comparative genomics identified 465 depolymerase homologues, 187 with predicted signal peptides. Distinct strategies─P. lemoignei’s four near-identical PhaZ paralogs versus P. stutzeri’s divergent broad-substrate α/β hydrolases─explain their comparable polyester breadth. Overall, this framework establishes a foundation for systematic accumulation of microbial biodegradation fingerprints.

works.title: Multiomics: TBPH Enhances Thyroid Hormone Synthesis via PIS-LPI-ERK-EGR1 Pathway
works.abstract: Abstract Bis(2-ethylhexyl)-tetrabromophthalate (TBPH), a high-production-volume novel brominated flame retardant (NBFR), has been shown to perturb thyroid hormone synthesis, yet the underlying molecular mechanism remains poorly understood. Using transcriptomics, phosphoproteomics, and metabolomics as discovery tools, combined with validation in Sprague–Dawley (SD) rats and human thyroid follicular epithelial cells (Nthy-ori 3–1), we investigated this mechanism. TBPH increased thyroglobulin (TG) and thyroid peroxidase (TPO) in rat thyroid and elevated circulating triiodothyronine (T3) and thyroxine (T4) levels. In Nthy-ori 3–1 cells, TBPH remodeled glycerophospholipid metabolism, leading to phosphatidylinositol synthase (PIS)-dependent accumulation of the signaling lipid lysophosphatidylinositol 18:1 (LPI_18:1). LPI 18:1 selectively activated the ERK-EGR1 signaling axis and drove TG/TPO upregulation. Knockdown of PIS or EGR1, or pharmacological inhibition of ERK, abolished TBPH-induced TG/TPO expression. These findings reveal a previously unrecognized PIS-LPI-ERK-EGR1 pathway through which TBPH enhances thyroid hormone synthesis, highlighting a lipid metabolism-driven mechanism of endocrine disruption and providing a mechanistic basis for reassessing the health risks of NBFRs.

works.title: Electrochemical Recycling of Spent Lithium-Ion Battery Cathodes: Direct Regeneration, Electrochemical Leaching, and Selective Separation
works.abstract: Abstract Growing volumes of spent lithium-ion batteries challenge waste management and resource security. Conventional recycling recovers metals but often consumes energy and chemicals while sacrificing cathode structural value. Electrochemical methods enable cathode repair, controlled dissolution, and selective recovery, yet their suitability for diverse feeds and product requirements remains unclear. This Critical Review develops a material-state- and product-oriented framework linking cathode degradation, electrochemical transformations, and product specifications. Relithiation, defect repair, and cell-level rejuvenation are evaluated as regeneration strategies, with functional repurposing considered separately. Electrochemical leaching is classified by direct or indirect redox transfer, while paired or coupled operation is treated as reactor-level integration. Electrodialysis, electrosorption, and electrodeposition are assessed for ion redistribution, selective capture, concentration, and product formation. Because extraction efficiency alone cannot establish successful recycling, we emphasize feedstock tolerance, selectivity, Faradaic and ion-transport efficiencies, energy and reagent consumption, component durability, and qualified-product yield within defined system boundaries. Future priorities include diagnosis-guided routing, realistic black-mass validation, standardized reporting, scalable reactors, and integrated techno-economic and life-cycle assessment. Electrochemical technologies can complement established recycling through feedstock-adaptive pathways that retain, recover, or upgrade cathode value.

works.title: Harvesting Corrosion Energy for Self-Powered Gravity-Driven Membrane Filtration and Fouling Regulation
works.abstract: Abstract Decentralized water treatment requires low-cost technologies that can remove dissolved metal ions while maintaining stable water production without external energy input. Here, we developed a soil-mediated corrosion-current hydrogel filtration system (SCHFs) that integrates a conductive adsorptive hydrogel membrane with a soil-based corrosion-energy-harvesting unit. Natural soil served as the solid electrolyte, while discarded Al and carbon cloth enabled direct harvesting of corrosion energy for conductive-membrane regulation during gravity-driven filtration. In 60-day continuous river water filtration, the SCHFs permeate concentrations of Cu2+ and Mn2+ approaching the detection limit under the tested conditions. In addition, SCHFs also accelerated NH4+-N stabilization and reduced the final permeate concentration to 0.2 mg L–1. Moreover, a thicker but more porous surface cake layer was formed during SCHF operation, limiting pore blockage and reducing the 60-day flux decline. Microbial community analysis further indicated that SCHFs reshaped the membrane biofilm and enriched taxa associated with nitrogen transformation. Soil and electrode analyses suggested that Al released from the sacrificial electrode was partly immobilized as aluminum-containing silicate minerals, suggesting a low secondary environmental risk under controlled Al input. These results suggest that coupling soil-mediated microcurrent in SCHFs regulate interfacial transport and fouling-layer architecture, thereby improving dissolved-metal retention and long-term hydraulic stability.

works.title: Modulation of the general stress response impacts protein expression, energy economy, and heterogeneity in virtually non-dividing yeast cultures
works.abstract: ABSTRACT Microbial cells adapt their physiology when growth is restricted by nutrient limitation, balancing survival with the capacity to produce proteins. Here, we investigated this adaptation in Saccharomyces cerevisiae by comparing retentostat cultures, in which specific growth rates reached below 0.001 h⁻¹, of a reference strain (ScNTi001) and a ∆ msn2 ∆ msn4 mutant (ScNTm001). We show that general stress-response transcription factors Msn2 and Msn4 are crucial for maintaining energy efficiency and for survival under this extreme calorie restriction. Their absence increased population heterogeneity and reduced viability, underscoring a role beyond merely stress resistance. To understand (heterologous) protein expression dynamics, we monitored how a stress-inducible promoter (P HSP12 ) and a constitutive promoter (P TEF1 ) impacted protein levels. The P HSP12 remained active at moderate to low growth rates, but expression sharply dropped below 0.001 h⁻¹, whereas the P TEF1 sustained protein expression, with activity linked to specific glucose uptake rates rather than growth rate. This decoupling revealed a trade-off: although P TEF1 -driven ymNeongreen-specific production rates were 70% higher in the absence of ∆ msn2 ∆ msn4 , overall product yields were 13% lower. IMPORTANCE This study demonstrates how Msn2 and Msn4 govern cellular robustness under extreme nutrient-limited conditions at near-zero growth rates. It also guides promoter selection strategies for growth-independent production processes. More broadly, this study shows that retentostats can be used as a valuable tool to dissect stress-response pathways, survival mechanisms, and growth-independent expression systems in microbial cell factories.

works.title: Micro-electric field enhanced biodegradation of refractory organics for strengthening industrial wastewater treatment: microbial electron flow, interspecies interactions, and scale-up
Physiological and ecological drivers of antibiotic resistance selection in microbial communities
Characteristic metabolite emergence and coordinated multi-omics reprogramming in a four-member synthetic Streptomyces consortium during rice straw deconstruction
Dark CO2 fixation via the ethylmalonyl-CoA pathway establishes metabolic parity: A stoichiometric basis for compounding ecosystem shifts
works.abstract: A central challenge in microbial ecology, particularly in engineered systems, is understanding how competing guilds coexist and why communities deviate from expected stability. Whereas polyphosphate accumulation provides energy and redox buffering in many heterotrophs, how lineages lacking polyphosphate synthesis manage equivalent redox imbalances remains an overlooked question. Using an enhanced biological phosphorus removal system, we integrated quantitative stoichiometry with metaproteomics to resolve alternative metabolic strategies that underpin cellular homeostasis in heterotrophs. We show that glycogen-accumulating organisms (Ca. Competibacter GAO) achieve stoichiometric yield parity with polyphosphate-accumulating organisms (Ca. Dechloromonas PAO) through a parallel redox-buffering mechanism: heterotrophic CO2/HCO3- assimilation via the ethylmalonyl-CoA pathway. This CO2/HCO3- fixation couples structural carbon conservation with tight redox control, mitigating intracellular electron overflow and eliminating the long-assumed GAO bioenergetic inferiority. The energetic efficiency of GAOs is further fortified by fine-tuned metabolic wiring, featuring energy-efficient high-affinity acetate activation, ferredoxin-mediated biochemistry, and ATP-neutral polyhydroxyalkanoate (PHA) mobilization. Metabolic parity is established between the two guilds growing on acetate, yet minor formate co-feeding tilts the delicate PAO-GAO balance. Formate supplementation creates an asymmetric bioenergetic niche that grants per-cycle energy gains primarily to GAOs. Decoupled from hydraulic throughput, solids retention time control retains cells carrying accumulated intracellular inventory, translating per-cycle energetic edges into a multi-generational ratchet that drives a community shift from PAO-GAO co-dominance to GAO dominance. By exposing limitations of traditional single-substrate and single-cycle steady-state models, our findings reveal how inorganic resource management and generational metabolic compounding shape community assembly in biomass-retaining microbial ecosystems.

works.title: Free-living autotrophs drive a carbon fixation peak within the Orca Basin chemocline while heterotrophs dominate total activity from seawater to brine
works.abstract: Deep hypersaline anoxic basins (DHABs) are stratified, polyextreme environments found within enclosed and semi-enclosed seas worldwide. Here, we quantified microbial activity in Orca Basin, the largest known DHAB, to investigate carbon cycling across its steep chemical and salinity gradients. We measured total anabolic activity and dissolved inorganic carbon (DIC) fixation as a function of metabolic lifestyle (autotroph or heterotroph) and spatial niche (free-living or particle-associated) using dual-isotope labeling experiments and single-cell analysis by nanoscale secondary ion mass spectrometry (nanoSIMS). Activity was detected within all ten depths investigated from seawater to hypersaline brine, including by most cells within the brine. DIC fixation and total anabolic activity peaked within the oxic-anoxic interface, notably separate from the peak in cell and particle density deeper in the halocline. Autotrophs drove the peak in DIC fixation, but heterotrophs drove that of total activity; autotrophs were more abundant than heterotrophs at this depth but on average smaller and slower growing. Particle-associated heterotrophs, but not autotrophs, were significantly more active than their free-living counterparts within the interface. Heterotrophic communities derived an average of 4% to 10% of their biomass from DIC across the vertical transect, contributing just 2% of total DIC fixation within the peak but the majority within overlying seawater. Metagenomic analysis of catabolically active, sorted cells indicated members of at least five phyla were active within the oxic-anoxic interface, including putatively autotrophic Thermoproteota. These data provide high-sensitivity microbial activity measurements in Orca Basin and highlight the widespread viability of the resident microbiome.

works.title: Temperature effects on life history strategies for rapid growth potential of leaf epiphytic bacteria
works.abstract: Phyllosphere bacteria, occupying both epiphytic and endophytic habitats, constitute a critical plant-atmosphere interface. However, their community assembly and life-history strategies (LHSs) in response to temperature increase remain poorly understood. Here, we compared leaf phyllosphere bacterial communities with those in other plant compartments across four representative plant species from an alpine meadow on the Qinghai-Tibet Plateau. By combining observations along an elevational gradient with a controlled warming experiment, we found that temperature was closely associated with the deterministic assembly of leaf phyllosphere bacterial communities. Elevated temperature corresponded to shifts in taxonomic composition, diversity, assembly process, cross-compartment bacterial source, and co-occurrence network. Furthermore, elevated temperature was associated with a shift toward r-strategists in leaf phyllosphere bacterial LHSs, evidenced by higher ribosomal RNA operon (rrn) copy numbers for rapid growth potential and corroborated by genome assemblies of four warming-responsive epiphytic isolates and metagenomic sequencing. Based on 880 public 16S rRNA gene datasets from 45 locations on six continents, we identified a global increase in the rrn copy number in leaf epiphytic bacterial communities across diverse plant species, which was associated with elevated temperatures and enhanced diurnal fluctuation. Finally, we proposed a concept of four LHSs (growth, stress tolerance, competition, and resource acquisition) based on functional inference from 16S rRNA data, supported by the assembled epiphytic bacterial genomes and metagenomes. Collectively, our findings established a trait-based framework for understanding responses of leaf phyllosphere bacteria to future warming.

Ecological commissioning links microbial succession to treatment stabilization during managed aquifer recharge
works.abstract: Managed aquifer recharge (MAR) systems require ecological as well as hydraulic commissioning, yet when attached microbial communities become spatially organized and associated with stable treatment remains unresolved. We operated duplicate 10 m sand-column trains supplied with River Lek water for 12 months and tracked water quality and bacterial communities monthly at 1, 5, and 10 m and in the effluent. Removal trajectories for dissolved organic carbon, Fe²⁺, Mn²⁺, NH₄⁺, and NO₂⁻ and bacterial diversity showed little sustained directional change after approximately 5 months, while distance-associated communities became evident after month 6. At month 12, ASVs shared with 10 m sand accounted for 69.7% of effluent sequence abundance. Only 11.6% of shared influent-sand sequence abundance was consistent with neutral expectations, whereas sand-to-effluent neutral-model fit increased to R² = 0.60. We define this coordinated transition as ecological commissioning: a months-long process in which environmental selection organizes attached communities, spatial zones emerge, and terminal-zone dispersal increasingly shapes produced-water microbiology. Although timing is system specific, this framework identifies start-up and terminal aquifer zones as targets for MAR treatment verification and biological water-quality management.

works.title: Revealing fermentation pathway of methane-to-organic acid bioconversion by aerobic methanotrophs
works.abstract: Bioconversion of methane to value-added liquid chemicals is a sustainable strategy to alleviate reliance on crude oil. Here, this study uncovers an efficient pathway for converting methane into organic acids, including acetic and formic acids, through aerobic methanotrophs. Under nitrogen-limiting conditions, methane is assimilated into intracellular storage compounds (glycogen or polyhydroxybutyrate), which are subsequently fermented into organic acids under oxygen-limiting conditions. This two-stage process is conserved across both Type I ( Methylococcus capsulatus Bath, 8326 μmol organic acids/g dry cell weight (DCW)) and Type II ( Methylosinus sp . LW4, 946 μmol organic acids/g DCW) methanotrophs in batch culture. Using 13 C-labelling and proteomics, carbon flux and functional genes were confirmed in this pathway, while transmission electron microscopy visualized the accumulation and consumption of intracellular storage compounds. By using the proven efficient fermentation pathway, this study further applied M. capsulatus Bath in both semi-continuous and continuous bio-fermenters and demonstrated sustained methane-to-organic acid conversion over 90 days. These findings unveil a likely universal fermentation strategy among aerobic methanotrophs, which can serve as a new platform for sustainable biological production of organic acids from methane feedstocks

works.title: Unraveling the relationship between population composition and metabolite induction in high-precision cellulosic bacterial–fungal co-cultivations
works.abstract: ABSTRACT Co-cultures of filamentous microorganisms are a tool to unlock the biosynthetic machinery encoded in silent gene clusters. However, if bioactive compounds are to be produced biotechnologically, it is essential to understand the dynamics of microbial partnership. In this context, we have previously introduced a co-cultivation platform based on low-cost crystalline cellulose as a substrate. Here, the fungus Trichoderma reesei RUT-C30 degrades α-cellulose into soluble sugars to support the growth of the natural product-producing bacterium Streptomyces coelicolor A3(2), which is unable to utilize cellulose. This co-cultivation approach mimics a carbon-limited interaction scenario of natural habitats. We investigated how the population dynamics of both strains affect metabolite production by combining high-throughput online fluorescence monitoring with high-resolution liquid chromatography–tandem mass spectrometry (LC-MS/MS)-based metabolomics. We then determined the metabolic profile of the cultures and identified metabolites specifically induced during co-cultivation. The coupled analysis of population ratios and metabolomic data indicated that the highest number of induced metabolites compared to axenic cultures is observed in co-cultures with a balanced ratio of both strains. This analysis further led to deciphering a biotransformation of dimerumic acid, a hydroxamate siderophore produced by T. reesei , into the dehydroxylated derivatives eleutherazine B and talarazine A by S. coelicolor . Additionally, a small cluster of unique metabolites strongly induced in co-cultures was found to be structurally similar to steroidal lactones of the withanolide class, thus highlighting the potential for the discovery of natural products. Overall, the platform described combines natural product prospecting with a biotechnological production strategy that can be extended also to other co-cultures. IMPORTANCE This work provides a comprehensive analysis of population dynamics and metabolite production in a complex microbial co-culture. This approach integrates three key aspects. First, high-throughput online monitoring enables biomass tracking through fluorescence labeling in a system containing two filamentous microorganisms with distinct macro- and micromorphologies and a non-soluble fibrous substrate. Second, concomitant metabolomics analysis during co-cultivation settings helps to resolve metabolic interaction patterns. Interestingly, a metal-acquisition compound produced by the first microbe is chemically modified by the second, suggesting a competition strategy for an essential micronutrient. Third, from a biotechnological perspective, substrate solubilization resembles a fed-batch strategy that minimizes carbon catabolite repression during secondary metabolite production. Overall, this platform advances our understanding of microbial interactions and culture conditions that can be transferred to other culture platforms of relevance in bioprocess intensification.

works.title: Hydrogen production and fermentation in heliobacteria
works.abstract: ABSTRACT Heliobacteria are the only phototrophic members of the gram-positive bacteria. Heliomicrobium modesticaldum can grow chemotrophically in the dark using pyruvate as a carbon source. It can grow phototrophically only on acetate (plus CO 2 ). We found that dihydrogen production occurred only when fixing N 2 and increased ~5-fold upon replacing N 2 with argon. Introduction of genes encoding a [FeFe] hydrogenase and maturases ( hydAEFG ) from Acetivibrio thermocellus conferred the ability to produce H 2 at much higher levels. The modified cells made the most H 2 when grown chemotrophically, less when grown mixotrophically, and none when grown phototrophically, suggesting that only excess electrons were available for H 2 production. We tested several molecules as potential reduced fermentation products by this species. Only propanoate was observed, and its extracellular concentration could reach several millimolar. There was an inverse correlation between light intensity and propanoate production when the cells were grown on pyruvate, and phototrophic cultures produced no detectable propanoate. We conclude that propanoate is the major reduced fermentation product made by Hmb. modesticaldum, and we propose a pathway to produce it that is essentially a mini-cycle within the reductive TCA (rTCA) cycle, combining the first four reactions of the rTCA cycle with methylmalonyl-CoA mutase and epimerase, and methylmalonyl-CoA:pyruvate carboxytransferase. This pathway would, in effect, dispose of four reducing equivalents while driving the conversion of pyruvate to propanoate. The genes for the last six enzymes of this pathway seem to be part of an operon; the genes and potential operon are conserved in other heliobacteria, suggesting that this pathway exists in all or most heliobacteria. IMPORTANCE This study establishes that heliobacteria, the only phototrophic members of the Bacillota , produce propanoic acid as the reduced fermentation product when growing chemotrophically. The pathway used to make it resembles that of the Propionibacteria , except in the context of a mini-cycle within the reductive TCA (rTCA) cycle. This work confirms that the Heliomicrobium genus lacks a functional hydrogenase to make hydrogen as a way to dispose of excess electrons. Finally, it is shown that these organisms can be engineered to make dihydrogen as a reduced fermentation product if the genes for a clostridial hydrogenase and assembly proteins are expressed in Heliomicrobium modesticaldum .

A high-rate anaerobic/oxic membrane bioreactor for phosphorus removal and carbon capture from municipal wastewater: Operational limits and energy-recovery potential via sidestream anaerobic digestion
works.abstract: Integrating enhanced biological phosphorus removal (EBPR) with high-rate activated sludge treatment is an attractive strategy for achieving simultaneous phosphorus removal and carbon recovery; however, its stability at short sludge retention times (SRT) under low hydraulic retention time (HRT) conditions remains poorly understood. In this study, a continuous anaerobic/oxic membrane bioreactor (A/O-MBR) was operated to treat real municipal wastewater under systematically varied SRT and HRT to determine the lower EBPR operational limits under carbon capture-oriented conditions. The membrane configuration reduced settling-related biomass loss, allowing the evaluation of EBPR performance under controlled sludge-age conditions. Stable EBPR was maintained at or above a practical lower SRT threshold of approximately 2 d, achieving effluent phosphate concentrations <0.5 mg P L -1 , even at a total HRT of 2.5 h. Reducing the SRT to <2 d resulted in a marked decline in phosphorus removal. Batch tests revealed suppressed anaerobic phosphate release and aerobic phosphate uptake at SRTs below 2 d, indicating weakened EBPR-related functional activity. Microbial community analysis showed clear shifts in the dominant taxa across operating conditions. At an SRT of 2 d, approximately 66% of the influent chemical oxygen demand (COD) was redirected to the sludge phase while limiting mineralization, thereby preserving methane recovery potential. A preliminary energy balance based on COD partitioning and biochemical methane potential projected that anaerobic digestion of the captured organics could offset a substantial portion of the system’s energy demand. These findings clarify the operational limits of short-SRT EBPR and demonstrate its potential for simultaneous carbon–phosphorus resource management.

The attachment rate of Vibrio anguillarum to microplastics strongly varies with strain identity, particle characteristics, and environmental conditions
works.abstract: ABSTRACT Microplastics (MPs), resulting from plastic objects and waste degradation, are increasingly abundant, particularly in marine environments. They exhibit a hydrophobic surface on which biofilms form easily. Metagenomic analyses of these biofilms have revealed that they often contain bacterial species potentially pathogenic to humans or animals. For this reason, MPs are suspected to present a risk to public health by acting as a vector for pathogenic bacterial species. To better understand this hazard, we studied different factors potentially affecting the bacterial attachment rate to MPs. Focusing on the fish pathogen Vibrio anguillarum , a collection of 16 GFP-labeled strains was assembled, including isolates from infected fish. Their attachment rates were measured using fluorescence microscopy on three types of MPs (milled polypropylene and polyethylene terephthalate particles, and commercially available polystyrene beads). A strong effect of the particle type was found, with higher attachment rates on milled particles, whose surface appeared qualitatively rougher based on visual examination of scanning electron microscopy images. Our results also revealed an intraspecific variation in attachment rate, highlighting the need for testing several strains of the same species to assess attachment rate and related hazards. Finally, it was observed that when a biofilm had formed by field incubation of the MPs, the differences in attachment rates between particle types were erased. The attachment of V. anguillarum depends on a combination of strain-related factors, particle characteristics, and environmental conditions, highlighting the need to combine microbiology, materials science, and environmental sciences to achieve a comprehensive risk assessment associated with MPs. IMPORTANCE Microplastics (MPs) are increasingly abundant, particularly in marine environments. They are suspected to present a risk to public health by acting as a vector for pathogenic bacterial species. Focusing on the fish pathogen Vibrio anguillarum , we measured the attachment rates of 16 strains on three types of microplastics (milled polypropylene and polyethylene terephthalate particles, and commercially available polystyrene beads). This study highlights a strong effect of the particle type, with higher attachment rates on irregular particles, as well as a strong intraspecific variation. In a second experiment, it was observed that when a natural marine biofilm had already formed on the microplastic particles, differences in attachment rates between particle types were erased. Our findings emphasize the importance of accounting for multiple factors when assessing the risks of MPs as carriers of pathogenic bacteria, with our study addressing the first step of the conceptual pathway linking attachment, persistence, transport, exposure, and ultimately infection.

works.title: An integrated cell culture–nanopore sequencing (ICC-NanoporeSeq) method for the simultaneous detection of multiple enterovirus types and quantification of infectious Enterovirus B
works.abstract: Enteroviruses (EVs) are ubiquitous contaminants of surface waters, where they can remain infectious for long periods of time. Most methods used for EV monitoring are unable to distinguish between infectious and non-infectious particles, or between EV types. Because different types exhibit both distinct environmental persistence and health implications, there is a need for type-resolved infectivity measurements. Here, we developed integrated cell culture-nanopore sequencing (ICC-NanoporeSeq), a method combining short-term cell culture amplification with nanopore sequencing of the VP1 gene. The ICC approach was adapted from a previously described ICC-reverse transcriptase quantitative PCR (ICC-RTqPCR) protocol, while the NanoporeSeq workflow was derived from a clinical EV typing protocol and optimized for environmentally circulating EV types. Using samples containing known concentrations of 10 EV types, the NanoporeSeq method accurately and reproducibly recovered the original proportions of all EV types after correction of biases. When applied to wastewater extracts, the method detected 45 EV types across five species. Furthermore, type-specific calibration curves generated with ICC-NanoporeSeq enabled quantification of the infectious concentrations of six EV types of the Enterovirus B species, allowing a simultaneous and type-resolved assessment of infectivity in mixed samples. Overall, ICC-NanoporeSeq provides a scalable approach for the parallel analysis of multiple EV types. Compared with the predecessor ICC-RTqPCR method, it eliminates the need for multiple type-specific PCR primers, and can therefore be readily expanded to include additional EV types.IMPORTANCECurrent methods used to detect enteroviruses (EVs) in environmental samples generally measure viral genome copies without determining whether viruses remain infectious, limiting their use in public health risk assessment or water quality monitoring. At the same time, available infectivity assays are often labor-intensive and cannot distinguish between different EV types. Here, we developed integrated cell culture-nanopore sequencing (ICC-NanoporeSeq), a method combining cell culture and nanopore sequencing to simultaneously quantify the infectious concentrations of multiple EV types in samples containing mixed EV populations. The method provides an efficient and scalable approach for studying EVs in complex environmental matrices. ICC-NanoporeSeq has potential applications in wastewater-based epidemiology, environmental surveillance, and disinfection studies, where understanding the persistence of different EV types simultaneously is crucial.

works.title: Cultivation of halophilic archaea in shallow subsurface Martian conditions has implications for extant life on Mars
works.abstract: ABSTRACT The present-day Martian surface is generally considered inhospitable to life because of low atmospheric pressure, intense surface radiation, global desiccation, and oxidizing chemistry, which has been increasing since the late Noachian. However, shallow Martian subsurface regions where mineralogy has shown groundwater movement may include localized hypersaline environments capable of retaining liquid water and supporting microbial metabolism. Haloferax volcanii , a model halophilic archaeon, has previously been shown to survive under low-pressure Martian conditions (24 mbar) and to grow anaerobically supported by the Mars-relevant oxyanions nitrate and perchlorate under high-salinity conditions. Here, we investigated whether H. volcanii could actively grow under a combination of environmental and chemical conditions relevant to potentially habitable shallow subsurface Martian lacustrine settings. Cultures were incubated for 160 days under anoxic, CO₂-enriched, low-pressure conditions (24 mbar) in hypersaline liquid media supplemented with nitrate or perchlorate. Growth was observed in all low-pressure treatments and was confirmed by increases in optical density and biological reduction of nitrate and perchlorate. Scanning electron microscopy revealed extensive biofilm formation in low-pressure cultures, and Raman spectroscopy demonstrated the persistence of carotenoid biosignatures after prolonged incubation under Martian conditions. Liquid loss remained below 4% across all treatments, indicating long-term stability of hypersaline brines throughout the experiment. These results demonstrate for the first time that a halophilic archaeon is capable of active growth and metabolism under a Mars-relevant combination of low pressure, high salinity, anoxia, and oxidizing chemistry, providing experimental support for the potential habitability of localized shallow subsurface Martian environments. IMPORTANCE The search for cellular life is a major objective of future Mars exploration. While many studies have examined whether microorganisms can survive under Martian conditions, far fewer have demonstrated active growth and metabolism. Here, we document Haloferax volcanii as the first halophilic archaeon capable of active growth under a defined combination of Mars-relevant low atmospheric pressure, high salinity, anoxia, and oxidizing chemical conditions. These findings expand the current understanding of the environmental limits of microbial growth and provide experimental evidence that localized brine environments in the shallow Martian subsurface could support active microbial metabolism if suitable organics and liquid water are present. These results are also relevant to planetary protection efforts, as they help constrain the potential for terrestrial halophilic microorganisms introduced during robotic or human exploration to persist and remain metabolically active in Martian environments. Furthermore, this study establishes a practical framework for cultivating halophilic microorganisms under low-pressure Martian conditions and may help guide future efforts to detect, cultivate, and characterize potential extant life on Mars.

works.title: A switch-rheostat circuit governs quorum sensing homeostasis in a phytopathogen
works.abstract: ABSTRACT Pseudomonas fuscovaginae , a wide-host-range plant pathogen of several cereal and grass species, possesses two canonical N -acyl homoserine lactone (AHL)-based quorum sensing (QS) systems called PfsI/R and PfvI/R, both of which are inactive under laboratory conditions but active in planta . The pfsI-pfsR intergenic region encodes RsaM, a putative protein that has since been hypothesized to act as a repressor switch of this QS circuit. In the present study, we demonstrate that the stringent repression exerted on the PfsI/R system depends entirely on the divergent promoter/intergenic pfsR-rsaM region rather than RsaM itself. Remarkably, this regulatory switch element stringently represses the expression of both the pfsR and rsaM genes. We further show for the first time that RsaM is endogenously expressed and functions as a negative regulator, modulating the PfsI/R circuit instead of preventing its activation. Taken together, our results evidence a unique two-tiered/hierarchical repression of a QS system, provided by a master repressor switch and a repressor modulator. IMPORTANCE Pseudomonas fuscovaginae is a globally occurring plant pathogen that employs N -acyl homoserine lactone (AHL)-based quorum sensing (QS) to regulate virulence. In this bacterium, QS signaling circuits display a rather unusual feature: the lack of activation at high cell densities under standard laboratory conditions. A hypothetical regulator named RsaM was previously linked to this phenomenon as a repressor switch acting on the PfsI/R AHL QS system in the absence of an unknown signal or stimulus. In this study, we show that a regulatory element within the pfsR - rsaM intergenic region acts as the primary switch of the PfsI/R QS system, independently of RsaM. Conversely, RsaM functions as a post-activation modulator that fine-tunes the QS response. This study advances our understanding of the regulatory configurations of unconventional QS systems by revealing a two-tier control mechanism in which a master regulatory switch governs circuit activation, while the previously uncharacterized protein RsaM controls signaling output once the system is engaged.

works.title: Correction for Lubin et al., “Characterization of chemotaxis in soybean symbiont Bradyrhizobium diazoefficiens ”
Harnessing phage defense systems to develop a Burkholderia bacterial host
works.abstract: ABSTRACT Heterologous production of metabolites and proteins requires the transfer of foreign DNA into a host. One common barrier to the genetic engineering of bacteria is their plethora of phage defense systems. Targeted deletion of defense system components can improve DNA transfer for downstream applications. We sought to improve the transformation efficiency of Burkholderia sp. FERM BP-3421, a β-proteobacterial host that has great potential for the high-titer production of bioactive small molecules. We investigated restriction-modification systems and the recently described Kiwa phage defense system. Through deletion of three restriction enzyme genes, transformation efficiency was improved nearly 7-fold. The electroporation protocol was also optimized with respect to temperature, cell density, and buffer composition, which resulted in an additional 40-fold improvement in transformation efficiency, reaching 1 × 10 6 CFU/µg plasmid DNA. Interestingly, a mimicry by methylation approach, where DNA is pre-methylated using two host DNA methyltransferases, outperformed the transformation efficiency obtained with restriction enzyme deletion mutants nearly 3-fold. Moreover, contrary to previous reports in Escherichia coli , deletion of the Kiwa system did not improve transformation efficiency into Burkholderia sp. FERM BP-3421. Understanding the impact of bacterial innate immune systems on genetic tractability is vital to improving non-model host strains to produce high-value molecules of interest. IMPORTANCE The ability to transfer DNA into bacteria is key to genetic engineering. However, bacteria have evolved immune defenses to recognize and protect themselves from foreign DNA, thwarting genetic manipulation. Here, we identified putative defense systems in a β-proteobacterial strain of interest and characterized their impact on DNA transfer. The defense systems studied belong to the well-known class of restriction-modification systems and to the recently described Kiwa system. Intriguingly, we observed higher DNA transfer efficiency by avoiding restriction-modification systems via pre-methylation rather than by restriction gene deletion. Future studies should investigate the underlying mechanism for this difference. Moreover, contrary to what was reported for γ-proteobacteria Escherichia coli , we showed that the Kiwa system does not impair DNA transfer into the β-proteobacteria Burkholderia sp. strain. There has been significant interest in the discovery of novel defense systems. Learning more about their complexity is important to enable genetic manipulation of previously intractable strains.

works.title: Novel electron transport powers archaeal methane metabolism across varied substrates and environments
works.abstract: ABSTRACT Methanogens are responsible for producing approximately one billion metric tons of methane each year within Earth’s anaerobic environments as a byproduct of their energy metabolism. They play a vital role in the global carbon cycle. There are three main pathways for methanogenesis: hydrogenotrophic, which uses H 2 and CO 2 to produce methane; methylotrophic, which utilizes methylated compounds like methanol and amines; and aceticlastic, which converts acetate into methane and CO 2 . Instead of substrate-level ATP production, methanogens conserve energy through a membrane-bound electron transport chain and flavin-based electron bifurcation (FBEB). Beyond the canonical modes of growth in methanogens, Methanosarcina acetivorans , a model acetotrophic methanogen, can conserve energy via direct interspecies electron transfer (DIET). Here, we review the metabolic pathways and electron transport processes involved in energy conservation during fermentative, respiratory, and DIET modes. Additionally, we discuss the role of FBEB in energy conservation in gut-associated Methanomassiliicoccus luminyensis . Finally, we discuss the potential roles of heterodisulfide reductase (Hdr) and the process of electron transfer during the reaction mechanism of electron-bifurcating HdrA2B2C2 complex in cytochrome-containing methanogens. Understanding the complex redox control mechanisms in these organisms has broader implications for sustainable energy and environmental management.

works.title: Sustainable 2-keto-L-gulonic acid biosynthesis via single-strain one-step fermentation
works.abstract: ABSTRACT L-ascorbic acid (vitamin C) is an essential antioxidant molecule that maintains normal physiological functions in humans. Currently, industrial production relies primarily on a three-strain, two-step fermentation process to produce 2-keto-L-gulonic acid (2-KLG), the direct precursor of vitamin C. 2-KLG is then converted to vitamin C through chemical lactonization. However, this process is limited by prolonged fermentation cycles, poor stability of the mixed-culture system, and complex process control. In recent years, engineered single-strain platforms capable of one-step 2-KLG biosynthesis have emerged as a promising strategy for more sustainable vitamin C production. Nevertheless, the efficiency of L-sorbose-to-2-KLG conversion in this system remains low, making it a major bottleneck to further improving 2-KLG production. This review summarizes recent advances on single-strain, one-step fermentation systems using Gluconobacter oxydans as the chassis strain. It focuses on strategies including genetic tool development, metabolic engineering, and key enzyme optimization. The review aims to provide a theoretical basis and technical reference for optimizing and industrializing green biomanufacturing systems for vitamin C.

works.title: A hybrid nature-based ecological restoration system stabilizes water quality and food-web recovery in a continuous nutrient-loaded pond
Spectral–temporal autofluorescence analysis for rapid and label-free microplastic differentiation in aquatic environments
works.abstract: Although plastic products facilitate our life essentially, the resulting pollution increasingly harms the terrestrial and aquatic environment and our health. To mitigate this pollution and to establish effective recycling strategies, analytical methods to specifically detect different plastics are required. However, common analytical methods such as Raman, near-infrared (NIR), and Fourier transform infrared (FTIR) spectroscopy are constrained by their complex instrumentation, their signal absorption in water and/or their low signal intensities, resulting in long measurement times. In this work, we demonstrate an analytical method to overcome these limitations and detect different plastic materials based on their intrinsic autofluorescence. We investigated 22 different plastic materials and identified characteristic fingerprints in their spectral and temporal autofluorescence using a phasor-based analysis. With the spectral and temporal autofluorescence, we could identify different plastic materials with an accuracy of up to 87.9% and 83.1%, respectively. The accuracy can even be improved to 95.7%, when combining the analysis of individually measured spectral and temporal autofluorescence signals. These results showcase that using spectral and temporal autofluorescence signals is a viable approach for plastic detection and differentiation, particularly when combining spectral and temporal dimensions. The, here, demonstrated analytical method comprises the advantage of high signal intensities, working in the spectral water window and needing no labels. Consequently, it can be implemented into high-throughput methods for microplastic detection in liquid sample analysis such as flow cytometric, as demonstrated in this work. This has huge potential for environmental in-field monitoring which would support the effective mitigation of plastic pollution.

Dual limit determination for recirculation control against inhibition and sludge washout in anammox expanded granular sludge bed reactor
works.abstract: Recirculation simultaneously alleviates substrate inhibition through dilution and intensifies sludge washout through increased upflow velocity, yet these opposing effects are rarely quantified as explicit limits for recirculation control. A dual limit approach was established for an anammox expanded granular sludge bed (EGSB) reactor treating partial-nitrification-pretreated food-waste anaerobic digestion dewatering liquor, with lower and upper recirculation limits defined by inhibition control and functional granule retention, respectively. During 360 d of operation, the nitrogen loading rate increased from 2 to 6 g N L −1 d −1 , while nitrogen removal efficiency remained generally within 84 to 90%. Apparent inhibition responses of free ammonia, free nitrous acid and nitrite were described using the Levenspiel model, yielding IC 10 app values of 43 mg NH 3 N L −1 , 4 μg HNO 2 N L −1 and 1500 mg NO 2 – N L −1 , respectively. Free nitrous acid imposed the highest dilution demand and determined an inhibition constrained lower limit of R = 17. Granules were further separated by size to resolve their composition, activity and settling behavior. The 0.5–1 mm fraction combined the lowest settling velocity with the highest relative volumetric activity index, supporting its selection for hydraulic-retention design. An experimentally critical granule diameter of 0.5 mm was therefore defined, and its settling constraint produced a hydraulically constrained upper limit of R = 23. Coupling the inhibition constrained lower limit and hydraulically constrained upper limit yielded a reactor-specific feasible control window of 17 ≤ R ≤ 23, converting recirculation selection from an empirical setting into a dual limit decision against inhibition and sludge washout.

Monitoring single-cell metabolic phenotyping changes of Daqu microbiota during fermentation by Raman spectroscopy
works.abstract: ABSTRACT Monitoring microbial community dynamics during natural food fermentation is essential for stabilizing fermentation processes and improving product flavor profiles. This study employed single-cell Raman spectroscopy to monitor the metabolic change of Daqu microbiota during fermentation. First, we developed an operational phenotypic unit (OPU)-based clustering method to process Raman spectral data of a nine-member microbial community. The clustering was validated by sorting out representative single cells from different OPUs and performing 16S/ITS region sequencing. Second, single-cell Raman spectroscopy was applied to the mixed Daqu sample throughout fermentation, identifying 10 OPUs and 54 sub-OPUs. Single cells from different OPUs were sorted and sequenced to obtain taxonomic annotation, which were correlated with the Raman spectral characteristics of each OPU. The OPU-based Raman spectroscopy method was successfully used to monitor the single-cell metabolic phenotypes of Daqu microbiota during fermentation, and taxonomic annotations revealed the succession of microbial community structure. This study presents a novel approach for monitoring the dynamics of metabolic phenotypes within Daqu microbial communities, offering a data-driven decision-making approach for subsequent production operations in multi-species fermentation processes. IMPORTANCE Microbial communities play pivotal roles in diverse industrial processes, yet monitoring their metabolic dynamics remains challenging. Current omics approaches, including metagenomics, transcriptomics, and mass spectrometry-based metabolomics, fail to establish direct genotype-phenotype linkages at the single-cell level and often require destructive sampling. This study introduces operational phenotypic units (OPUs) as a novel framework to bridge this gap by integrating single-cell Raman spectroscopy with sequencing technologies. Our method enables non-destructive, rapid monitoring of metabolic phenotypes while preserving cells for downstream analysis. By applying this approach to solid-state Daqu fermentation, we demonstrate its capability to track microbial community succession and identify functionally distinct populations in real time. This data-driven strategy offers significant potential for optimizing multi-species fermentation processes across food, environmental, and biotechnological industries, providing a powerful tool for microbial community management and process control.

works.title: Antibiotic class shapes O-antigen-dependent phage outcomes in a clinical Pseudomonas aeruginosa isolate
works.abstract: ABSTRACT Pseudomonas aeruginosa is a high-priority opportunistic pathogen characterized by significant genetic plasticity and increasing multidrug resistance. Although phage–antibiotic combinations are increasingly explored to combat antimicrobial resistance, whether these interactions are synergistic or antagonistic and how different antibiotic classes influence phage replication and the subsequent development of resistance remain unclear. In this study, we examined combinations of the O-antigen-dependent phage phipa10 with amikacin (AMK), levofloxacin (LEV), or meropenem (MEM) against P. aeruginosa ZS-PA-35. At 24 h, the combinations showed antibiotic-dependent patterns of bacterial growth suppression. High concentrations of amikacin and meropenem reduced the extracellular yield of infectious phipa10. The highest tested levofloxacin concentration also reduced the recovered phage yield. Whole-genome sequencing of phage-resistant mutants showed that meropenem treatment drove large chromosomal deletions encompassing galU and hmgA , resulting in a characteristic brown pigmentation phenotype. LEV-selected isolates carried smaller deletions involving galU , whereas AMK-selected isolates shared a galU substitution. In a Galleria mellonella infection model, phipa10–antibiotic combinations improved host survival relative to either treatment alone, although the magnitude of the benefit varied across antibiotic classes. The meropenem combination yielded the highest observed survival proportion despite reduced phage yield in vitro . These results show that bacterial suppression, infectious phage yield, and resistance outcomes can diverge among the three tested antibiotic partners. IMPORTANCE Phage–antibiotic combinations may affect bacterial suppression, phage yield, and resistance-associated phenotypes differently. We compared three antibiotic partners in a single Pseudomonas aeruginosa –phage system. The observed growth, genetic, and larval survival outcomes varied across the tested treatments. Reduced phage yield did not preclude improved survival in the infection model. These observations support evaluating multiple outcomes when assessing a phage–antibiotic combination. Their broader relevance requires validation with additional isolates, phages, and antibiotics.
