Scaffold-level validation is needed for phage–host inference from metagenome-assembled genomes
works.abstract: Accurate phage-host prediction underpins ecological interpretation and experimental validation of uncultivated phages, yet most current approaches rely heavily on metagenome-assembled genomes (MAGs). This reliance implicitly assumes that MAG-level quality metrics, such as completeness and contamination, ensure scaffold-level correctness. Here, we demonstrate that this assumption can be violated under particular challenging conditions. Tetranucleotide frequency (TNF) analyses reveal that CRISPR-associated regions often diverge compositionally from their host genomes, increasing the risk of misbinning, while experimentally validated phage-host genome pairs show consistent TNF separation between phages and their hosts, challenging compositional binning assumptions. Through controlled simulations, we further show that the incorporation of substantial amounts of TNF-matched, non-host phage sequences into high-quality MAGs does not substantially alter standard completeness and contamination estimates, rendering such errors largely undetectable. Together, these results expose a systematic and underappreciated source of bias in MAG-based phage-host inference and highlight the need for explicit scaffold-level validation beyond conventional genome-quality metrics. We further propose a practical scaffold-level validation framework that integrates structural linkage and taxonomic consistency to improve the reliability of phage-host inference from MAGs.

works.title: Interaction mechanisms of core dominant fungi during fermentation of Massa Medicata Fermentata: volatile compounds of Saccharomycopsis fibuligera inhibit the growth of Rhizopus oryzae
works.abstract: ABSTRACT Massa Medicata Fermentata (MMF) is a traditional fermented medicine whose quality is governed by complex microbial interactions. This study investigated the antagonistic effect of the core yeast Saccharomycopsis fibuligera against the filamentous fungus Rhizopus oryzae and its underlying mechanisms. In vitro co-culture assays demonstrated that S. fibuligera suppressed R. oryzae growth and amylase activity in a cell-density-dependent manner, with significant inhibition observed at cell densities of ≥1 × 10⁷ cells·mL⁻¹. The antagonism was driven by two putative pathways: direct spatial/nutritional competition and indirect suppression mediated by yeast-secreted volatile organic compounds (VOCs). HS-SPME-GC-MS analysis identified six major VOCs, primarily fatty acid ethyl esters and 2-phenylethanol, with the latter being the most abundant (0.5664 ± 0.0422 µg·g⁻¹ medium). Single-compound antifungal assays confirmed that isoamyl acetate, ethyl hexanoate, and 2-phenylethanol completely inhibited the growth of R. oryzae at elevated doses. Mechanistic investigations via SEM, PI staining, and biochemical assays revealed that these VOCs induce cell death by disrupting mycelial morphology, compromising membrane integrity, inhibiting ergosterol biosynthesis, and triggering lipid peroxidation. These findings elucidate a key antagonistic interaction between core functional fungi during MMF fermentation, providing a theoretical basis for targeted fermentation regulation and industrial standardization of this traditional herbal medicine. IMPORTANCE By revealing the cell-density-dependent dual-mode antagonism between S. fibuligera and R. oryzae , this study deepens our understanding of microbial interactions in traditional fermentation. The discovery of specific inhibitory VOCs and their membrane-disrupting mechanisms provides a theoretical basis for targeted process regulation. These insights are crucial for achieving precise fermentation control, which is essential for improving product consistency, reducing batch-to-batch variability, and advancing the traditional fermentation standardization of herbal medicines.

FOG Deposit Accumulation in a Pipe-Loop System: Influences of Wet Wipes, Facial Tissues and Food Debris on Rheology and Flow Behaviour
works.abstract: Fat, oil and grease (FOG) accumulation is a major cause of sewer blockages worldwide, yet the mechanisms governing deposit formation and their hydraulic impacts remain poorly understood under realistic flow conditions. This study introduces a laboratory-scale semi-continuous pipe-loop system that replicates sewer hydraulic conditions to investigate the formation, spatial distribution and flow behaviour of FOG deposits. The system enables controlled observation of deposit growth and its interactions with common sewer solids, including food debris (WFFD), facial tissues (WFFT), wet wipes (WFWW) and combined wastes (WWA). The mass of accumulated deposits increased by 48.7%, 66.4%, 64.7% and 67.5% in the presence of WFFD, WFFT, WFWW and WWA, respectively, compared with FOG-only deposits which had an accumulated mass of 47.88 ± 1.81 g. The spatial distribution of accumulated deposits containing solids was non-uniform, with greater deposit thickness observed near the inlet and a gradual decrease towards the outlet of the pipe loop. The average thickness of deposits with WFFT, WFWW and the WWA were 15.2 ± 4.24 mm, 14 ± 0.57 mm and 15.75 ± 0.52 mm, respectively, and the maximum thickness reached about 23 ± 5.42 mm, 20.5 ± 4.95 mm and 26.5 ± 4.95 mm, respectively. The rheological behaviour of these deposits was characterised using Herschel-Bulkley and Power Law models and integrated with computational fluid dynamics (CFD) simulations to quantify their hydraulic implications. Rheological analysis revealed that post-yield stress ( τ > τ 0 ) plays a critical role in the development of sewer blockage, governing deposit mobility after yielding. Deposits containing solids show substantial yield stress and consistency index, indicating strong resistance to flow even after the yield threshold is exceeded. CFD simulations further demonstrated that deposit density strongly influenced pressure gradients, with higher densities generating increased inlet pressures as flow velocity increases, while yield stress directly governed wall shear stress development. Overall, the integrated pipe-loop-rheology-CFD framework provides a mechanistic understanding of FOG deposit behaviour and offers a robust platform for evaluating blockage risks and designing more resilient sewer systems.

Sulfonate-enriching coating technique for nanofiltration membranes to enhance water permeation and removal of per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances
works.abstract: The removal of per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFASs) from contaminated water sources can be significantly enhanced by adopting water treatment using nanofiltration (NF) membranes in drinking water applications. This study aimed to develop a sulfonate-enriching membrane surface coating technique to achieve high rejection of perfluorooctanoic acid (PFOA) and perfluorooctanesulfonic acid (PFOS) while preserving water permeance. Optimization of the surface coating technique involved optimizing the number of polyethylenimine (PEI) and poly(sodium 4-styrenesulfonate) (PSS) coats and different types of chemical treatments before and after the surface coating process. Notably, the triple-coated NF membrane pre-treated with NaOH exhibited a 15–24% increase in the rejection of PFOA and PFOS, and its permeance was 15% greater than that of an uncoated NF membrane. Characterization of the membranes indicated that the improved PFOA and PFOS rejection was likely due to the reduced pore size and increased electrostatic repulsion from the denser sulfonate groups in the polyamide separation layer of the NF membrane. The practicality of the developed NF membranes was demonstrated by the significant mitigation of membrane fouling during the treatment of typical surface water (dam water) and heavily contaminated water (simulated by primary wastewater effluent). The findings of this study highlight the potential of sulfonate-functionalized membrane surfaces to enhance PFOA and PFOS rejection, decrease the fouling tendency of NF membranes, and improve membrane permeability.

Adaptive Integration of Wastewater and Digital Proxies for Infectious Disease Forecasting: A Flexible Pipeline Evaluated Across Multi-Country Datasets
works.abstract: Accurate infectious disease forecasting using wastewater surveillance data is often limited by small sample sizes and the inherent stochasticity of environmental signals. We developed a data-centric modeling framework that embeds feature selection and applied it to one-week-ahead prediction of reported COVID-19 cases at 11 sites in France, Spain and Japan during 2020-2021, before the emergence of the Omicron variant. The framework compared the added value of data pipeline components with the effect of algorithm selection, using Ridge Regression as a common estimator for pipeline comparisons. Extended Time Series (n ≈ 50) were evaluated by walk-forward forecasting, and Short Time Series (n ≈ 20) by repeated random splitting, which assesses prediction within the observed epidemic trajectory. Adding Google Trends data and a government stringency index to wastewater signals reduced RMSE by 49.9% on average at four French sites (R² = 0.68-0.80), with a lower RMSE in 89-95% of random splits, and reduced forecasting error at all four Extended Time Series sites. No consistent improvement was observed at three low-incidence Spanish sites with erratic case dynamics. Temporal feature engineering reduced forecasting error by 21.0% and 40.8% at the two sites with the strongest wastewater-case correlations, and data augmentation added a further improvement at one site only. Differences among algorithms were smaller and less consistent than those between pipelines in the Short Time Series group, whereas Ridge outperformed tree-based models in walk-forward forecasting. In a negative-control analysis, decoy search terms were selected less frequently than Google Trends terms at all sites with positive R². These results indicate that the added value of digital proxies and policy indices depends on the local signal and requires site-specific evaluation. The proposed framework offers a practical workflow for identifying useful data sources for wastewater-based case prediction in data-scarce settings.

Illuminating an overlooked sewage crisis – synthesising evidence on foul waste contaminating surface water sewers across England and Wales
works.abstract: Separated sewer systems transport foul waste to treatment facilities while directing surface waters into freshwater environments. However, sewer-related issues can lead to foul waste contaminating surface water pipes, which subsequently enters waterbodies via ‘Polluted Surface Water Outfalls’ (F-PSWOs). Despite creating significant environmental and human health problems globally, F-PSWOs remain overlooked and under-researched. This paper synthesizes evidence from England and Wales (United Kingdom) on F-PSWO causes, impacts and management pathways. A novel conceptualisation is presented that details illicit misconnections, failing sewer infrastructure and foul sewer blockages as primary F-PSWO causes. These have been historically examined in siloes, but their collective and interactive effects should be more widely investigated. F-PSWO impacts have been sparsely researched, but elevated concentrations of ammonia- and phosphorus-related parameters, increased biochemical oxygen demand and declines in pollution-sensitive taxa have been consistently reported. These trends were broadly supported in new empirical analysis presented, whereby F-PSWOs yielded strong statistical effects on various water quality and ecological responses. These findings were less marked for Combined Sewer Overflows, which likely reflects their lower prevalence regionally, but nevertheless highlights that F-PSWOs can be a principal driver of sewage-related impacts in certain freshwater contexts. Finally, F-PSWO management pathways from their original cause to remediation are discussed, including challenges on legal complexities in sewerage governance, monitoring inefficiencies and public (un)awareness, which are discussed alongside emerging opportunities. This study hence sheds much needed light on this neglected sewage crisis, and highlights the pressing need to protect freshwater ecosystems from the environment damages caused by F-PSWOs.

Membrane-aerated biofilm reactors (MABRs) are enriched with filamentous fungi at high carbon concentrations
works.abstract: Membrane-aerated biofilm reactors (MABRs) are an energy-efficient wastewater treatment technology based on biofilms grown on gas-permeable membranes. As with most wastewater treatment technologies, MABR biofilms are typically dominated by bacteria. However, here we show that MABRs supplied with high organic carbon loadings can be dominated by filamentous fungi, leading to thick, stiff biofilms. When fed with food processing wastewater at approximately 550 mg COD L⁻¹, filamentous fungi accounted for 85% of the biofilm, compared to 30% for co-diffusional controls. The MABR biofilms showed EPS matrices enriched in protein and extracellular DNA, and were approximately tenfold stiffer than co-diffusional biofilms. When supplied with 550 mg COD L⁻¹ acetate in minimal medium, filamentous fungi accounted for 67% of the biofilm and were dominated by Geotrichum and Galactomyces . In contrast, MABRs supplied with 150 mg COD L⁻¹ acetate had only 4% filamentous fungi. These findings identify filamentous fungi as important and overlooked members of MABR biofilms, especially for high carbon loadings. A potential benefit is that fungi can degrade recalcitrant compounds not degraded by bacteria. However, the biofilm’s greater mechanical strength may lead to excessive biofilm accumulation and may require special measures to promote detachment.

works.abstract: The growing demand for biostimulants has promoted microalgae as promising biotechnological platforms. Chlorella sorokiniana has shown potential for agricultural applications; however, the effects of carbon substrates under mixotrophic conditions on biomass productivity, metabolite accumulation, and biostimulant activity remain poorly understood. Complex organic carbon substrates enhanced carotenoid production and biostimulant potential. Glucose supported the highest growth rate (0.6 d −1 ) and biomass productivity (2.9-fold the carbon-free control), whereas lactose reduced productivity to 0.57-fold. Lactose at 1 g C·L −1 maximized carotenoid accumulation (0.92% DW, 85% above the control), while skim milk at 5 g C·L −1 yielded the highest volumetric carotenoid productivity (0.46 mg·L −1 ·d −1 ). Quantifiable phytohormone concentrations ranged from 131.0 to 2924.1 ng·g −1 DW. Carbon substrate and concentration influenced phytohormone profiles, with concentration-dependent changes in the relative predominance of indole-3-acetic acid (IAA) and jasmonic acid (JA). Germination indices ranged from 232% with glucose at 1 g C·L −1 to 10% with bicarbonate at 5 g C·L −1 , maintaining identical substrate rankings across concentrations. Cell adhesion varied from 1671 to 105,544 cells·mm −2 , with bicarbonate promoting attachment at low concentrations, glycerol at high concentrations, and lactose consistently limiting adhesion. These findings demonstrate that carbon substrate selection strongly influences growth, carotenoid accumulation, phytohormone profiles, biostimulant activity, and cell adhesion in mixotrophic C. sorokiniana , highlighting its potential for producing biomass with tailored agricultural applications

Salicylic acid offsets productivity-infrastructure trade-off in marine microalga cultivation without carbon dioxide dosing
works.abstract: Salicylic acid supplementation recovered part of the productivity lost when a marine microalga was grown at elevated salinity without carbon dioxide dosing or pH control. Chrysochromulina rotalis was grown in a six-stage sequential-batch cascade in 10 L bubble-column photobioreactors, with pH control switched off, restored and switched off again at 35 and 50 practical salinity units and paired supplemented and control reactors at every stage. Commercial marine salts served as a controlled proxy for desalination concentrate. Withdrawing carbon dioxide dosing lowered maximum biomass productivity by 54%, whereas higher salinity with pH control retained 85% of reference productivity. With both stressors combined, reactors receiving 30 mg L −1 salicylic acid reached 52–54% higher maximum productivity than paired controls, recovering one-third of the loss relative to the reference, and raised nitrate removal from 55% to 81%; total fatty acid content nearly tripled along the stress gradient and was unaffected by supplementation. Each route was modelled as a 200-t yr −1 plant fed with seawater reverse-osmosis concentrate, with its own mass, energy and equipment balance. Production costs were 12.61, 28.54 and 19.19 € kg −1 , and cradle-to-gate global warming potentials 3.89, 3.92 and 2.65 kg CO 2 -eq kg −1 , for the reference, unsupplemented and supplemented routes. Supplementation was cheaper than the unsupplemented route in every Monte Carlo iteration but did not reach cost parity with the reference and fell below break-even once downstream recovery and processing costs were charged. Salicylic acid makes low-infrastructure cultivation cheaper and lower in carbon, but not yet competitive with conventional pH-controlled operation.

Environmental Drivers of Nontuberculous Mycobacteria in Tropical Freshwater Systems
works.abstract: Whilst microbial diversity still remains largely unexplored across environments and scales, microbial biogeography is shaped by edaphic and ecological drivers, and shifts in microbial community composition are frequently associated with host community structure and health. Nontuberculous mycobacteria represent a striking example of environmental microorganisms with opportunistic pathogenic potential. Unfortunately, understanding of their diversity and distribution in tropical freshwater environments remains limited, while such knowledge is crucial for predicting disease emergence and transmission. Here we aimed at (i) identifying microhabitat abiotic and biotic drivers influencing their diversity and distribution in French Guiana, (ii) comparing their diversity and distribution between French Guiana and Côte d'Ivoire, and (iii) examining co-occurrences between mycobacterial communities in different environmental contexts. By deploying an eDNA-based metabarcoding approach from tropical freshwater ecosystems, we suggest that their diversity and distribution are mainly driven by habitat type (urban vs. rural), sample type (water vs. sediment), and local abiotic factors such as phosphorus levels in sediments (with species-specific effects). Moreover, we found a stratified distribution of mycobacteria depending on sediment texture (fine silts vs. coarse sand) and depth. Overall, we suggest that their ecological interactions may occur at the microhabitat level rather than following clear biogeographic patterns.

works.title: Insight Into the Evolution of Symbiosis in the Cupriavidus Genus: Highly Conserved Symbiotic Island and a Patchy Phylogenetic Distribution
works.abstract: Currently, diversity and evolutionary studies on beta-rhizobia have primarily focused on Paraburkholderia, leaving the evolutionary history of symbiosis in the Cupriavidus genus largely unexplored. The present work provides an updated view of symbiotic Cupriavidus diversity and analyses the origin and evolution of their nitrogen-fixing capabilities. Using whole-genome phylogenetic reconstructions, we demonstrate that symbiotic Cupriavidus strains belong to five distinct evolutionary lineages, intermixed with non-symbiotic species. Comparative genomics revealed high synteny and sequence conservation within the symbiotic island across all lineages, suggesting a single ancestral acquisition of the nod-nif-fix clusters. However, in contrast, we observed very low sequence conservation among the (mega)plasmids carrying these genes. This finding definitively excludes the existence of a universal conserved replicon carrying the symbiotic genes within beta-rhizobia. Instead, our results reveal a mosaic evolutionary pattern where a highly conserved symbiotic island is mobilized across highly variable plasmid backbones. Ultimately, our findings highlight that the distribution of symbiotic traits in Cupriavidus has been shaped by a complex interplay of horizontal gene transfer, plasmid remodelling, and host-driven selective pressures, positioning South America as a key hotspot for beta-rhizobial biodiversity.

works.title: Long‐Term Acclimation and Membrane Lipid Remodelling Enable Anaerobic Oxidation of Methane at Low‐ pH by ‘ Ca . Methanoperedens vercellensis’
works.abstract: Anaerobic methanotrophic archaea are key members of the methane cycle, preventing emissions of the potent greenhouse gas into the atmosphere. Previous studies of freshwater anaerobic methanotrophs targeted their activity at circumneutral pH whereas molecular ecology studies detected anaerobic methane oxidizers in acidic environments such as peatlands. However, it remains unclear whether they can adapt to low pH and sustain an effective biological methane filter under acidic conditions. Here, we show that a granular enrichment culture of the freshwater methanotroph 'Ca. M. vercellensis' remains metabolically active down to pH 5.65 with appropriate acclimation time while it loses activity when experiencing immediate acid stress. Population-wide acclimation is required to support anaerobic methane oxidation at lower pH. Archaeal lipid analyses revealed an increased abundance of zwitterionic intact polar lipids over anionic lipids. This coincided with structural changes in biomass granules while methane oxidation rate and enrichment proportion of 'Ca. M. vercellensis' remained stable. These results demonstrate that 'Ca. M. vercellensis' remains metabolically active at lower pH values, despite increased maintenance energy requirements and the need for cytoplasmic pH homeostasis. Furthermore, they highlight that stress adaptations in slow-growing microorganisms requires long-term observation. Our findings provide new insights into methane cycling in acidic ecosystems.

works.title: The Broad Ecological Range of Salmonella enterica Serotype Typhimurium Is Associated With Genomic Diversification
works.abstract: Salmonella Typhimurium is a versatile foodborne pathogen with a broad ecological range, making it an ideal model to better understand pathogen adaptations that allow them to infect multiple hosts and persist across environments. Here, we analysed 595 genomes of S. Typhimurium representing three food animal sources (bovine, swine, and poultry) and one non-food animal source (wild birds). We found that S. Typhimurium from food animal sources generally had a more open pangenome and harboured more antimicrobial resistance genes (ARGs). Notably, swine isolates exhibited the most open pangenome and the highest prevalence of ARGs, patterns that were associated with a greater presence of mobile genetic elements, particularly plasmids. Despite similar core genome sizes, S. Typhimurium from different sources displayed distinct patterns of positive selection in the core genome that varied in frequency and targeted functional categories. In contrast, although accessory genome sizes varied substantially across sources, the frequency of positive selection remained similar. Using machine learning, we identified source-predictive genetic variants, many of which are associated with stress-response functions. These findings suggest that gain and loss of accessory genes and positive selection acting on core genes support differential adaptation in S. Typhimurium, potentially contributing to its broad ecological range.

We characterized the taxonomic diversity of river microbial communities across diverse sites using high-throughput sequencing. Our findings demonstrate that environmental drivers—from seasonal cycles to farm-level inputs—predictably reshape the bacterial landscape, providing a framework for monitoring aquatic ecosystem dynamics.

works.title: Host Development and Environment Influence the Microbiomes of Aquatic Insects and Riparian Spiders
works.abstract: Larval aquatic insects harbour diverse microbiomes critical for physiology and development, yet the effects of metamorphosis combined with environmental exposures on this community remain unknown. Herein we examined bacterial microbiome composition and predicted function across larval and adult stages of three families of aquatic insects and riparian spider predators, collected upstream and downstream of wastewater treatment plants (WWTPs) in Ontario, Canada. Insect host developmental stage was the primary driver of microbiome structure. Larval microbiomes were more diverse and showed higher abundances in pathways reflecting active feeding. Larval and adult populations of holometabolous insects shared few ASVs (3.8%-12.6% of the combined ASV pool), whereas a larger proportion was shared in hemimetabolous insects (23.4%). WWTP effluent exposures led to selective microbial filtering rather than broad community restructuring. Macroinvertebrate and spider microbiomes sampled downstream were characterized by higher abundances in bacterial taxa associated with wastewaters and increased xenobiotic degradation pathways. Such impacts on spider microbiomes provide evidence that ecological impacts of effluents cross the aquatic-terrestrial boundary. Lastly, a significant decrease of vertically transmitted endosymbionts (Rickettsiella, Wolbachia) was detected in aquatic insects, representing a pathway through which effluent pollution may affect host fitness without detectably altering overall microbiome diversity.

works.title: Targeted Mutagenesis Reveals Noncanonical Genetic Requirements for Carbon Monoxide Oxidation
works.abstract: ABSTRACT Carbon monoxide (CO) oxidation is a widespread microbial energy metabolism catalysed by MoCu CO dehydrogenase (CODH). Of the two phylogenetically distinct forms (form‐I and form‐II), only form‐I CODH is functionally verified. CODH activity requires maturation of the [CuSMoO 2 ] active site, linked in the carboxydotroph Afipia carboxidovorans OM5 to the genes coxDEF . CODH maturation remains untested outside of this system. Paraburkholderia terrae COX, a recently isolated carboxydovore, encodes both forms of CODH with a reduced and reorganised cox gene cluster. Using targeted mutagenesis, we identify rcoM , coxL , coxF , and coxG as essential for CO oxidation, whereas coxD, coxE , and mocA are non‐essential. Deletion of the accessory coxDEF genes produced distinct phenotypes compared to A. carboxidovorans OM5, revealing alternative routes for CODH maturation. Both coxL paralogs were deleted singly and in double knockouts, providing the first molecular evidence that form‐II CODH does not contribute to CO oxidation in vivo in these groups of bacteria. Together, these findings show that CODH maturation and function are not universally conserved and caution against inferring CO‐oxidising capacity solely from gene presence. Pb. terrae COX emerges as a genetically tractable model for elucidating the diversity and evolution of metalloenzyme assembly pathways in bacteria.

works.title: Functional Genomics of a Zinc‐Solubilising Kosakonia cowanii RL ‐16 and Its Application for Zinc Biofortification in Oryza sativa L.
works.abstract: Zinc (Zn) is assumed to be the most important micronutrient due to its involvement in different biochemical processes. The daily requirement of Zn for the human body, however, cannot be fulfilled by traditional staple crops such as rice due to its low availability to plants, especially in alkaline soils. The present study was carried out to investigate the potential of indigenous microbial flora, isolated from different agroecological zones, for Zn solubilization and combating Zn deficiency in rice. Out of a total of 135 isolates, RL-16, identified as Kosakonia cowanii, emerged as the most valuable resource for sustainable agricultural applications due to its incredible Zn solubilization potential and additional PGP characteristics. Gene mining of RL-16 revealed the footprints of solubilization of Zn and other nutrients. Under microcosmic conditions, zinc content was significantly improved for the treatment with RL-16 (134.7 mg/kg ± 0.6), compared to the control containing only an insoluble zinc source (107.7 mg/kg ± 1.6). Zinc translocation in seed (ZnSd) was enhanced by the application of RL-16 across both varieties, which was also confirmed by field evaluation. This study demonstrates the whole genome sequence analysis of Kosakonia cowanii and its potential role in Zn biofortification for more targeted and sustainable agricultural practices.

works.title: Microbial Syntrophy Drives Methanogenesis From Residual Hydrocarbons in Anaerobic Oil Sands Tailings
works.abstract: Anaerobic oil sands tailings can generate methane for decades as residual naphtha-range and petroleum hydrocarbons sustain microbial metabolism, but how microbial interactions link hydrocarbon turnover to methanogenesis remains poorly resolved. To characterize these microbial associations, we analyse two naphtha-amended anaerobic tailings incubation series using 16S rRNA gene relative abundance, hydrocarbon consumption, and methane production data within a cooperative game-theoretical framework. The abundance-informed Shapley analysis attributes system-level variation to bacterial-archaeal coalitions, highlighting key syntrophic partnerships. Several taxa show inferred contributions to methanogenesis that are disproportionate to their relative abundance, indicating that model-based attribution can differ from abundance ranking. Sensitivity analysis shows that the main methane-attribution patterns remain interpretable across alternative abundance-weighted coefficient formulations. These interaction patterns shift across incubation phases, showing that microbial control over hydrocarbon-dependent methanogenesis changes through time. When incorporated into stochastic forecasting, Shapley-derived reaction intensities improve predictive performance compared with reduced microbial and non-microbial benchmarks. Together, our results indicate that methane production in oil sands tailings can be interpreted through abundance-informed bacterial-archaeal coalition structure, providing a coalition-aware basis for interpreting and forecasting methanogenic hydrocarbon transformation.

works.title: Issue Information
Seasonal and Environmental Influences on Microbial Community Dynamics in the Dunk River Watershed, Prince Edward Island, Canada
works.abstract: Riverine ecosystems are crucial biogeochemical hubs, with their microbial communities playing a key role in nutrient cycling and overall ecosystem health. This study used shotgun metagenomic sequencing to characterize the seasonal and environmental drivers of taxonomic and functional microbial community structure (read depth between 1.91 and 30.44 bp) in four tributaries of the Dunk River watershed in Prince Edward Island (PEI), a landscape shaped by intensive agriculture and groundwater-dominated streamflow, where the seasonal and land-use impacts on the river's microbiome remain understudied. Although taxonomic composition showed no significant spatial variation among sampling sites, functional profiling identified subtle but distinct spatial signatures, primarily driven at the site with the least human impacts. Mass effects driven by above- or below-ground water dispersal pathways may override local selective pressures, resulting in a more uniform community structure across different locations. The study also identified significant correlations between certain rare microbial taxa and nutrient concentrations. This work provides critical baseline data on microbial ecology in PEI river systems, indicating that while temporal factors are the primary identifiable drivers among the measured variables, a substantial majority of the community variance remains unexplained, likely reflecting the inherent stochasticity of open riverine ecosystems.

works.title: Flagella‐Mediated Biofilm Formation and 3D Swarming Drive Virulence in the Honey Bee Pathogen Paenibacillus larvae
works.abstract: American foulbrood, a devastating bacterial disease affecting honey bee larvae, represents a major threat to apiculture worldwide. Its etiological agent, the Gram-positive, endospore-forming bacterium Paenibacillus larvae, has therefore been extensively studied to elucidate the molecular mechanisms underlying its pathogenicity and to identify key virulence determinants. In the present study, we identified the peritrichous flagella of P. larvae as a novel and important virulence factor of the genotype ERIC II. A flagella-deficient mutant was generated and shown to exhibit multiple defects in vitro associated with biofilm formation, including altered biofilm architecture, reduced adhesion, impaired floating capacity and loss of swarming motility. Survival assays using honey bee larvae, complemented by fluorescence in situ hybridization (FISH) analyses of infected larvae, further demonstrated the crucial contribution of flagella to virulence in vivo by mediating biofilm formation on the larval midgut epithelium as well as three-dimensional swarming during epithelial invasion.

works.title: The Association of Diet, Intestinal Microbial Starch Utilizers and Butyrate‐Producers in Early Life
works.abstract: During the first year of life, infant diet changes from liquid to solid food. Resistant starch is one of the first complex carbohydrates available to gut microbiota. With the overall goal to gain mechanistic understanding on the development of microbial starch utilization capacity and its impact on fermentation activity, we investigated the interplay of diet, starch utilizers Ruminococcus bromii and Bifidobacterium adolescentis and the butyrate producer Anaerobutyricum hallii using samples from the longitudinal CARE cohort, and in vitro. Infants started to consume resistant starch at 4 months. While less than one quarter of the infants harboured starch utilizers at 5 months, occurrence increased until the end of year one. In vitro, R. bromii and B. adolescentis degraded resistant starch but only R. bromii released reducing sugars. B. adolescentis formed acetate and lactate. In co-cultures, R. bromii with A. hallii produced more butyrate via reducing sugars than with lactate and acetate from B. adolescentis. At one year of age, infants that harboured both starch utilizer and A. hallii had higher faecal butyrate levels than those without these species. Our results suggest that differences in the mode of resistant starch degradation and cross-feeding contributed to functional redundancy and affected butyrate formation.

works.title: The Promise and Limitations of Metabolic Trait Prediction Across Diverse Bacteria
works.abstract: Metabolic traits mediate microbial interactions and underpin mechanistic models of community assembly. With the rapid expansion of genomic data and bioinformatic tools, it is widely assumed that metabolic traits such as substrate utilization can be reliably inferred from genomes alone. Here, we systematically evaluate this assumption by comparing genome-based predictions from four commonly used tools to high-throughput growth phenotypes of 186 marine bacteria. For simple substrates, prediction accuracy was limited and highly variable across taxa and substrates, with many strains predicted at or near chance levels. For three of four tools, most errors were false positives, indicating that apparent pathway completeness frequently fails to translate into growth under laboratory conditions. In contrast, genomic prediction of polysaccharide utilization based on carbohydrate-active enzyme content performed substantially better, suggesting that traits that depend on a few highly specific enzymes are easier to predict. While genome-based approaches can recover broad statistical patterns in metabolic strategies, their limited strain-level reliability constrains ecological inference and modelling. For the foreseeable future, large-scale experimental phenotypic characterization will remain an indispensable component of microbial ecology, both to reveal trait distributions and to ground-truth and improve genomic predictions.

works.title: Links Between Environmental Quality, Gut Microbiota, and Host Performance in Nutrient‐Impacted Springs
works.abstract: Microbial symbionts may enhance adaptation to environmental stress, yet their role in nutrient-enriched freshwater habitats remains unclear. We conducted a full-factorial laboratory experiment with least killifish, Heterandria formosa, manipulating water chemistry from four Florida springs and gut microbiota inoculations from conspecifics at those sites. Sequencing of 16S rRNA revealed that gut microbial richness was higher in fish reared in less nutrient-loaded waters, but inoculation treatments, if successful, did not produce significant shifts in composition. Gut communities consistently differed from ambient water, with enrichment of Pseudomonadota and Planctomycetota. Females grew more slowly in the most polluted water. In a parallel result, males displayed higher mass-specific metabolic rates in the most nutrient-loaded water. Reproductive output per female nearly doubled when experimental microbiota and water originated from the same site, despite stable microbial diversity, though parentage and inoculation success were not verified; therefore, these results should be interpreted cautiously. These results indicate that environmental quality shapes gut microbiota and host performance, and that matching microbial communities to habitat conditions can boost reproduction. Such interactions may contribute to freshwater fish resilience and merit integration into conservation strategies.

works.title: Divergent Responses of Bacterial and Microeukaryotic Diversity to Water‐Level Fluctuations in a Lake‐Floodplain System
works.abstract: Water-level fluctuations (WLF) are widely accepted as key drivers of aquatic species diversity in lake-floodplain systems, with diversity increasing as water levels rise. However, microorganisms may challenge this pattern that their richness does not necessarily increase with water levels. To resolve this inconsistency, we applied 16S and 18S rRNA gene amplicon sequencing to bacterial and microeukaryotic assemblages in Dongting Lake, China, during the low-water (LWP; January 2024) and high-water periods (HWP; August 2024). Microeukaryotic richness was higher during HWP than LWP (p < 0.01), whereas bacterial richness remained comparable (p = 0.96). Habitat-of-origin annotation indicated that terrestrial-derived microeukaryotes contributed to this increase (p = 0.02), whereas terrestrial bacterial inputs did not (p > 0.3), consistent with their divergent fates in the water column: soil microeukaryotes are more likely to persist after flooding than soil bacteria. Co-occurrence networks evidenced substantially stronger bacteria-microeukaryote associations at high water and partial least squares path modelling resolved a DOC-to-bacteria-to-microeukaryotes pathway activated only during the HWP. These signals suggest that enhanced hydrological connectivity promoted community coalescence, possibly through intensified trophic coupling, although this interpretation requires experimental verification. This study highlights that natural WLFs reshape microbial richness by intermittently reconnecting terrestrial and aquatic microbial species pools.

works.title: Mycoviruses in the Genomic Era: Ecological, Evolutionary and One Health Perspectives
works.abstract: Mycoviruses are widespread and ecologically significant components of the biosphere, acting as hidden modulators of fungal diversity, metabolism and symbiotic interactions. This review synthesizes historical and technological advances in mycovirus discovery within an integrative One Health framework linking human, animal, plant and environmental health. We trace the transition from early dsRNA-based detection and Sanger sequencing to modern metatranscriptomic, metagenomic and petabase-scale data-mining approaches that have dramatically expanded known mycovirome diversity, uncovering deeply divergent RNA virus lineages. We survey the major mycovirus families and their genomic architectures and compare the strengths and inherent biases of current discovery strategies. We critically assess evidence for horizontal viral transfer across kingdoms, distinguishing experimentally demonstrated cross-host replication from phylogenetic inference alone and review mycovirus roles in modulating fungal virulence in agricultural and clinical settings, explicitly separating robust findings from preliminary or speculative reports. Hypovirulence-based biocontrol of phytopathogenic fungi emerges as the only application currently supported by field-validated evidence, whereas mycovirus-based therapy for human fungal infection remains a long-term hypothesis rather than a near-term clinical strategy. We underscore the need to combine rigorous experimental and computational approaches to characterize mycovirome complexity and function and outline priority research directions for the coming decade.

works.title: Estuarine Biofilm Communities Adapt to Changing Conditions While Retaining Crucial Pollutant‐Combatting Functions
works.abstract: Industrialization has increased the influx of toxicants into intertidal and estuarine ecosystems. Intertidal sediments are exposed to heavy metals, polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons, pesticides, and other xenobiotics through effluents, shipping, spillages, battery disposal, and agricultural run-off. Pollutants accumulate in sediments, disrupting nutrient cycling and impairing primary productivity, thereby threatening coastal food webs. Sediment-bound biofilms or microphytobenthos are complex assemblages of microorganisms embedded in extracellular polymeric substances and play vital roles in biogeochemical cycling, sediment stabilization, and pollutant remediation. Their functional responses to contaminant exposure remain poorly understood, particularly in tropical estuaries. Biofilms from contaminated estuarine sediments were analysed using metagenome-assembled genomes (MAGs) and genome-scale metabolic models (GEMs) in a paired field-laboratory approach. Greater metabolic diversity of field biofilms indicated broader functional capacities to sustain pollutant exposure. Conserved genes linked to organic compound degradation and metal transport co-occurred across MAGs, suggesting integrated detoxification strategies. GEM-based simulations revealed metabolic cross-feeding underlying contaminant transformation. Culture conditions shaped microbial succession and ecological roles, yet core pollutant degradation and nutrient processing functions persisted, operated by dominant taxa. Microphytobenthic experimental studies rely on laboratory-cultured communities derived from field-collected samples. Contrasting community dynamics and altered metabolism due to 'bottle effect' are foundational for correctly interpreting laboratory-based experimental outcomes.

works.title: Widespread Microbial Suppression and Functional Shifts in Wastewater Treatment Microbiomes Under Climate Warming
works.abstract: Climate warming is expected to reshape microbial communities, yet its impacts on engineered microbial ecosystems remain poorly understood. Here, we developed a deep-learning framework to assess microbial responses to climate warming across global wastewater treatment plants (WWTPs). Under a +1.5°C warming perturbation, ~77% of analyzed microbial taxa showed predicted declines in relative abundance, accompanied by decreased weights in ~54% of reconstructed microbial associations. Keystone taxa were also predominantly predicted to decline, suggesting potential changes in community association structure under warming. From an exploratory ecological perspective, warming-associated increases in viral abundance may further contribute to microbial suppression through enhanced viral pressure on key taxa. Taxonomically inferred functional profiles suggested warming was also associated with broad shifts in ecological functional profiles, including potential impairments in nutrient cycling. Notably, increases in methanogenesis-associated taxa coupled with reduced methane oxidation suggested a potential imbalance in methane cycling. Together, these findings indicate that climate warming may substantially reshape the composition, interactions and ecological functioning of WWTP microbiomes. Our study provides a global assessment of climate-associated risks in engineered microbial ecosystems and offers a basis for developing climate-resilient wastewater management strategies.

works.title: Influence of Soluble and Mineral Sources of Cobalt on Methanogenesis and Growth in Methanosarcina barkeri Fusaro and Methanococcus maripaludis S2
works.abstract: ABSTRACT Cobalt (Co) is a required component of cofactors and coenzymes in all life and has a pronounced role in the one carbon metabolism of methanogens. However, methanogens often inhabit sulphidic environments where Co precipitates and is incorporated into low solubility mineral phases, such as pyrite (FeS 2 ). Here, we initially examined the influence of Co availability on the growth kinetics of (1) Methanosarcina barkeri with different methanogenesis substrates and (2) Methanococcus maripaludis with different sulphur sources. We then investigated Co acquisition from cobaltoan pyrite [(Co,Fe)S 2 ]. Co demand was highest in M. barkeri grown on methanol/acetate relative to hydrogen/carbon dioxide or methanol only and in M. maripaludis grown with sulphide relative to cysteine or cysteine/thiosulphate. Methanol/acetate‐grown M. barkeri and formate‐grown M. maripaludis grew with (Co,Fe)S 2 as well as with soluble sources of Co, Fe and S. Both strains required direct contact to reduce and solubilize Fe and S from (Co,Fe)S 2 . Further, M. barkeri grown with (Co,Fe)S 2 produced an equal amount of cobamides relative to cells provided with soluble Co, Fe, and S. These findings indicate that the availability of methanogenesis substrates and sulphur sources influence Co requirements for methanogens and that these organisms can acquire Co, Fe and S from (Co,Fe)S 2 .

works.title: Immobilized Epiphytic Bacteria Enhance Macrophyte Suppression of a Bloom‐Forming Cyanobacterium
works.abstract: Harmful cyanobacterial blooms are an increasing threat to freshwater ecosystems and water security worldwide. Biological control using macrophytes or algicidal bacteria is often studied separately despite natural co-occurrence. Here we show that the epiphytic bacterium Priestia megaterium strain BW, isolated from submerged macrophytes, exhibits strong algicidal activity and forms an enhanced suppression system with its host plant Vallisneria natans. Pre-colonization of BW on V. natans leaves achieves > 80% inhibition of Microcystis aeruginosa biomass within 5 days. When immobilized on a ceramic material carrier, BW rapidly suppresses algal photosynthetic efficiency within 48 h. Mechanistically, the algicidal effect follows a multi-pathway process involving early photosynthetic impairment, oxidative stress and subsequent cellular disintegration. Notably, the combined application of immobilized BW with V. natans produces stronger and faster suppression than either the bacterium or the plant alone. Our findings demonstrate that an epiphytic bacterium can retain potent algicidal activity outside its native biofilm and that its efficacy is markedly enhanced when re-integrated with the plant, providing direct evidence for plant-microbe synergistic control of cyanobacterial blooms.

works.title: Endophytic Success of Salmonella enterica and Escherichia coli in Plants via Root Uptake Is Governed by Stochasticity in Transpiration
works.abstract: Human foodborne pathogens can internalize into edible plant tissues through root uptake, yet the mechanisms governing this process remain poorly understood. Here, we developed a localized enrichment inoculation system that enables robust and reproducible investigation of bacterial internalization in plants. Using Arabidopsis thaliana and multiple microgreen species, we show that Salmonella enterica and Escherichia coli rapidly penetrate intact roots and translocate to shoots independent of bacterial motility, virulence, plant immunity or root tissue damage. Instead, internalization is strongly associated with plant transpiration activity. Transcriptomic and physiological analyses revealed that stochastic variation in photosynthesis and transpiration between genetically identical plants underlies highly heterogeneous contamination outcomes, producing near-bimodal distributions of bacterial load among individual plants. Suppression of transpiration through cooling or abscisic acid treatment significantly reduced pathogen internalization. These findings establish plant physiological stochasticity as a critical determinant of foodborne pathogen uptake and reveal new opportunities for mitigation strategies in agriculture.

works.title: Synthetic microbial communities enable sustainable restoration of coal gangue-impacted soils by reprogramming nutrient cycling
works.abstract: Coal gangue disrupts microbial diversity and impairs nutrient cycling, constraining sustainable regional development. Traditional bioremediation relies on functional microbial traits, yet they often fail to colonize and perform in carbon-limited environments despite exogenous carbon inputs. We designed activity-oriented synthetic microbial communities (SynComs) to leverage exogenous carbon amendments and subsequently evaluated carbon use efficiency (CUE) as a community-level functional trait. High-activity SynComs were assembled from native and non-native strains based on their activity and metabolite interactions. The native-derived SynCom (SC3) enhances carbon and nitrogen cycling, whereas the non-native-derived SynCom (SC5) boosts diversity and phosphorus cycling (P < 0.05). These contrasts were associated with differences in strain functional contributions, community interactions, and carbon-source utilization. Metabolomics revealed greater functional microbial activation in SC5-conditioned biochar-derived metabolites than in glucose-derived metabolites. Multi-omics, single-cell Raman spectroscopy, and field studies confirmed the positive roles of SynComs in rhizosphere metabolism and nutrient cycling. Activity-driven SynComs approach was more efficient than single amendments, offering a potentially scalable strategy to restore carbon-limited tailing ecosystems and promote sustainability.

works.title: Behavior of radionuclides in high temperature combustion processes: A radiological hazard?
works.abstract: High temperature combustion processes, such as combustion of fossil fuels or biomass for energy production, tobacco smoking, organic waste incineration, or wildfire events in forests, are governed by the same physical, chemical, and thermal mechanisms that control the partitioning, enrichment, migration, volatilization, and condensation of radionuclides, either anthropogenic or naturally occurring, which may pose a significant radiological hazard to the environment and to human health. A review was carried out up to the end of 2025, using a PRISMA-style workflow. In this review, those combustion scenarios are presented within a common mechanistic framework to better understand the behavior of primordial and anthropogenic radionuclides under these conditions. Modeling and empirical results under controlled conditions show that radionuclide volatility drives the different activity concentrations when comparing heavy bottom ashes, lighter fly ashes, and flue gases (smoke). Enrichment factors can vary by orders of magnitude depending on temperature profiles, redox conditions, chlorine, sulfur and calcium content, and particle size distributions. Radioisotopes of volatile elements and compounds, such as C137s under chlorine-rich atmosphere conditions, or P210o, or P210b exhibit preferential condensation on fine particulate matter (< 2.5 μ m), whereas refractory elements and compounds, including isotopes of uranium, thorium, plutonium, or americium, concentrate in heavier fractions. In particular, C137s, P210o and P210b can show enrichment factors of up to 1000 times in fine particles due to vapor and condensation mechanisms, following an inverse correlation between radioactivity and particle diameter. This fact is relevant as the inhalation of submicron particles (< 1 μ m) may constitute one of the primary exposure pathways, and thus a radiological hazard, with combined-exposure implications with other co-contaminants, like heavy metals or organic toxics, which are often present in the gases of combustion processes. A structured synthesis was developed, highlighting where this framework is applicable, and providing advice on future research on radionuclide speciation in high-temperature, ultrafine-particle characterization, weathering of aged ash, small and dispersed combustion sources, and the effect of modern ultra-low-emission retrofits and biomass co-firing on radionuclide partitioning.

works.title: Matrix-specific oxidant demand shapes antibiotic and antimicrobial resistance mitigation during wastewater ozonation
works.abstract: Ozonation is increasingly used for wastewater-based antimicrobial resistance (AMR) mitigation; however, how wastewater matrix complexity shapes simultaneous multiclass antibiotic degradation, bacterial inactivation, ARG degradation, and molecular determinants under realistic treatment conditions remains insufficiently understood. This study provides the first integrated matrix-dependent evaluation of multiclass antibiotic degradation, bacterial inactivation, ARGs degradation, and structure-reactivity relationships across actual WWTP effluent and controlled water matrices within a unified experimental framework. In WWTP effluent, ozonation completely removed 31 of 35 antibiotics while achieving > 99% viable bacterial reduction and > 97% ARGs reduction within 60 min. Matrix-dependent behavior was compound-class specific: amphenicols, nitroimidazoles, and β-lactams were highly sensitive to matrix composition, whereas tetracyclines and sulfonamides were largely unaffected. Lower pH selectively decreased degradation of fluoroquinolones and macrolides, highlighting the importance of pH-dependent speciation and intrinsic structural reactivity. Electronic susceptibility (HOMO) dominated in simple systems, whereas in complex matrices, interactions with dissolved organic matter (DOM) and bacterial components shifted control toward polarity, hydrophobicity, and polarizability, highlighting matrix-dependent determinants of antibiotic degradation. Critically, antibiotic residues minimally affected bacterial inactivation in actual WWTP effluent but significantly inhibited 16S rRNA and ARG degradation; whereas under simplified bacteria-containing PBS, they suppressed both processes because of stronger oxidant competition. DOM imposed immediate inhibition, whereas antibiotics caused persistent oxidant demand, jointly constraining ARGs removal. These findings demonstrate that conventional treatment endpoints may overestimate true AMR hazard reduction, as ARGs persistence remains more vulnerable to matrix-specific oxidant competition. Together, these findings establish matrix-specific oxidant demand as a mechanistic basis for optimizing ozone-based AMR mitigation.

works.title: Unravelling PFAS Disruption of Thyroxine Transport by Transthyretin Using Machine Learning-Augmented Modelling
works.abstract: Thyroid-disrupting chemicals (TDCs) pose a significant risk to human health and have been associated with adverse neurological and cardiovascular effects. Among these chemicals, per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) have been shown to bind to transthyretin (TTR), disrupting thyroid hormone homeostasis and leading to adverse outcomes. In this study, we present a refined workflow for modelling and predicting PFAS activity toward TTR, where training compounds were labelled as Active or Inactive based on experimental activity values (binding affinities) exceeding 50% relative to the control, thyroxine, the biological binding partner of TTR. A curated dataset comprising experimental data from published studies was processed, resulting in 131 unique PFAS structures for modelling. The dataset was further augmented with molecular descriptors and molecular docking derived scores, followed by model optimisation and evaluation through an automated machine learning (AutoML) approach. Among the tested classification algorithms, XGBoost demonstrated the best performance, achieving an external test accuracy of 0.818. To provide mechanistic insights, molecular docking calculations and Shapley value analysis were employed, revealing that increased PFAS lipophilicity enhances binding within the hydrophobic TTR pocket, in agreement with experimental observations. In accordance with the Findable, Accessible, Interoperable, Reusable (FAIR) principles for data and models, the curated dataset is publicly available through the ChemPharos database (https://db.chempharos.eu/datasets/Datasets.zul?datasetID=ds21). The final model was implemented as a user-friendly web application on the Enalos Cloud Platform, enabling rapid screening of existing or novel PFAS and PFAS-like compounds and supporting chemical safety management (https://enaloscloud.novamechanics.com/scenarios/thyrotox/), and is fully documented via a QSAR model report format (QMRF).

Longevity and impact of PFAS contamination from legacy landfills on groundwater
works.abstract: Per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) leaching from landfills pose a risk to groundwater. This study developed a conceptual understanding of long-term PFAS leaching from legacy landfills by reviewing PFAS occurrence data and simulating leaching from two landfill types: dry landfills underlain by an unsaturated zone, and wet landfills without one. PFAS leaching was investigated using coupled 1D landfill leaching and 2D subsurface models. Scenario modelling evaluated the impact of sorption and infiltration on PFAS release over time. PFAS release and leaching longevity were controlled by retention processes within the landfill and underlying unsaturated zone, landfill type, landfill history, and hydrological conditions. Simulated dry landfills exhibited substantial retention of long-chain PFAS due to air-water interfacial sorption, leading to prolonged leaching over decades or centuries. Simulated contaminant mass discharge showed delayed peaks for long-chain PFAS, indicating the importance of long-term monitoring and management of legacy landfills. PFAS observations from Danish landfills suggest that long-chain PFAS reach groundwater earlier than predicted by the models, potentially due to heterogeneities and preferential flow paths not represented in the model. This study provides novel insights into PFAS leaching behaviour and offers a conceptual framework for risk assessment, while highlighting the critical role of the unsaturated zone.

Characterization of physical and chemical properties controlling the transport of 129I and 99Tc in ultra-high-performance grout
works.abstract: Ultra-high-performance grout (UHPG) was evaluated as an engineered barrier for encapsulating solid waste generated during nuclear waste processing. The objective of this study was to measure geochemical, hydrological, and physical properties related to 129 I and 99 Tc transport through UHPG. 99 Tc and 129 I are key health-risk drivers associated with near-subsurface nuclear disposal facilities. To provide context, a second flowable Baseline grout currently used in nuclear waste disposal facilities was also characterized. Compressive strength and bulk density were appreciably greater in the UHPG (120.5 MPa and 2.2 g/cm 3 , respectively) than the Baseline grout (8.4 MPa and 1.5 g/cm 3 ). UHPG had appreciably lower porosity (0.15 cm 3 /cm 3 ) and hydraulic conductivity ( K = 5.8 ×10 −14 cm/sec) than the Baseline grout (porosity = 0.32 cm 3 /cm 3 ; K = 9.4 ×10 −7 cm/sec). Desorption partitioning experiments indicated that both grouts had similar 129 I partitioning coefficients (C Solid /C Liquid ; K d ), of ∼100 (moles/g)/(moles/mL) and had similar aqueous iodine speciation: I - > > IO 3 - > organo-I. 99 Tc aqueous concentrations appeared to be controlled by solubility (7 ×10 −8 mol/L) in the UHPG, likely because slag in the UHPG formulation produced a reducing environment that converted the highly mobile aqueous TcO 4 - to a much less mobile Tc(IV) solid species, TcO 4 · n H 2 O. 129 I and 99 Tc observed diffusivity ( D obs ) were 6 and 7 orders of magnitude less, respectively, in the UHPG than in the Baseline grout. These tests provide multiple lines of evidence indicating that UHPG possesses excellent characteristics for encapsulating 99 Tc and 129 I waste.

works.abstract: Microplastic contamination is pervasive across aquatic ecosystems, including protected coastal environments. Todos os Santos Bay, the second-largest bay in Brazil, encompasses 1385 km² within a multiple-use marine protected area and supports over three million inhabitants, major port activities, petrochemical industries, mangrove forests, and coral reefs. Here, we assessed microplastic contamination using three filter-feeding bivalve species as sentinels, and evaluated its associations with population density, human modification, socioeconomic deprivation, and distance to river discharges using Crassostrea sp., the only species sampled at all 16 sites. A total of 834 microplastics were detected, with average concentrations of 3.21, 2.88, and 2.36 particles g-1 in clams, oysters, and mussels, respectively. These concentrations exceeded the literature-based Brazilian average for bivalves (2.06 particles g-1), indicating comparatively elevated contamination levels in Todos os Santos Bay. Microplastic contamination was widespread across Todos os Santos Bay despite all sampling sites being located within a multiple-use protected area. No consistent overall differences in microplastic concentrations were detected among species; however, a significant Species × Site interaction indicated that interspecific differences varied across sampling sites. Fibers, small and transparent particles predominated, whereas anthropogenic cellulose accounted for 56.8% of the spectroscopically characterized subset. Population density received the strongest statistical support among the evaluated socio-environmental predictors and was positively associated with microplastic concentrations in oysters. This spatial association highlights the importance of reducing land-based microplastic inputs in densely populated coastal areas through improved wastewater treatment, urban drainage, and solid waste management.

Pangolin scales as a potential retrospective biomonitoring matrix for environmental and rescue-associated chemical exposures in endangered wildlife
works.abstract: ABSTRACT Pangolins are among the world's most trafficked and endangered mammals, yet their exposure to emerging organic contaminants (EOCs) remains largely uncharacterized. Their keratinous scales represent an untapped matrix for potentially non-invasive biomonitoring. This study developed and validated a modified QuEChERS-based extraction coupled with liquid chromatography–quadrupole time-of-flight mass spectrometry (LC-QTOF/MS) for suspect screening and targeted quantification of EOCs in pangolin scales. The workflow was applied to scales collected from 18 deceased wild Formosan pangolins ( Manis pentadactyla pentadactyla ) with and without documented rescue histories. A total of 57 EOCs spanning six chemical classes were tentatively identified, reflecting environmental contamination and rescue-associated pharmaceutical exposure. Eight EOCs were further selected and confirmed as targets. The method achieved recoveries of 70–120%, relative standard deviations ≤20%, and method detection limits ranging from 0.1 to 2.0 µg kg −1 . Target EOC concentrations spanned nearly four orders of magnitude, from 0.84 µg kg −1 (isoxaflutole) to 15,400 µg kg −1 (enrofloxacin). Compositional and quantitative EOC patterns showed substantial inter-individual variation and rescue-associated pharmaceutical signatures. This study provides the first report of multiple EOC residues in pangolin scales, supporting their further evaluation as a potential retrospective biomonitoring matrix for wildlife conservation across the family Manidae .

works.title: Simultaneous cesium desorption and surfactant degradation from montmorillonite by coupled capacitive deionization–electro-oxidation
works.abstract: Remediation of cesium-contaminated clay minerals is difficult because Cs + is strongly retained within collapsed interlayer spaces. Cationic surfactants can promote Cs + release, but residual surfactant creates a secondary pollution risk requiring post-treatment. Here, a coupled capacitive deionization–electro-oxidation (CDI-EO) system using a boron-doped diamond (BDD) anode and activated carbon cathode was developed for one-step Cs + desorption and in situ surfactant degradation from Cs-saturated montmorillonite (0.95 mmol g -1 , 85% of cation exchange capacity, CEC). Electrochemical degradation of dodecyltrimethylammonium bromide (DTAB) was first optimised in a static electrolytic cell, reaching ~96% degradation at 150 mA cm -2 after 12 h for a DTAB loading of 0.5 × CEC. These conditions (150 mA cm -2 , 0.4 M Na 2 SO 4 , pH 7) were then applied in a recirculating flow-by CDI cell at 20 mL min -1 . Within 6 h, DTAB degradation reached 84–89% and Cs + desorption up to ~89%, with maximum Cs + release within 1 h due to surfactant-induced interlayer expansion and electric-field-driven ion extraction. XRD showed interlayer contraction to 1.22–1.25 nm after treatment, confirming effective surfactant removal from the clay structure. Over five consecutive cycles, Cs + desorption remained ~70% and surfactant degradation exceeded 80%, demonstrating sustained treatment performance. Electrical energy consumption was 129–140 kWh kg -1 clay for the dilute laboratory batches studied, and the electrosorption capacity of the unmodified AC cathode is identified as the bottleneck for net Cs⁺ capture. The integrated CDI-EO process therefore provides a simplified single-step route for radionuclide-contaminated clay remediation, simultaneously combining decontamination and surfactant removal while avoiding a separate post-treatment stage for disposal.

works.title: Seasonal variation in the spatial distribution, community assembly, and associated factors of antibiotic resistance genes in tropical drinking water reservoirs of Hainan, China
works.abstract: Antibiotic resistance genes (ARGs) have been widely investigated in temperate and subtropical reservoirs but remain poorly understood in tropical drinking-water reservoirs. We sampled four drinking-water reservoirs in Hainan during both winter and summer, integrating physicochemical, heavy-metal, and metagenomic data to investigate the diversity, spatiotemporal patterns, and assembly of ARGs, mobile genetic elements (MGEs), and microbial communities. ARG composition and community structure differed significantly by season and reservoir. Contig-based analysis identified ARG-MGE arrangements in diverse putative hosts; sul1 and qacEdelta1 co-occurred with integrases and transposases, demonstrating MGE co-localization. Null-model analysis indicated reservoir-specific ARG assembly in winter but predominantly stochastic assembly in summer, whereas microbial community assembly was deterministic in both seasons. Mantel and Spearman analyses showed seasonal variation in ARG relationships: stronger correlations with environmental factors in winter and more positive correlations with MGEs in summer. Summer co-occurrence networks were larger and more connected, with more positive ARG-MGE-microbial genus associations. Partial least squares path modeling (PLS-PM) showed positive MGE-ARG associations in both seasons, whereas microbial community composition was negatively associated with ARGs only in winter. These results characterize seasonal ARG variation and its associations with MGEs and microbial communities in tropical reservoirs, providing a baseline for monitoring regional drinking-water sources.

works.abstract: The increasing use of biomass for renewable energy generation has resulted in growing quantities of biomass bottom ash (BBA), most of which is still landfilled despite its potential as a secondary mineral resource. Quartz-rich BBA generated in fluidized-bed combustion is a unique waste stream due to the incorporation of silica bed material; however, its environmental safety and long-term durability constraints remain poorly understood. This study comprehensively evaluated BBAs from industrial-scale circulating and bubbling fluidized-bed biomass power plants to assess their suitability for resource recovery as secondary fine aggregates. Physicochemical characterization (XRF, XRD, SEM-EDS), environmental risk assessment (aqueous leaching, TCLP, BCR sequential extraction, Risk Assessment Code), aggregate performance testing, and accelerated alkali-silica reactivity (ASR) tests were conducted. Both BBAs contained high quartz contents (74.6-78.3 wt.%), low loss on ignition (≤0.32%), and strongly alkaline pH (11.4-11.9). Heavy metals and metalloids showed low leachability, while sequential extraction indicated that Pb and Cd were mainly associated with stable mineral fractions. Zn exhibited moderate mobility according to the Risk Assessment Code, but overall release remained low under aqueous and acidic conditions. Based on regulatory criteria, circulating fluidized-bed ash was classified as non-hazardous waste and bubbling fluidized-bed ash as inert waste. Despite meeting requirements for fine aggregates in road construction, microstructural defects and accelerated expansion tests demonstrated severe alkali-silica reactivity of thermally altered quartz, indicating a critical durability limitation for cementitious applications. Durability constraints associated with reactive silica must be considered alongside contaminant mobility in resource recovery strategies for biomass combustion residues.

Towards post-growth policymaking: Barriers and enablers for wellbeing economy and Doughnut economics initiatives
works.abstract: Providing wellbeing for all while safeguarding planetary boundaries may require governments to pursue post-growth policies. An important question is the extent to which government-led post-growth initiatives can be transformative within the existing institutional context. Initial empirical studies have highlighted some of the limitations these initiatives currently face, but a broader empirical assessment of the underlying barriers and enablers across institutional contexts is still lacking. To address this gap, we examine wellbeing economy and Doughnut economics government initiatives across governance scales in Europe, New Zealand, and Canada. To identify barriers and enablers as well as priorities for future action, we develop and apply a framework that captures systemic and political dimensions to analyze the data. Overall, our results suggest that the overarching economic growth paradigm severely limits the initiatives’ scope of action. Important enablers of existing initiatives in our study include crises, the political agency of key individuals, and high-level political support. Civil servants who promote growth-critical perspectives often face tensions: they need to appeal to broad stakeholder groups while avoiding co-optation. To create the political and organizational conditions for transformative policy change we suggest focusing on two areas: fostering a critical consciousness of growth hegemony in society, and institutionally embedding post-growth-aligned political priorities whenever there are political windows of opportunity. Strengthening government-led post-growth initiatives will also require stronger engagement with — and pressure from — civil society.

works.abstract: Mexico's rapid growth in battery electric vehicle (BEV) adoption has not been accompanied by a regulatory framework for the end-of-life management of lithium-ion batteries (LIBs), creating environmental risks and limiting the recovery of strategic materials. This study evaluates four end-of-life management strategies for BEV LIBs in Mexico (controlled disposal, hydrometallurgical recycling, pyrometallurgical recycling, and repurposing) using an integrated framework that combines Life Cycle Assessment (LCA), the Material Circularity Indicator (MCI), and a criticality-weighted extension (MCI-c). The proposed MCI-c incorporates material criticality into the circularity assessment, allowing resource recovery to be evaluated not only in terms of material recirculation but also considering the strategic importance of recovered materials. Repurposing achieved the best overall environmental and circularity performance, while hydrometallurgical recycling consistently outperformed pyrometallurgical recycling among recycling alternatives. Incorporating criticality into the assessment altered the prioritization of management strategies under increasing lithium criticality, demonstrating that criticality can influence end-of-life management priorities. These findings highlight the importance of integrating environmental performance, material circularity, and criticality into the evaluation of end-of-life LIBs management strategies. For Mexico, they support the development of a dedicated regulatory framework that prioritizes higher-value recovery strategies and incorporates criticality into end-of-life decision-making. More broadly, the proposed framework provides a practical approach for evaluating end-of-life LIBs management in countries facing similar challenges in battery circularity and critical material supply.

Between symbols and substance: Voluntary impact reporting of funds
works.abstract: Impact investing has emerged as a prominent investment approach to addressing social and environmental challenges while generating financial returns. Given its dual mandate to generate impact and financial returns, impact investing faces heightened pressures on its legitimacy, making transparent impact reporting essential to counter allegations of impact-washing and to safeguard the credibility of the approach. Despite the growing relevance of impact reporting, little is known about the underlying motivations and reporting strategies of fund managers who voluntarily publish impact reports. Drawing on legitimacy theory, the paper investigates the motivations and reporting strategies behind voluntary impact reporting by fund managers using a sequential exploratory design. First, 13 semi-structured interviews with impact-reporting professionals were analyzed following Grounded Theory principles. Second, a qualitative content analysis of 141 publicly available impact reports was conducted to analyze how reporting strategies are implemented in practice. The findings of the interviews reveal that fund managers’ motivations are driven by a need to show the alignment of profit with purpose, move beyond institutional compliance, and foster impact reflexivity. These motivations are operationalized through six reporting strategies: rationalization, contextualization, verification, institutionalization, participation, and transformation, which cluster around the dimensions of justification, integration, and adaptation. The content analysis assesses the potential for more substantive forms of legitimation in individual reporting elements. The paper contributes to legitimacy theory in the context of reporting by demonstrating that reporting strategies are interdependent and to practice by offering practitioners and standard setters a starting point for critically reflecting on the design of impact reporting.

works.title: Environmental and economic assessment of olefin synthesis from waste as an emerging alternative to conventional light olefin production routes
works.abstract: Light olefins such as ethylene and propylene are essential petrochemical intermediates but remain highly energy- and carbon-intensive to produce using conventional fossil-based technologies. We conduct the life-cycle environmental and economic assessment (LCA/LCC) of seven olefin production pathways, such as coal-based, natural gas-based, shale gas-based, crude oil-based, bio-based, waste-to-olefins and waste-to-olefins with sorption-enhanced olefin synthesis, to understand trade-offs and identify decarbonisation opportunities. A cradle-to-gate LCA employs nine EF 3.1 midpoint indicators, using foreground data from industrial sources, Aspen Plus V14 modelling, and ecoinvent v3.10 inventories. Results show that coal-based olefin production exhibits the highest environmental burdens, particularly for climate change, freshwater ecotoxicity, eutrophication, and water use. Natural gas-based and crude oil-based routes perform better across non-climate categories but remain carbon-intensive. Bio-based olefin production route provides partial climate benefits but is penalised by large land and water requirements. In contrast, waste-to-olefins and waste-to-olefins with sorption-enhanced olefin synthesis achieve net-negative greenhouse gas emissions due to biogenic carbon uptake and integrated CO 2 capture. Sorption-enhanced olefin synthesis further reduces energy demand via in-situ water removal and process intensification, yielding lower GHG emissions (47%), reduced water use by 64%, and improved selectivity compared with conventional waste-to-olefin routes. However, higher impacts persist in ozone depletion and ionising radiation categories, driven by upstream electricity supply chains. Economic analysis indicates that gasification and CO 2 management dominate overall costs, while the sorption-enhanced synthesis adds only a modest incremental cost to waste-to-olefin pathways. Total life cycle costing for waste-to-olefins with sorption-enhanced olefin synthesis falls within EUR 2130 to 3550 t −1 olefin, including environmental cost, competitive with emerging green olefin pathways. Overall, the findings demonstrate that combining waste feedstocks, CO 2 capture, and sorption-enhanced process intensification offers a promising pathway for low-carbon, resource-efficient olefin production, especially within future decarbonised energy systems.
