Valorization of Brassica juncea waste into iron oxide nanoparticles for efficient hexavalent chromium [Cr(VI)] remediation: characterization, experimental kinetics, isotherms, and machine learning optimization
Biodegradation of polyethylene and polyvinyl chloride by soil-screened Aspergillus versicolor and Aspergillus aflatoxiformans
RNA viruses as drivers of rapid diatom succession within a single bloom event
works.abstract: Diatoms frequently dominate seasonal phytoplankton blooms and contribute ~40% of marine primary production. Viruses drive phytoplankton mortality and bloom collapse, yet how viruses regulate diatom bloom dynamics is not well resolved. Here, using quantitative metatranscriptomics, we tracked temporal patterns of diatoms and associated viruses at near-daily resolution during the spring bloom in the Gulf of Aqaba, Red Sea. We captured distinct phases and rapid restructuring within both the diatom community and cell-associated virosphere. Diatom transcriptional profiling indicated activation of stress and death pathways prior to taxon-specific demise. RNA viruses emerged as dominant players within the bloom, with fluctuations of putative diatom-infecting RNA viruses across intracellular and extracellular fractions revealing sequential waves of active virus infection that were consistent with virus-mediated diatom mortality. Correlation and codon usage analyses further implicated specific diatom taxa as putative hosts for the identified RNA viruses. Rather than a uniform 'boom and bust', the spring diatom bloom comprised a mosaic of overlapping successional waves of diatom and viral taxa unfolding on daily timescales. These findings support RNA viruses as drivers of diatom turnover, advancing our understanding of how viruses temporally structure diverse diatom assemblages and the biogeochemical trajectory of diatom blooms in marine systems.

works.title: Bioprospecting perchlorate-reducing bacteria: report of the genera Psychrobacter, Planococcus, Carnobacterium, and Paeniglutamicibacter isolated in Cierva Point, Antarctica, and its contribution to SDG 3
works.abstract: Abstract Perchlorate (ClO 4 − ) is a global contaminant that has been detected in various environmental matrices. ClO 4 − is considered an emerging pollutant because of its potent endocrine-disrupting effects, which impairs iodine uptake in the thyroid gland, and its high toxicity and persistence. Therefore, the development of technologies for its reduction in ecosystems is imperative; bioremediation is a promising technology for ClO 4 − reduction. In this study, bacterial strains isolated from marine sediments at Cierva Point, an Antarctic Specially Protected Area (ASPA No. 134), were characterized. The methodology consisted of four stages: i) isolation of the bacterial strains; ii) characterization of isolated strains by morphological, biochemical, and molecular traits; iii) susceptibility tests against NaCl and ClO 4 − ; iv) ClO 4 − removal assays using a selective electrode. The strains grew at 10 °C for 7 days and tolerated NaCl concentrations up to 30% w/v. All isolates grew at ClO 4 − concentrations of 10,000 mg/L, and five isolates also grew at 15,000 mg/L. Phylogenetic analysis identified members of the genera Psychrobacter, Planococcus, Carnobacterium , and Paeniglutamicibacter , capable of removing the contaminant in percentages between 40% and 52%. In alignment with UN Sustainable Development Goal 3 on promoting health and well-being, this project supports both ecosystem conservation and public health protection. In conclusion, the bacterial strains isolated from Cierva Point marine sediments, Antarctica, represent valuable resources for the bioremediation of ClO 4 − contamination, demonstrating significant potential to reduce and mitigate the pollutant in affected ecosystems.

works.title: Development of biomaterials for bioremediation in agriculture: the importance of correct classification of the biocompatibility of immobilized microorganisms
authors: Nelson Luís Gonçalves Dias de Souza
works.abstract: The development of biomaterials for environmental bioremediation has emerged as a sustainable and promising strategy, becoming a consolidated research area within the field of contaminated soil treatment. In this context, advances in material science and biotechnology have enabled the development of innovative immobilization supports that improve microbial stability, protection, and biodegradation performance. Among these materials, polymeric matrices combined with natural biodegradable components have demonstrated significant potential for enhancing pesticide degradation efficiency while reducing environmental impacts. However, the accurate, standardized, and robust characterization of biocompatibility remains a critical challenge, which limits the large-scale application and commercialization of these biomaterials. To address this knowledge gap, this review discusses the importance of biocompatibility classification, microbial immobilization strategies, and viability assessment methods for microorganisms entrapped in different matrices. Additionally, it underscores the imperative for the development of more dependable quality control methodologies to guarantee the efficacy, safety, and scalability of biomaterial-based bioremediation technologies.

works.title: Lineage II Escherichia coli O157:H7: genomes, prophages, colicins, and the absence of detectable Stx2
works.abstract: ABSTRACT The genomes of three lineage II strains of E. coli O157:H7 (FRIK2069, FRIK2455, and FRIK2533) with different pulsed-field gel electrophoresis patterns were sequenced, assembled, and compared. The genomes were closely related, with overall synteny, with the exception of a 302 kbp inversion in FRIK2069. FRIK2533 lacked pO157, which may account for its limited isolation. FRIK2455 was the dominant strain isolated over several years and was selected for comparison with lineage I (Sakai) and lineage I/II (EC4115) strains. Distinct polymorphisms were identified in prophages and MGEs among the three lineages. All lineages contained stx1 prophages and the locus of enterocyte effacement. The stx2a prophage was present in Sakai and EC4115, while the stx2c prophage was found in EC4115 and FRIK2455. Eleven geographically disparate LII strains from the United States were tested for functional phage and Stx2. Three of the 11 LII strains underwent delayed lysis after 24 h post-mitomycin C treatment. stx2 transcription was observed in two of the three lytic strains, but Stx2 was not detected in the lytic or non-lytic LII strains by Western blot. The supernatant of lysates from eight lineage II strains inhibited growth of the phage host ( E. coli strain MG1655) due to the production of a colicin (D, B, or M). These findings add to the body of evidence that LII EHEC do not produce functional phage or a detectable level of Stx2. Additionally, colicin production and pO157 may be key characteristics to the persistence of EHEC strains in the bovine host and farm environment. IMPORTANCE Escherichia coli O157:H7 is a human pathogen that is phylogenetically separated into three lineages. Strains belonging to lineages I and I/II are isolated from both clinical and bovine samples, whereas lineage II strains are only isolated from bovine and environments they occupy. This study sequenced, assembled, and compared the genomes of three lineage II strains. The genomes were closely related and syntenic, with differences in plasmid content and a chromosomal inversion. Comparison of the genome from FRIK2455 (lineage II strain) with the genomes of lineage I and I/II strains found distinct polymorphisms in prophages and mobile genetic elements. None of the lineage II strains examined produced functional phage or Stx2, but eight strains produced a colicin. Results from this study support previous reports that lineage II strains do not produce a detectable level of Stx2. Additionally, colicin production and pO157 may contribute to the persistence of EHEC in bovine.

works.title: Plasmid-mediated copper resistance in Xanthomonas euvesicatoria pv. perforans : determination of plasmid copy number and stability
works.abstract: ABSTRACT The management of bacterial spot of tomato is challenged by the widespread occurrence of copper resistance among its causal pathogens. In Xanthomonas euvesicatoria pv. perforans , a major causal agent, copper resistance is conferred by cop genes organized in an operon located on either the chromosome or plasmid. In the United States, copper resistance is predominantly chromosomally encoded. Plasmid-borne resistance is limited to a few phylogenetic groups but is prevalent in other bacterial spot pathogens. We hypothesized that plasmid-encoded copper resistance genes exhibit higher expression than chromosomally encoded genes but may be unstable in the absence of selective pressure for resistance. To test this hypothesis, we examined how the chromosomal versus plasmid-borne cop operon influences gene copy number and expression, as well as plasmid stability. Relative to strains with only chromosomal resistance, strains carrying plasmid-encoded resistance exhibited an increased copy number of copB , a key gene in the operon, while strains carrying both chromosomal and plasmid-encoded resistance showed an even greater increase in gene copy number. Correspondingly, copB expression was elevated in both groups. During in vitro growth without copper, partial or complete plasmid loss occurred in a subset of strains, and genome sequencing of colonies with reduced plasmid size revealed transposase-mediated plasmid rearrangements. These findings demonstrate that plasmid-borne copper resistance increases gene copy number and expression of copper resistance genes but can be unstable without copper selection in some strain backgrounds, highlighting the role of mobile genetic elements in shaping Xanthomonas euvesicatoria pv. perforans adaptation to changing copper environments. IMPORTANCE Plasmids are key players in the dissemination of antimicrobial resistance. Although copper resistance is widespread among Xanthomonas euvesicatoria pv. perforans strains, copper-based bactericides remain at the forefront of disease management. We previously demonstrated that distinct genetic elements, including plasmid- and chromosomally encoded genomic islands, contribute to the acquisition of copper resistance and the occurrence of multicopy resistance in X. euvesicatoria pv. perforans . Here, we show that the localization of copper resistance genes on a plasmid, chromosome, or both influences gene copy number and expression of copper resistance genes. Furthermore, rearrangements between co-resident plasmids affect plasmid stability, leading to the loss of copper resistance in X. euvesicatoria pv. perforans . These findings highlight how plasmid dynamics can shape bacterial evolvability and adaptation to selective environments.

works.title: A thin carbon membrane to capture carbon
A circular oligo(disulfide) anolyte enables practical aqueous redox flow batteries
Recyclable flow battery chemistry
Efficient carbon dioxide separation with molecularly thin bilayer carbon membranes
Integration of In Vitro Exposure Data into the ECOTOXicology Knowledgebase and Application to Adverse Outcome Pathway Development
works.abstract: Abstract Chemical safety evaluations are shifting to incorporate alternative methods (e.g., in vitro and in silico approaches) to meet demand for rapid, efficient chemical hazard assessments for human health and ecological impacts. Historically, toxicity results from in vitro exposures were not candidates for inclusion in the U.S. EPA’s ECOTOXicology Knowledgebase (ECOTOX). ECOTOX is the world’s largest compilation of curated ecotoxicity data for aquatic and terrestrial organisms, providing support for ecological chemical assessments through identification and curation of toxicity results. Presented here is ECOTOX’s recent expansion to incorporate in vitro studies of chemical ecotoxicity using well-established ECOTOX systematic literature review procedures. Since 2017, in vitro ecotoxicity data from over 575 publications were added to the public website (www.epa.gov/ecotox), with cell, tissue, and/or enzyme exposures from 310 species, including fish, amphibians, reptiles, birds, mammals, plants, algae, and invertebrates. Here we summarize in vitro ecotoxicological data available, identify where in vitro data are currently lacking for research and risk assessment, and demonstrate application of ECOTOX in vitro data in adverse outcome pathway development. This in vitro expansion continues and will evolve to support study quality evaluations and validation of new approach methodologies, necessary components for strengthening evidence certainty and furthering application of alternative approaches in regulatory frameworks.

works.title: Rice husk biochar-immobilized bacterial consortium enhances reduction of parent-herbicide residues in wheat-vegetated soil contaminated with a ternary herbicide mixture
Electron transfer to nitrogenase in Paenibacillus polymyxa
works.abstract: ABSTRACT Nitrogenase requires low-potential electrons to reduce N 2 to produce ammonia. The direct electron donors to nitrogenase are reduced ferredoxin (Fd) and flavodoxin (Fld). The enzymes that reduce Fd or Fld for N 2 fixation mainly include pyruvate-flavodoxin (ferredoxin) oxidoreductase (PFOR), ferredoxin-NADP + reductase (FNR), R hodobacter n itrogen f ixation protein complex (Rnf), and bifurcating electron transfer flavoprotein complex (Fix). Paenibacillus polymyxa is a model for studies of nitrogen fixation, but the pathways of electron transport to nitrogenase are unknown. In this study, we characterized the electron transport pathway to nitrogenase in P. polymyxa . Deletion analysis showed that among 15 genes encoding Fds, Fld, and Fd-/Fld-reducing enzymes, only cbiW gene and pfoAB operon decreased nitrogenase activity (31% and 37% relative to wild type, respectively). Triple deletion of cbiW and pfoAB led to a reduction of nitrogenase activity by 61%. Elemental analysis and ultraviolet-visible absorption spectroscopy revealed that the purified Fd protein encoded by cbiW is a [2Fe-2S] Fd. The purified Fd protein was able to substitute for Klebsiella NifF (Fld) to transfer electrons from pyruvate to Klebsiella nitrogenase in vitro. The pfoAB operon encodes PFOR, which is composed of two subunits. Klebsiella oxytoca NifJ (PFOR) was able to support nitrogen fixation in the Δ pfoAB mutant. These findings suggest that [2Fe-2S] Fd encoded by cbiW and PFOR encoded by the pfoAB operon constitute an electron transport pathway to Paenibacillus nitrogenase. IMPORTANCE Gram-positive and facultatively anaerobic Paenibacillus polymyxa is a model diazotroph whose nif (nitrogen fixation) genes encoding nitrogenase have been used for engineering yeast and plants. However, the pathway of electron transfer to Paenibacillus nitrogenase is unknown. In this study, we demonstrate that Fd encoded by cbiW and PFOR encoded by the pfoAB operon constitute an electron transport pathway to Paenibacillus nitrogenase. Fd encoded by cbiW is a [2Fe-2S] Fd, and PFOR encoded by the pfoAB operon is a heterodimer. In contrast, in many gram-negative diazotrophs, [4Fe-4S] Fds are widely used as electron donors to nitrogenase, and PFORs (NifJs) are homodimers. These results suggest that there may be some differences in the mechanisms of electron transfer to nitrogenase between gram-negative and gram-positive bacteria. The identified electron transport components in P. polymyxa will have great potential for use in engineering eukaryotes.

works.title: Chemical diversity analysis identifies inhibitory compounds in the secretomes of citrus-associated Bacillus spp. to the Huanglongbing pathogen, “ Candidatus Liberibacter asiaticus,” and citrus root pathogens
works.abstract: ABSTRACT Huanglongbing (HLB) is a devastating and incurable citrus disease associated with the gram-negative, phloem-limited, and unculturable bacterium “ Candidatus Liberibacter asiaticus” ( C Las), transmitted by the psyllid Diaphorina citri . Our goal was to identify high-performing microbial candidates from a previously established citrus-associated microbial collection for the management of HLB and associated root pathogens. Candidate selection was based on bioactivity, genomic, and metabolomic profiles. Eighteen Bacillus isolates were screened for antagonistic activity against Liberibacter crescens , C Las, and citrus-associated Phytophthora and Fusarium spp. Phylogenetic analysis grouped the isolates into four species groups: Bacillus velezensis , B. subtilis , B. pumilus , and B. cereus . Among these, B. velezensis exhibited the strongest and broadest inhibitory activity, followed by B. subtilis . This enhanced antagonistic potential is likely associated with the greater number and diversity of biosynthetic gene clusters (BGCs) identified. Notably, C Las-inhibitory isolates included B. velezensis (CB0021 and CB0909) and B. altitudinis (CB0086). Bacilysin and surfactin BGCs were conserved across all C Las-inhibitory isolates, suggesting a potential role in C Las suppression. Accordingly, surfactins were detected in bioactive fractions of B. velezensis (CB0027 and CB0909) and B. subtilis (CB0893), supporting their likely contribution to bioactivity and inhibiting L. crescens growth in vitro , highlighting their potential as candidate compounds for C Las management. Overall, this study underscores the importance of microbial discovery, screening, and characterization as an effective strategy for identifying sustainable solutions to manage HLB. IMPORTANCE Huanglongbing (HLB) is a severe disease of citrus that has altered the citrus landscape worldwide and currently has no cure. It is caused by the bacterium “ Candidatus Liberibacter asiaticus” ( C Las) and transmitted by the psyllid Diaphorina citri . Currently, the most effective control strategy for this disease relies on trunk injection of antibiotics oxytetracycline and streptomycin, and there is a need to find alternative solutions to complement or replace chemical control. Here, we aimed to select high-performing candidates from our previously established citrus-associated microbial collection to manage HLB and root-associated pathogens. We screened 18 Bacillus isolates for antagonistic activity against Liberibacter crescens , C Las, and citrus-associated Phytophthora and Fusarium spp., and we generated their genomic and metabolomic profiles. Our research centers on selecting microbial candidates for their bioactivity and antimicrobial metabolite production, aiming to develop effective plant-protective bioinoculants for mitigation of HLB.

works.title: Beyond the Tip of the Iceberg: The Vast Unexplained Fraction of Extractable Organofluorine in Water
works.abstract: Recommendations P er-and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFASs) are a class of chemicals characterized by the presence of at least one -CF 2or -CF 3 group in their molecular structure.1 Due to their extreme environmental persistence, toxicity, and ubiquity, several PFASs, such as perfluorooctanesulfonate (PFOS) and perfluorooctanoic acid (PFOA), have been subjected to regulations in many countries.While the total number of PFASs has exceeded 10,000, 2 only a few dozen are routinely monitored.Consequently, more than 98% of PFASs in river water and wastewater remain unidentified.3,4 To capture the total PFAS burden in aquatic environments and drinking water, various analytical approaches have been developed, among which extractable (organic)fluorine (EF/EOF) analysis has emerged as a highly promising method.

works.title: River Geomorphology Shapes the Pollution Intensity and Chemical Fingerprints of Inland Shipping VOC Emissions
works.abstract: Abstract Inland shipping is a critical source of volatile organic compounds (VOCs), but emission inventories rely on spatially averaged load factors that fail to capture localized transient events. We addressed this gap through an 800-km high-frequency mobile measurement campaign along the Yangtze River. The observations revealed a striking spatial anomaly: the most intense pollution hotspots (>50 ppbV) were spatially decoupled from the high-traffic Wuhan megacity, clustering instead within the remote, sinuous Jingjiang channel. Chemical forensics explicitly ruled out topographical trapping. Unlike steady cruising plumes, these hotspots exhibited exceptionally high toluene-to-benzene ratios (∼13.0) and enriched unburned fuel tracers. High-frequency GPS tracking confirmed that this distinct fingerprint is driven by a 4.2-fold increase in vessel speed fluctuation variance, proving that hydrodynamic resistance in tortuous channels compels vessels into inefficient transient combustion regimes. We conclude that navigational complexity acts as an invisible stressor creating localized pollution risks evaded by regional traffic-based models.

works.title: Poly(3-hydroxybutyrate) production from thermally pretreated cheese whey by Stutzerimonas stutzeri BPSNITW100893: optimization, validation and characterization
Multilayered network analysis reveals the centrality of newly discovered Nucleocytoviricota in wastewater treatment plant communities
works.abstract: Viruses of the phylum Nucleocytoviricota are remarkable entities due to their exceptionally large genomes and complex gene repertoires, which blur the lines between viral and cellular life. Previous research has leveraged computational approaches to map their extensive diversity. Experimental work has, in parallel, begun to elucidate their intricate interactions with hosts, bacterial symbionts, co-infecting virophages, and other mobile genetic elements.Although unlikely to replicate all simultaneously within the same host cell, the convergence of these entities within a single environment creates a dense hub of potential interactions that calls for a holistic, topology-based analysis. Here, we recovered high-quality genomes of 61 Nucleocytoviruses, 15 virophages and 14 polinton-like viruses from deeply sequenced metagenomes of 23 Danish wastewater treatment plants, and integrated them into a multilayered interaction network together with microbial contigs. This network recovered putative interactions across multiple levels, including Nucleocytoviruses co-occurring with hyperparasitic elements, associations with abundant activated sludge bacteria, and read-level signals of integration events. We show that the giants among viruses act as centrality-inducing entities, elevating others into highly central positions within the community and therefore are key players shaping the microbial community structure, ecology and evolution in wastewater treatment plants.

works.title: Wildlife-associated ecosystems in Algeria harbor internationally distributed ESBL-producing clones and plasmids, including a CTX-M-15 Klebsiella pneumoniae ST17 lineage associated with a conserved IncFIB(K) resistance plasmid
works.abstract: ABSTRACT Expanded-spectrum cephalosporin-resistant Enterobacterales (ESC-R-E) have disseminated beyond clinical settings, but their occurrence and genomic epidemiology in wildlife remain poorly characterized, particularly in low- and middle-income countries. ESC-R may result from the production of extended-spectrum β-lactamases (ESBLs) or AmpC-type cephalosporinases. We investigated the prevalence, resistance mechanisms, and population structure of ESC-R-E in free-ranging wildlife, captive wild animals, and zoo workers in Algeria. Between October 2021 and June 2023, 1,899 fecal samples were collected across six Algerian provinces. ESC-R-E isolates were recovered by selective culture and characterized by antimicrobial susceptibility testing, and whole-genome sequencing. Overall, 73 ESC-R-E isolates (3.9%) were identified, including seven OXA-48-like carbapenemase co-producers (0.4%). Carriage was significantly higher in captive animals (13.5%) than in free-ranging wildlife (1.6%) or zoo workers (7.7%). Among the 66 ESBL-producing isolates analyzed, CTX-M enzymes predominated ( n = 61), particularly CTX-M-15 ( n = 53). Klebsiella pneumoniae was the predominant species ( n = 33), with ST17 accounting for 27/33 isolates. Closely related CTX-M-15-producing ST17 isolates were recovered from captive animals, free-ranging wildlife, and a zoo worker and carried an IncFIB(K) plasmid harboring bla CTX-M-15 within a multidrug resistance region closely related to globally disseminated plasmids. Globally disseminated high-risk Escherichia coli clones were also detected, namely ST167, ST361, ST410, and a persistent ST38 lineage in Algerian wildlife since 2016. These findings demonstrate the circulation of high-risk Enterobacterales lineages and mobile resistance plasmids in Algerian wildlife-associated ecosystems and highlight the need for integrated One Health surveillance of antimicrobial resistance at the human-animal-environment interface. IMPORTANCE Wildlife is increasingly recognized as a potential reservoir and sentinel for antimicrobial resistance, yet genomic data from low- and middle-income countries remain scarce. This study provides one of the largest genomic investigations of expanded-spectrum cephalosporin-resistant Enterobacterales in wildlife from North Africa. We demonstrate that internationally disseminated high-risk Klebsiella pneumoniae and Escherichia coli lineages, together with globally distributed CTX-M-15-carrying plasmids, are circulating among captive animals, free-ranging wildlife, and humans in zoological environments. The recovery of closely related K. pneumoniae ST17 isolates from different host species highlights the potential for antimicrobial resistance dissemination across the human-animal-environment interface. These findings extend the known ecological range of clinically important resistant Enterobacterales beyond healthcare settings and identify wildlife-associated ecosystems as part of the broader antimicrobial resistance network. Our study underscores the value of integrating wildlife into One Health surveillance programs to better understand and mitigate the environmental spread of antimicrobial resistance.

works.title: Antidepressant desvenlafaxine identified in wastewater promotes transformation and antibiotic resistance risk in Acinetobacter baylyi ADP1 via metabolic adaptations
works.abstract: ABSTRACT Wastewater treatment plants (WWTPs) are known reservoirs of antibiotic resistance genes (ARGs). Non-antibiotic compounds, such as antidepressants, may further promote ARG acquisition through horizontal gene transfer (HGT). Desvenlafaxine, a serotonin-norepinephrine reuptake inhibitor (SNRI) listed on the EU Surface Water Watch List, is among the most frequently detected antidepressants in WWTP effluents, yet its role in HGT has not been examined. Here, we detected desvenlafaxine at the highest concentrations among four antidepressants monitored across three municipal WWTPs in western New York. Using Acinetobacter baylyi ADP1 as a model recipient in natural transformation assays ( n = 6), we found that desvenlafaxine significantly increased transformation frequency at 10 mg/L (1.74 ± 0.33-fold) and 50 mg/L (1.49 ± 0.19-fold; P adj < 0.05). Effects occurred without induction of reactive oxygen species or loss of membrane integrity, consistent with its very low toxicity (IC 20 ~1,300 mg/L). Instead, desvenlafaxine induced dose-dependent increases in membrane fluidity and shifts to less negative zeta potentials, suggesting that electrostatic interactions between its cationic amine group and the negatively charged membrane reduce surface repulsion and facilitate plasmid proximity during uptake. Non-targeted proteomics revealed a biphasic response: at 10 mg/L, competence-associated proteins (PilB, ComM) were upregulated, and STRING analysis identified networks linked to membrane transport, transcriptional regulation, and envelope remodeling, while no connected network was recovered at 50 mg/L. Electron microscopy confirmed higher pilus frequency at both doses. Together, these findings reveal a non-oxidative, envelope-mediated route by which a widely detected antidepressant increases bacterial competence. IMPORTANCE The spread of antibiotic resistance poses a serious and escalating threat to human health worldwide. While antibiotic use is widely recognized as a key driver, non-antibiotic pharmaceuticals released into the environment through wastewater have received far less attention. Antidepressants are among the most frequently detected drugs in treated wastewater effluents, yet their potential to promote antibiotic resistance transfer in bacteria remains poorly understood. This study demonstrates that desvenlafaxine, one of the most abundant antidepressants found in municipal wastewater, can increase the uptake of antibiotic resistance genes in an environmental bacterium at concentrations above those currently measured in effluent, and identifies the bacterial cell-surface changes that enable this without cytotoxicity.

works.title: How to Accurately Predict the Fate and Effects of Engineered Nanomaterials
works.abstract: RecommendationsE ngineered nanomaterials (ENMs) challenge risk assess- ment because their environmental fate and toxicity cannot be predicted from manufactured properties alone.After release, ENMs transform under pH, ionic strength, redox conditions, dissolved organic matter, and surrounding phases.Dissolution, aggregation, sulfidation, corona formation, and mineral interactions alter particle size, surface chemistry, speciation, and bioavailability, changing the magnitude and mechanisms of impact. 1 Consequently, organisms may encounter forms substantially different from the original material.For example, in a pilot wastewater treatment plant, silver nanoparticles (AgNPs) rapidly associated with biosolids, transforming into Ag 2 S. 2 Sulfidation reduced AgNP-mediated inhibition of Escherichia coli in vitro.3 Similarly, Huo et al. showed that AgNPs participate in a dynamic transformation network involving AgNPs, Ag + and secondary Ag 0 nanoparticles.The relative contributions of these species to toxicity changed over time, with Ag + contributing strongly to early effects and particulates increasingly contributing during prolonged exposure.4 A toxicity value for pristine AgNPs may therefore not represent the evolving species generated after release.Copper oxide (CuO) and zinc oxide (ZnO) engineered nanoparticles (ENPs) provide complementary examples.Sulfidation and protein-corona formation altered the composition, morphology, surface chemistry, aggregation, dissolution and toxicity of CuO ENPs, with effects depending on transformation pathway and biological end point.5 In plants, transformed CuO nanoparticles produced different patterns of Cu uptake, translocation, ionomic disruption and stress responses from pristine particles.Similarly, transformation and protein-corona formation altered ZnO morphology, Zn 2+ release, aggregation and toxicity, with transformed particles exhibiting lower toxicity than pristine ENPs.These findings demonstrate that ENM transformations alter toxicity, highlighting the need to identify the resulting forms, their persistence, abundance, and associated risks.Natural organic matter (NOM) can form eco-coronas that alter ENM fate and biological interactions, reducing the aquatic ecotoxicity of metal-based ENMs but increasing the toxicity of nanoscale plastics in gastrointestinal models.ENMs can also carry cocontaminants; TiO 2 ENMs increased heavymetal accumulation in organisms, creating exposure scenarios not captured by assessing pristine substances individually.

works.title: Linking Millimeter-Scale Heterogeneity to Rapid CO2 Migration in the Otway International Test Centre for Geological Carbon Storage
works.abstract: Abstract Field observations at geological CO2 storage sites, including the Otway International Test Centre (OITC), report rapid plume migration, potentially driven by highly channelized flow pathways caused by small-scale heterogeneities. However, how small-scale heterogeneities govern upscaled flow behavior, particularly the role of fluid connectivity, remains unclear due to imaging resolution limitations. To address this, we combined steady-state core-flooding experiments with micro-CT imaging (10 μm resolution) to directly visualize CO2 distribution for a heterogeneous core from OITC. Strong flow channelization was observed, leading to low core-average CO2 saturations. CO2 connectivity increased at the expense of brine connectivity over a narrow saturation interval, leading to steep brine relative permeability curves. A simple reservoir model was used to demonstrate that our derived relative permeability functions produce faster lateral CO2 plume migration and improved pore-space utilization. This work provides a foundation for improving relative permeability parametrization in reservoir simulations, aiding safe and efficient CO2 storage design.

works.title: Sustainable bilge water treatment and bioelectricity generation in microbial fuel cells: impact of substrate complexity on microbial adaptation
Nanoscale pesticide delivery suppresses pathogens and enriches beneficial microbiomes for safer crop protection
works.abstract: Nanocarrier-based pesticide delivery platforms substantially boost agrochemical utilization efficiency, yet their cascading ecological repercussions for rhizosphere and soil microbial ecology remain insufficiently understood. Here, a star polycation (SPc) nanocarrier was employed to construct a matrine nano-formulation (MT@SPc) with typical nano-pesticide characteristics. MT@SPc and commercial matrine formulation (MT SL) were employed as representative systems to further evaluate their impacts on rhizosphere and soil microbial ecosystems. Compared with MT SL, MT@SPc reshaped rhizosphere microbial communities by suppressing phytopathogens and promoting the enrichment of beneficial bacteria. Further validation using four representative bacterial isolates obtained from soil demonstrated that MT@SPc significantly inhibited the growth of the phytopathogen Pectobacterium carotovorum, whereas enriched beneficial bacteria exhibited lower susceptibility to MT@SPc. Multi-scale mechanistic analyses revealed that MT@SPc could interact with bacterial cell surfaces through physicochemical interactions, resulting in pronounced surface deformation and structural damage in P. carotovorum. Multi-omics analyses associated with physiological and biochemical assays further demonstrated that MT@SPc disrupted cell wall and membrane integrity, leading to ionic imbalance, metabolite leakage and oxidative stress. However, beneficial bacteria maintained higher stability, and their enrichment was associated with microbial community shifts following pathogen suppression. Overall, this study reveals that nano-pesticides drive rhizosphere community restructuring through differential microbial responses, providing mechanistic insights into nano-pesticide-microbiome interactions in complex ecological systems.

works.title: Contrasting edaphic and land-use signatures of microbial phosphorus mobilisation and accumulation genes
works.abstract: Phosphorus (P) is an essential nutrient that constrains productivity across many terrestrial ecosystems. Soil microorganisms regulate P transformation through distinct functional strategies, yet how these strategies vary with land use and environmental conditions across chronically P-impoverished landscapes remains poorly understood. Here, we combined 268 soil metagenomes from natural, pasture, and cropland systems across Australia with genome-resolved analyses of 1,077 metagenome-assembled genomes (MAGs). Results revealed contrasting genomic distributions among P-cycling strategies. P accumulation genes were widely distributed across bacterial phylogeny, whereas mineralization gene and solubilisation gene were concentrated within specific lineages. Land-use-associated differences were most evident in the relative abundances of mineralisation and solubilisation genes, whereas accumulation genes showed comparatively little variation. Soil properties were stronger predictors of relative P-cycling gene abundance than climatic variables. Among these variables, soil pH was the strongest predictor of both the combined relative abundance of P-cycling genes and mineralisation genes, whereas accumulation genes were negatively associated with the mineral-associated organic carbon fraction. Continental predictions further suggested higher combined relative P-cycling gene abundance in wetter south-western and coastal eastern regions. These analyses reveal contrasting microbial P-cycling gene strategies across Australian soils and provide a genome-resolved framework for understanding their phylogenetic distributions and environmental associations at the continental scale.

works.title: Whole-genome analysis uncovers four novel Streptomyces species linked to sweet potato soil rot in China
works.abstract: ABSTRACT Sweet potato soil rot, caused by pathogenic Streptomyces , is an emerging threat to sweet potato production in China. However, the diversity and pathogenic mechanisms of the associated species remain poorly understood. In this study, symptomatic storage roots exhibiting typical pox-like lesions were collected from major production regions in Henan and Guangdong provinces. A total of 225 actinomycete strains were isolated using optimized methods, and six highly pathogenic strains were identified through tuber slice, hydroponic, and pot inoculation assays. Morphological, physiological, whole-genome sequencing, and phylogenetic analyses revealed considerable diversity among these pathogenic isolates. Average nucleotide identity (ANI) analysis showed that strain (ST10) was closely related to Streptomyces albogriseolus , whereas the remaining strains displayed substantial genomic divergence, indicating diverse taxonomic affiliations. Comparative genomic analysis identified a conserved core genome together with extensive strain-specific gene content, reflecting both functional conservation and adaptive evolution. Phylogenomic analysis placed several isolates close to S. ipomoeae , and others within distinct pathogenic lineages. Notably, none of the six strains possessed the canonical thaxtomin biosynthetic gene cluster, suggesting that pathogenicity is mediated by alternative virulence mechanisms. Instead, conserved gene clusters associated with siderophores and stress-related metabolites were identified, indicating potential roles in host colonization and ecological adaptation. These findings expand our understanding of the genomic diversity and potential pathogenic mechanisms of sweet potato-associated Streptomyces and provide a valuable foundation for disease management and resistance breeding. IMPORTANCE Herein, we established an optimized isolation method yielding 225 actinomycete strains and a rapid pipeline for pathogenic identification of sweet potato-associated Streptomyces . Six isolates were confirmed as causal agents of sweet potato soil rot, including four novel species. Complete genome sequences of five strains provide a fundamental resource for elucidating pathogenesis mechanisms and advancing taxonomic and evolutionary studies of the genus. The absence of canonical thaxtomin biosynthetic genes across all pathogenic strains, combined with the presence of conserved siderophore and stress-related metabolite clusters, demonstrates that these pathogens utilize alternative virulence mechanisms distinct from well-characterized Streptomyces plant pathogens. Comparative genomics reveals a conserved core genome alongside strain-specific gene content, reflecting functional conservation and adaptive evolution. These genomic resources and experimental validations establish a foundational framework for understanding pathogen diversity, enabling accurate diagnosis of emerging strains and directly informing resistance breeding programs by identifying genetic targets for screening sweet potato germplasm.

works.title: Local temperature and humidity are associated with proportion of antimicrobial-resistant Escherichia coli isolates in farm environments: considerations for on-farm surveillance
works.abstract: ABSTRACT Evidence suggests that increased local temperatures are associated with higher prevalence of antimicrobial resistance (AMR) in environmental bacteria. This observational cohort study investigates associations between local climate and the proportion of antimicrobial-resistant Escherichia coli isolated from 2,766 farm environment samples from 53 English dairy farms. A non-linear Bayesian model that accounts for decreased test sensitivity at low E. coli abundance was used to estimate the proportion of antimicrobial-resistant E. coli from colony count data. A 20°C increase in local temperature was associated with a 5.0-fold increase in the proportion of streptomycin-resistant E. coli (95% credible interval [CI]: 1.03–33.0; absolute increase: 0.2%, 95% CI: 2.3 × 10 −3 %–1.2%). Weaker evidence suggested that increased temperatures were associated with increased proportions of tetracycline-resistant E. coli . Increasing relative humidity was associated with an increase in the proportion of amoxicillin-, streptomycin-, and tetracycline-resistant E. coli . A 32% increase in relative humidity (from 60% to 92%) was associated with a 4.7-fold increase in the proportion of amoxicillin-resistant E. coli (median; 95% CI: 1.4–15.7; absolute increase: 1.3%, 95% CI: 0.2%–3.5%). For amoxicillin and streptomycin, a synergistic effect where increasing both temperature and humidity was associated with increased proportions of antimicrobial-resistant E. coli was observed, with weak evidence of this effect observed for tetracycline. These findings highlight the importance of considering weather conditions, sample characteristics, and seasonality in livestock AMR surveillance. Associations between local weather conditions and the proportion of livestock E. coli exhibiting AMR suggest that climate change may influence the burden of One Health AMR. IMPORTANCE Understanding how environmental conditions are associated with variability in antimicrobial resistance (AMR) prevalence is critical for developing robust livestock AMR surveillance and anticipating the potential effects of climate change. The non-linear Bayesian modeling approach developed here adjusts for Escherichia coli abundance-associated variability in test sensitivity, enabling the influence of risk factors associated with the proportion of antimicrobial-resistant E. coli within samples to be more accurately estimated. Applying this approach to 2,766 fecal samples from 53 dairy farms in Southwest England indicated that the proportion of antimicrobial-resistant E. coli generally increased under warmer and wetter conditions. These findings suggest that environmental conditions can influence the prevalence of antimicrobial-resistant E. coli in dairy farm environments and demonstrate the importance of accounting for weather-related variability in livestock AMR surveillance. Adjusting for these associations in livestock AMR surveillance could improve the accuracy of modeling AMR trends and strengthen the assessment of climate-associated AMR risks.

Observation-Based Quantification of Pollution-Dependent Activation and Empirical Activation Boundaries of Black-Carbon-Containing Particles
works.abstract: Abstract The activation of black-carbon-containing particles (BCc) as cloud condensation nuclei influences their incorporation into clouds, wet removal, and atmospheric lifetime, yet remains challenging to quantify under ambient conditions. Using a coupled size-resolved CCNc–SP2 measurement system, the critical activation diameter and activation fraction of BCc (D50,BCc and AFBCc, respectively) were quantified at supersaturations (SS) of 0.1–0.3% under different pollution conditions during wintertime in urban Beijing. At SS = 0.1%, D50,BCc remained nearly constant at ∼ 222 nm as pollution increased, whereas AFBCc rose from 32% to 44%, consistent with an increased abundance of larger BCc. At SS = 0.3%, D50,BCc increased from 128 to 146 nm with increasing pollution, accompanied by a greater contribution of small, relatively less-coated BCc (<150 nm), while AFBCc remained consistently around 77%. Logistic regression was used to derive empirical activation boundaries relating D50,BCc to BC core size (Dc). At a given SS and D50,BCc within the overlapping observed range, the corresponding Dc generally increased from light to heavy pollution. Boundary slopes decreased with increasing SS, indicating a smaller change in D50,BCc per unit change in Dc along the fitted boundaries. These observations reveal contrasting pollution-dependent activation characteristics and empirical BC core-size relationships across supersaturations.

works.title: Contrasting Impacts on Plant Endogenous Metabolic Pathways from Trace Organic Contaminants Relevant to Recycled Water
works.abstract: Abstract Plant uptake and metabolism of contaminants from recycled water raise concerns regarding exposure through crops but may also cause plant endogenous metabolic network perturbation. In this work, we investigated impacts on endogenous metabolic pathways of Brassicaceae model plant Arabidopsis thaliana following hydroponic exposure for 48 h to anticorrosive benzotriazole (BT) or antimicrobial benzoisothiazolinone (BIT) at 200 μg/L and 2 mg/L, trace organic contaminants relevant to recycled water. We observed ∼99.9% uptake of both compounds and 13–25% lower plant biomass in exposed plants compared to no-exposure control plants. Despite the similar uptake and effect on biomass, plant metabolomics revealed that BT exposure significantly impacted the tryptophan metabolism through downregulation of indole metabolites and upregulation of kynurenic acid, indicating altered tryptophan utilization. Conversely, BIT exposure impacted antioxidant defense and oxidative stress signaling pathways through downregulation of flavonoids and upregulation of jasmonic acid. Even within shared impacted pathways such as phenylpropanoid biosynthesis, BT exposure shifted the main pathway toward benzoic acid derivatives, whereas BIT exposure shifted the pathway toward antioxidant defense-related compounds (e.g., flavonoids, sinapic acid). These findings demonstrate that structurally similar contaminants can cause distinct pathway-level metabolic shifts, highlighting the importance of evaluating biological impacts of specific trace organic contaminant uptake in crops relevant to recycled water irrigation.

works.title: Electrochemical Biofilms Enable Bioeffect-Informed Biofunctional Response Classification
works.abstract: Abstract Conventional concentration-based environmental assessment does not directly capture pollutant-induced biological responses, whereas existing bioassays often lack rapid, continuous, and biologically interpretable readouts. Here, we developed a bioeffect-informed response classification framework based on electrochemical biofilms (ECBs), which translates electrochemical signals into biofunctionally anchored classifications of biofilm impairment within approximately 7 min. ECB responses quantitatively tracked independently measured biofunctional perturbations and exhibited a strong dose–response relationship (R2 = 0.9987). A three-level classification was established using IC20 (0.830 μg L–1) and IC50 (3.939 μg L–1) response landmarks, whose biological significance was validated through structural, functional, and molecular analyses. Although the assays reflect different end points, ECB detected U(VI)-induced perturbations at concentrations over 3 orders of magnitude lower than the conventional Vibrio fischeri assay. Natural seawater validation demonstrated agreement with ICP–MS and enabled biofunctionally anchored classification, providing a rapid and interpretable strategy for effect-based water-quality screening.

works.title: Ecophysiology of the cosmopolitan nitrite-oxidising genus Candidatus Nitromaricola
works.abstract: The majority of marine nitrite-oxidising bacteria (NOB) belong to three uncultured genera within the Nitrospinaceae family and thus the ecophysiology of these main nitrate producing microorganisms in the ocean remains poorly resolved. Here, we report on the environmental characterization of one of these genera, which we name Candidatus Nitromaricola. A single species within this genus, Candidatus Nitromaricola pontica, comprises >95% of the nitrite-oxidising community in the permanently stratified Black Sea. This provided a unique opportunity to study this globally abundant genus in situ, across pronounced environmental gradients of oxygen and inorganic nitrogen concentrations. We show that Ca. Nitromaricola pontica is capable of oxidising nitrite at similar rates in both oxic and apparently anoxic waters, although it had a higher abundance in the more oxygenated waters of the Black Sea. The genome of Ca. Nitromaricola pontica indicates that like other NOB, it is a chemolithoautotroph, oxidising nitrite, and fixing inorganic carbon. However, Ca. Nitromaricola pontica and other members of the Ca. Nitromaricola genus lack canonical high affinity terminal oxidases found in some other NOB genera. Single-cell analyses confirmed active autotrophic growth and showed that ammonium and urea, rather than nitrite, were the main nitrogen sources for biomass production. Our findings identify Ca. Nitromaricola as a globally abundant marine NOB and highlight its cosmopolitan lifestyle.

Sustainable valorization of traditional Chinese medicine residues via semi-permeable membrane composting: the impacts of nitrogen sources
works.abstract: Abstract Driven by global disease challenges, the traditional Chinese medicine (TCM) industry has flourished, however, the massive surge in TCM residues has emerged as a major bottleneck to its sustainable development. Semi-permeable membrane aerobic composting provides a key technology for TCM residue valorization, which typically relies on exogenous nitrogen supplementation to optimize the carbon-to-nitrogen (C/N) balance. Nevertheless, a systematic understanding of how differentiated nitrogen sources impact this composting process remains lacking. To address this, this study introduced distinct nitrogen sources as co-substrates for semi-permeable membrane aerobic composting to elucidate their modulation of key physicochemical parameters and microecological succession. The results demonstrated that peanut meal exhibited the optimal composting performance compared to alfalfa meal, soybean meal, and urea. Specifically, its thermophilic phase (> 55°C) persisted for over 7 days, and total organic carbon (TOC) degraded most rapidly and stably, achieving a reduction rate of 49.82%. At maturity, the ammonium nitrogen (NH 4 + -N) content and electrical conductivity (EC) dropped to as low as 81 mg/kg and 2606µS/cm, respectively, while the peak total nutrient content reached 5.79%. Meanwhile, the dynamic trend of the E4/E6 ratio aligned with typical aerobic composting patterns, indicating a high degree of humification. Community analysis revealed that Bacillus , Bifidobacterium , and Cupriavidus were key bacterial taxa driving composting efficiency, whereas fungi dominated by Thermomyces , Mycobacterium , and Aspergillus played pivotal roles in NH 4 + -N and lignocellulose degradation, significantly accelerating compost maturation. Overall, this study provides critical microecological insights and a practical nitrogen optimization strategy for efficient and sustainable TCM residue composting.

works.title: Quantifying assets for the geopolitics of climate change mitigation
works.abstract: Abstract Climate change mitigation reshapes the distribution of economic assets in the low-carbon transition. Here we quantify climate-related assets for 169 countries across four dimensions: fossil fuel production, climate change damages, renewable energy potential and land carbon sequestration capacity. We combine integrated assessment models, climate projections, economic damage functions and biosphere datasets to assess asset changes under multiple mitigation scenarios. Geopolitical challenges and opportunities arise from climate change mitigation because losses and gains across energy and environmental assets are country-specific, which we further characterize through a broad clustering and a detailed pairwise similarity analysis. Our analysis suggests comparatively moderate impacts for the USA, the European Union and China, highlighting the challenge that the largest economic powers may not be those with the strongest asset-based interest for climate action. While our framework remains limited, our data provide input for integrating other ethical, governance and socioeconomic factors in future analyses of opportunities and challenges for ambitious climate change mitigation.

Trace Amines Scavenge Terpenoid-Derived Criegee Intermediates at Air–Liquid Interfaces to Form Atmospheric Organic Nitrogen
works.abstract: Abstract Organic nitrogen (ON) represents a chemically diverse fraction of atmospheric aerosols that profoundly modulates particle aging, toxicity, and light absorption. However, the exact kinetic pathways and timing of interfacial ON formation remain poorly constrained. Utilizing surface-sensitive mass spectrometry, we experimentally demonstrate that ambient, trace-level amines (5–40 ppt) can efficiently scavenge terpenoid-derived stabilized Criegee intermediates (SCIs) at the air–liquid boundary, successfully outcompeting interfacial hydration. Crucially, we elucidate a complete kinetic hierarchy for ON evolution across three sequential generations: SCIs, α-hydroxyalkyl-hydroperoxides (α-HH), and functionalized aldehydes all react with amines to converge on identical ON products. The reaction rates follow the strict order of SCI > α-HH > functionalized aldehyde, bypassing conventional bulk-phase carbonyl condensation via rapid nucleophilic attack and spontaneous H2O2 elimination. Rather than predicting global yields, our data explicitly identify a rapid, nonphotolytic entry point for ON formation that current condensed-phase schemes miss. Incorporating this bounded SCI–amine pathway into future multiphase mechanisms will significantly improve parametrizations of aerosol nitrogen chemical aging and ON-linked light absorption.
